🔑

Big idea

  • Quadratic equation a x2 + b x + c = 0 has roots x = (-b +/- sqrt(D)) / 2a with discriminant D = b2 - 4ac
  • D > 0 two distinct real roots
  • D = 0 equal roots
  • D < 0 no real roots
Read the full explanation

Quadratic equation a x^2 + b x + c = 0 has roots x = (-b +/- sqrt(D)) / 2a with discriminant D = b^2 - 4ac. D > 0 two distinct real roots; D = 0 equal roots; D < 0 no real roots. Example: 2x^2 - 7x + 3 = 0: D = 49 - 24 = 25, roots 3 and 0.5. Sum of roots = -b/a; product = c/a. AP: a_n = a + (n - 1) d; S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d]. For 2, 5, 8, ...: S_20 = 10 (4 + 57) = 610.

🧮

Quadratic equations

  • An equation that can be written as a x2 + b x + c = 0 with a not equal to 0
  • The highest power of x is 2, so there are at most two roots
  • If a = 0 the x2 term vanishes and it is only linear
  • Method 1: factorisation (splitting the middle term)
Read the full explanation

What it is. An equation that can be written as a x^2 + b x + c = 0 with a not equal to 0. The highest power of x is 2, so there are at most two roots. If a = 0 the x^2 term vanishes and it is only linear. Method 1: factorisation (splitting the middle term). To solve a x^2 + b x + c = 0, find two numbers whose product is a x c and whose sum is b. Split b x into those two terms, group, and use the zero product rule: if P x Q = 0 then P = 0 or Q = 0. Example: 6x^2 - x - 2 = 0. a x c = -12; the numbers 3 and -4 give sum -1. So 6x^2 + 3x - 4x - 2 = 3x(2x + 1) - 2(2x + 1) = (3x - 2)(2x + 1) = 0, so x = 2/3 or x = -1/2. Method 2: completing the square. Divide by a, move the constant, add (b/2a)^2 to both sides: (x + b/2a)^2 = (b^2 - 4ac)/4a^2. Taking the square root gives the quadratic formula, so the formula is simply this method done once for all equations. Method 3: the quadratic formula. x = (-b +/- sqrt(b^2 - 4ac)) / 2a. It always works, even when factorising is hard. Put brackets round negative values of b when substituting. Discriminant D = b^2 - 4ac tells the nature of the roots before you solve: D > 0 two distinct real roots; D = 0 two equal real roots x = -b/2a; D < 0 no real roots (the parabola does not touch the x-axis). If a, b, c are integers and D is a perfect square the roots are rational. Sum and product of roots. If the roots are p and q then p + q = -b/a and p q = c/a. A quadratic with given roots is x^2 - (p + q) x + p q = 0. Useful identities: p^2 + q^2 = (p + q)^2 - 2 p q and |p - q| = sqrt(D)/|a|. Word problems. Define the unknown, write one equation, reduce it to standard form, solve, and reject answers that cannot be real quantities (a negative length, age or number of people). Typical types: two numbers with a given sum of squares; a rectangle with given area and perimeter relation; speed, distance and time (time = distance / speed); two taps filling a tank; consecutive integers. Common mistakes. Forgetting that a x^2 + b x + c must equal 0 before factorising; dividing both sides by x and losing the root x = 0; dropping the minus sign of b; reading D = b^2 - 4ac as b^2 - 4 a c with the wrong sign when c is negative (then D is a sum: b^2 + 4|a c|).

🧠

Arithmetic progressions

  • A list in which every term after the first is got by adding the same number d (the common difference)
  • D can be positive, negative or zero
  • Check with d = a_(k+1) - a_k for any two neighbouring terms
  • A_n = a + (n - 1) d
Read the full explanation

Definition. A list in which every term after the first is got by adding the same number d (the common difference). d can be positive, negative or zero. Check with d = a_(k+1) - a_k for any two neighbouring terms. nth term. a_n = a + (n - 1) d. The 10th term of 7, 11, 15, ... is 7 + 9 x 4 = 43. To check whether a number belongs to the AP solve a + (n - 1) d = that number: n must be a positive whole number. Sum of n terms. S_n = n/2 [2a + (n - 1) d] = n/2 (a + l) where l is the last term. Also a_n = S_n - S_(n-1). The sum of the first n natural numbers is n(n + 1)/2, of the first n odd numbers is n^2, of the first n even numbers is n(n + 1). Useful facts. Three numbers a - d, a, a + d are in AP; four numbers a - 3d, a - d, a + d, a + 3d are in AP. If a, b, c are in AP then 2b = a + c (b is the arithmetic mean). The kth term from the end of an AP with last term l is l - (k - 1) d. Equal gaps mean the sum of terms equidistant from the ends is constant. Word problems. Savings that grow by a fixed amount, seats in rows of a hall, instalments of a loan, and the number of logs in a stack are all APs. Write a, d and what is asked (a_n or S_n or n), then substitute. If the equation for n has two solutions, check which are whole and positive.

lessons.title: Pair of linear equations in two variables
yt: class 10 pair of linear equations

blocks.x: A pair of linear equations a1 x + b1 y + c1 = 0 and a2 x + b2 y + c2 = 0 is solved graphically (two lines) or algebraically by substitution, elimination, or cross-multiplication. The nature of the solution depends on a1/a2, b1/b2 and c1/c2.
Deep dive: nature of solutions

For a1 x + b1 y + c1 = 0 and a2 x + b2 y + c2 = 0: if a1/a2 != b1/b2 the lines intersect at one point, so the pair is consistent with a unique solution. If a1/a2 = b1/b2 != c1/c2 the lines are parallel: no solution (inconsistent). If a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2 the lines coincide: infinitely many solutions (dependent, consistent).
Deep dive: methods

**Substitution:** express one variable from one equation and substitute into the other. **Elimination:** multiply to make the coefficients of one variable equal in size, then add or subtract. **Cross-multiplication:** x/(b1 c2 - b2 c1) = y/(c1 a2 - c2 a1) = 1/(a1 b2 - a2 b1). **Graphical:** plot both lines; the intersection is the solution. Each method must give the same answer, so always verify by substituting back into both equations.
Deep dive: word problems

Choose two unknowns, form two equations from the two conditions, solve, and state the answer with units. Typical types: ages (now, years ago, years later), numbers (two-digit number and reversed digits), fractions (add to numerator and denominator), speed (upstream and downstream, with and against wind), geometry (angles of cyclic quadrilateral), money (cost of items), and area/perimeter of rectangles. **Common mistakes:** sign errors while multiplying through, forgetting that the speed downstream is u + v and upstream u - v, not checking both equations.

Visual lesson

Pair of linear equations in two variables

A pair of linear equations a1 x + b1 y + c1 = 0 and a2 x + b2 y + c2 = 0 is solved graphically (two lines) or algebraically by substitution, elimination, or…

minutes
formulas
Q&A
quiz
Flat concept map (2D)
1Big idea›2Nature of solutions›3Methods›4Word problems
Two-digit number10x + y
Reversed number10y + x
🔑

Big idea

  • A pair of linear equations a1 x + b1 y + c1 = 0 and a2 x + b2 y + c2 = 0 is solved graphically (two lines) or algebraically by substitution…
  • The nature of the solution depends on a1/a2, b1/b2 and c1/c2
🧪

Nature of solutions

  • For a1 x + b1 y + c1 = 0 and a2 x + b2 y + c2 = 0: if a1/a2 != b1/b2 the lines intersect at one point, so the pair is consistent with a unique…
  • If a1/a2 = b1/b2 != c1/c2 the lines are parallel: no solution (inconsistent)
  • If a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2 the lines coincide: infinitely many solutions (dependent, consistent)
🔄

Methods

  • Substitution: express one variable from one equation and substitute into the other
  • Elimination: multiply to make the coefficients of one variable equal in size, then add or subtract
  • Cross-multiplication: x/(b1 c2 - b2 c1) = y/(c1 a2 - c2 a1) = 1/(a1 b2 - a2 b1)
  • Graphical: plot both lines
Read the full explanation

Substitution: express one variable from one equation and substitute into the other. Elimination: multiply to make the coefficients of one variable equal in size, then add or subtract. Cross-multiplication: x/(b1 c2 - b2 c1) = y/(c1 a2 - c2 a1) = 1/(a1 b2 - a2 b1). Graphical: plot both lines; the intersection is the solution. Each method must give the same answer, so always verify by substituting back into both equations.

✍️

Word problems

  • Choose two unknowns, form two equations from the two conditions, solve, and state the answer with units
  • Typical types: ages (now, years ago, years later), numbers (two-digit number and reversed digits), fractions (add to numerator and denominator)…
  • Common mistakes: sign errors while multiplying through, forgetting that the speed downstream is u + v and upstream u - v, not checking both equations
Read the full explanation

Choose two unknowns, form two equations from the two conditions, solve, and state the answer with units. Typical types: ages (now, years ago, years later), numbers (two-digit number and reversed digits), fractions (add to numerator and denominator), speed (upstream and downstream, with and against wind), geometry (angles of cyclic quadrilateral), money (cost of items), and area/perimeter of rectangles. Common mistakes: sign errors while multiplying through, forgetting that the speed downstream is u + v and upstream u - v, not checking both equations.

lessons.title: Polynomials
yt: class 10 polynomials

blocks.x: Zeroes of a polynomial p(x) are the values of x for which p(x) = 0; they are the x-coordinates where its graph cuts the x-axis. A quadratic ax^2 + bx + c with zeroes alpha and beta has alpha + beta = -b/a and alpha beta = c/a.
Deep dive: zeroes and graphs

A linear polynomial ax + b has one zero, -b/a, and its graph is a straight line cutting the x-axis once. A quadratic polynomial has a parabola as its graph: opening upward if a > 0 and downward if a < 0. It has two, one (touching) or no real zeroes according as the parabola cuts, touches or misses the x-axis. A cubic polynomial has at most three zeroes; its graph cuts the x-axis at most three times. In general a polynomial of degree n has at most n zeroes.
Deep dive: relation between zeroes and coefficients

Quadratic ax^2 + bx + c: sum of zeroes = -b/a, product = c/a. Cubic ax^3 + bx^2 + cx + d: alpha + beta + gamma = -b/a, alpha beta + beta gamma + gamma alpha = c/a, alpha beta gamma = -d/a. Given the sum S and product P, the quadratic is k [x^2 - S x + P] for any non-zero k.
Deep dive: division algorithm

For polynomials p(x) and g(x) with g(x) != 0 there exist q(x) and r(x) with p(x) = g(x) q(x) + r(x), where r(x) = 0 or deg r < deg g. If r(x) = 0, g(x) is a factor of p(x). Use this to find the other zeroes of a polynomial when one or two zeroes are known. **Common mistakes:** forgetting the minus sign in -b/a, writing the quadratic as x^2 + Sx + P, and dividing without arranging terms in descending powers.
Hindi saransh
Zero = jahan graph x-axis ko kaatta hai. Sum = -b/a, product = c/a.
Quadratic from zeroes: x^2 - (sum)x + (product).

Visual lesson

Polynomials

Zeroes of a polynomial p(x) are the values of x for which p(x) = 0

minutes
formulas

Flat concept map (2D)
1Big idea›2Zeroes and graphs›3Relation between zeroes and…›4Division algorithm
🔑

Big idea

  • Zeroes of a polynomial p(x) are the values of x for which p(x) = 0
  • They are the x-coordinates where its graph cuts the x-axis
  • A quadratic ax2 + bx + c with zeroes alpha and beta has alpha + beta = -b/a and alpha beta = c/a
📌

Zeroes and graphs

  • A linear polynomial ax + b has one zero, -b/a, and its graph is a straight line cutting the x-axis once
  • A quadratic polynomial has a parabola as its graph: opening upward if a > 0 and downward if a < 0
  • It has two, one (touching) or no real zeroes according as the parabola cuts, touches or misses the x-axis
  • A cubic polynomial has at most three zeroes
Read the full explanation

A linear polynomial ax + b has one zero, -b/a, and its graph is a straight line cutting the x-axis once. A quadratic polynomial has a parabola as its graph: opening upward if a > 0 and downward if a < 0. It has two, one (touching) or no real zeroes according as the parabola cuts, touches or misses the x-axis. A cubic polynomial has at most three zeroes; its graph cuts the x-axis at most three times. In general a polynomial of degree n has at most n zeroes.

🧠

Relation between zeroes and coefficients

  • Quadratic ax2 + bx + c: sum of zeroes = -b/a, product = c/a
  • Cubic ax3 + bx2 + cx + d: alpha + beta + gamma = -b/a, alpha beta + beta gamma + gamma alpha = c/a, alpha beta gamma = -d/a
  • Given the sum S and product P, the quadratic is k [x2 - S x + P] for any non-zero k
🌟

Division algorithm

  • For polynomials p(x) and g(x) with g(x) != 0 there exist q(x) and r(x) with p(x) = g(x) q(x) + r(x), where r(x) = 0 or deg r < deg g
  • If r(x) = 0, g(x) is a factor of p(x)
  • Use this to find the other zeroes of a polynomial when one or two zeroes are known
  • Common mistakes: forgetting the minus sign in -b/a, writing the quadratic as x2 + Sx + P, and dividing without arranging terms in descending powers
Read the full explanation

For polynomials p(x) and g(x) with g(x) != 0 there exist q(x) and r(x) with p(x) = g(x) q(x) + r(x), where r(x) = 0 or deg r < deg g. If r(x) = 0, g(x) is a factor of p(x). Use this to find the other zeroes of a polynomial when one or two zeroes are known. Common mistakes: forgetting the minus sign in -b/a, writing the quadratic as x^2 + Sx + P, and dividing without arranging terms in descending powers.

lessons.title: Trigonometry and heights and distances
yt: class 10 trigonometry heights and distances

blocks.x: In a right triangle: sin = opposite/hypotenuse, cos = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan = opposite/adjacent. Standard values: sin 30 = 1/2, sin 45 = 1/sqrt 2, sin 60 = sqrt 3/2; cos 60 = 1/2; tan 45 = 1; tan 30 = 1/sqrt 3. Identity sin^2 + cos^2 = 1. **Heights and distances:** angle of elevation is measured upward from the horizontal. Example: standing 20 m from a tower with an angle of elevation 30 degrees: height = 20 tan 30 = 20/sqrt 3 = **11.55 m**. **Probability:** P(E) = favourable / total. A card from 52: P(heart) = 13/52 = **1/4**.
Deep dive: trigonometric ratios

**Definitions.** In a right triangle, for an acute angle A: sin A = opposite / hypotenuse, cos A = adjacent / hypotenuse, tan A = opposite / adjacent. Reciprocals: cosec A = 1/sin A, sec A = 1/cos A, cot A = 1/tan A. Also tan A = sin A / cos A and cot A = cos A / sin A. **Standard angles.** sin: 0, 1/2, 1/sqrt 2, sqrt 3/2, 1 for 0, 30, 45, 60, 90 degrees. cos is the same list reversed. tan: 0, 1/sqrt 3, 1, sqrt 3, not defined. A memory trick: sin = sqrt(0/4), sqrt(1/4), sqrt(2/4), sqrt(3/4), sqrt(4/4). **Complementary angles.** sin (90 - A) = cos A; cos (90 - A) = sin A; tan (90 - A) = cot A; cot (90 - A) = tan A; sec (90 - A) = cosec A; cosec (90 - A) = sec A. So sin 35 = cos 55 and tan 20 x tan 70 = 1. **Identities.** sin^2 A + cos^2 A = 1; 1 + tan^2 A = sec^2 A; 1 + cot^2 A = cosec^2 A. To prove an identity, work on the more complicated side, write everything in sin and cos, and simplify. **Behaviour.** As A rises from 0 to 90 degrees sin A rises from 0 to 1, cos A falls from 1 to 0, tan A rises from 0 without limit. The value of sin A and cos A never exceeds 1; sec A and cosec A are never below 1.
Deep dive: heights and distances

**Angles.** The angle of elevation is the angle between the horizontal and the line of sight upward to an object. The angle of depression is measured downward from the horizontal to an object below. The angle of depression from the top equals the angle of elevation from the bottom (alternate angles). **Method.** Draw a clear figure; mark the right angle, the known side and the angle; choose the ratio that links the known and unknown sides: height and distance use tan, height and line of sight use sin, distance and line of sight use cos. Typical forms: height = distance x tan (angle); two observation points give two equations that share the height. **Common values.** At 45 degrees height equals distance. At 30 degrees height = distance / sqrt 3. At 60 degrees height = distance x sqrt 3. Take sqrt 3 = 1.732 and sqrt 2 = 1.414 for numerical answers.
Deep dive: probability

**Definition.** P(E) = number of favourable outcomes / total number of equally likely outcomes. 0 <= P(E) <= 1; P(sure event) = 1; P(impossible event) = 0; P(E) + P(not E) = 1. **Standard sample spaces.** A coin: 2 outcomes. A die: 6. Two coins: 4. Two dice: 36. A pack of cards: 52 cards, 4 suits of 13, 12 face cards, 26 red, 26 black, 4 aces, 4 kings.

Visual lesson

Trigonometry and heights and distances

In a right triangle: sin = opposite/hypotenuse, cos = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan = opposite/adjacent

minutes

Flat concept map (2D)
1Big idea›2Trigonometric ratios›3Heights and distances›4Probability
cosec A1 / sin A
sec A1 / cos A
🔑

Big idea

  • In a right triangle: sin = opposite/hypotenuse, cos = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan = opposite/adjacent
  • Standard values: sin 30 = 1/2, sin 45 = 1/sqrt 2, sin 60 = sqrt 3/2
  • Tan 30 = 1/sqrt 3
  • Identity sin2 + cos2 = 1
Read the full explanation

In a right triangle: sin = opposite/hypotenuse, cos = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan = opposite/adjacent. Standard values: sin 30 = 1/2, sin 45 = 1/sqrt 2, sin 60 = sqrt 3/2; cos 60 = 1/2; tan 45 = 1; tan 30 = 1/sqrt 3. Identity sin^2 + cos^2 = 1. Heights and distances: angle of elevation is measured upward from the horizontal. Example: standing 20 m from a tower with an angle of elevation 30 degrees: height = 20 tan 30 = 20/sqrt 3 = 11.55 m. Probability: P(E) = favourable / total. A card from 52: P(heart) = 13/52 = 1/4.

📌

Trigonometric ratios

  • In a right triangle, for an acute angle A: sin A = opposite / hypotenuse, cos A = adjacent / hypotenuse, tan A = opposite / adjacent
  • Reciprocals: cosec A = 1/sin A, sec A = 1/cos A, cot A = 1/tan A
  • Also tan A = sin A / cos A and cot A = cos A / sin A
  • Standard angles
Read the full explanation

Definitions. In a right triangle, for an acute angle A: sin A = opposite / hypotenuse, cos A = adjacent / hypotenuse, tan A = opposite / adjacent. Reciprocals: cosec A = 1/sin A, sec A = 1/cos A, cot A = 1/tan A. Also tan A = sin A / cos A and cot A = cos A / sin A. Standard angles. sin: 0, 1/2, 1/sqrt 2, sqrt 3/2, 1 for 0, 30, 45, 60, 90 degrees. cos is the same list reversed. tan: 0, 1/sqrt 3, 1, sqrt 3, not defined. A memory trick: sin = sqrt(0/4), sqrt(1/4), sqrt(2/4), sqrt(3/4), sqrt(4/4). Complementary angles. sin (90 - A) = cos A; cos (90 - A) = sin A; tan (90 - A) = cot A; cot (90 - A) = tan A; sec (90 - A) = cosec A; cosec (90 - A) = sec A. So sin 35 = cos 55 and tan 20 x tan 70 = 1. Identities. sin^2 A + cos^2 A = 1; 1 + tan^2 A = sec^2 A; 1 + cot^2 A = cosec^2 A. To prove an identity, work on the more complicated side, write everything in sin and cos, and simplify. Behaviour. As A rises from 0 to 90 degrees sin A rises from 0 to 1, cos A falls from 1 to 0, tan A rises from 0 without limit. The value of sin A and cos A never exceeds 1; sec A and cosec A are never below 1.

🧠

Heights and distances

  • The angle of elevation is the angle between the horizontal and the line of sight upward to an object
  • The angle of depression is measured downward from the horizontal to an object below
  • The angle of depression from the top equals the angle of elevation from the bottom (alternate angles)
  • Draw a clear figure
Read the full explanation

Angles. The angle of elevation is the angle between the horizontal and the line of sight upward to an object. The angle of depression is measured downward from the horizontal to an object below. The angle of depression from the top equals the angle of elevation from the bottom (alternate angles). Method. Draw a clear figure; mark the right angle, the known side and the angle; choose the ratio that links the known and unknown sides: height and distance use tan, height and line of sight use sin, distance and line of sight use cos. Typical forms: height = distance x tan (angle); two observation points give two equations that share the height. Common values. At 45 degrees height equals distance. At 30 degrees height = distance / sqrt 3. At 60 degrees height = distance x sqrt 3. Take sqrt 3 = 1.732 and sqrt 2 = 1.414 for numerical answers.

🌟

Probability

  • P(E) = number of favourable outcomes / total number of equally likely outcomes
  • 0 <= P(E) <= 1
  • P(sure event) = 1
  • P(impossible event) = 0
Read the full explanation

Definition. P(E) = number of favourable outcomes / total number of equally likely outcomes. 0 <= P(E) <= 1; P(sure event) = 1; P(impossible event) = 0; P(E) + P(not E) = 1. Standard sample spaces. A coin: 2 outcomes. A die: 6. Two coins: 4. Two dice: 36. A pack of cards: 52 cards, 4 suits of 13, 12 face cards, 26 red, 26 black, 4 aces, 4 kings.

lessons.title: Coordinate geometry, circles and similar triangles
yt: class 10 coordinate geometry

blocks.x: **Distance formula:** d = sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2); e.g. (0, 0) to (3, 4) is **5**. **Section formula:** point dividing (x1, y1), (x2, y2) in ratio m:n = ((m x2 + n x1)/(m + n), (m y2 + n y1)/(m + n)); midpoint is the case m = n. Area of triangle = (1/2)|x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2)|. **Similar triangles:** corresponding sides in the same ratio; areas in the ratio of the squares of sides. **Circle:** tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact; tangents from an external point are equal. If tangent length is 12 and radius 5, the distance from the centre is sqrt(144 + 25) = **13**.
Deep dive: coordinate geometry

**Cartesian plane.** Two perpendicular axes meet at the origin O (0, 0). A point is (x, y): x is the abscissa and y the ordinate. The quadrants are I (+,+), II (-,+), III (-,-), IV (+,-). Points on the x-axis have y = 0; points on the y-axis have x = 0. **Distance formula.** PQ = sqrt ((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2). Distance from the origin to (x, y) is sqrt (x^2 + y^2). Use it to test shapes: an isosceles triangle has two equal sides; a right triangle satisfies Pythagoras; a parallelogram has equal opposite sides and bisecting diagonals; a rhombus has four equal sides; a rectangle has equal diagonals; three points are collinear when the sum of two distances equals the third. **Section formula.** The point dividing A (x1, y1) and B (x2, y2) internally in the ratio m : n is ((m x2 + n x1)/(m + n), (m y2 + n y1)/(m + n)). The midpoint is ((x1 + x2)/2, (y1 + y2)/2). The centroid of a triangle is ((x1 + x2 + x3)/3, (y1 + y2 + y3)/3). To find the ratio in which a line divides a segment, let the ratio be k : 1 and solve. **Area of a triangle.** Area = (1/2) |x1 (y2 - y3) + x2 (y3 - y1) + x3 (y1 - y2)|. Three points are collinear when this area is 0. The area of a quadrilateral is found by splitting it into two triangles.
Deep dive: similar triangles and circles

**Similar triangles.** Two triangles are similar if their angles are equal; then corresponding sides are proportional. Criteria: AAA (or AA), SSS (sides in the same ratio) and SAS (two sides in the same ratio and the included angle equal). The ratio of areas is the square of the ratio of corresponding sides. The basic proportionality (Thales) theorem: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio. **Tangents.** A tangent touches a circle at exactly one point, the point of contact. The tangent is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact. From an external point exactly two tangents can be drawn and they are equal in length. If the distance from the centre to the external point is d and the radius r then the tangent length is sqrt (d^2 - r^2). A circle has infinitely many tangents; from a point inside it none.

Visual lesson

Coordinate geometry, circles and similar triangles

Distance formula: d = sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2)

minutes
formulas
Q&A
quiz
Flat concept map (2D)
1Big idea›2Coordinate geometry›3Similar triangles and…
Distance from the originsqrt (x^2 + y^2)
Midpoint((x1 + x2)/2, (y1 + y2)/2)
Area of a triangle(1/2)
Tangent lengthsqrt (d^2 - r^2)
🔑

Big idea

  • Distance formula: d = sqrt((x2 - x1)2 + (y2 - y1)2)
  • E.g. (0, 0) to (3, 4) is 5
  • Section formula: point dividing (x1, y1), (x2, y2) in ratio m:n = ((m x2 + n x1)/(m + n), (m y2 + n y1)/(m + n))
  • Midpoint is the case m = n
Read the full explanation

Distance formula: d = sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2); e.g. (0, 0) to (3, 4) is 5. Section formula: point dividing (x1, y1), (x2, y2) in ratio m:n = ((m x2 + n x1)/(m + n), (m y2 + n y1)/(m + n)); midpoint is the case m = n. Area of triangle = (1/2)|x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2)|. Similar triangles: corresponding sides in the same ratio; areas in the ratio of the squares of sides. Circle: tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact; tangents from an external point are equal. If tangent length is 12 and radius 5, the distance from the centre is sqrt(144 + 25) = 13.

📐

Coordinate geometry

  • Cartesian plane
  • Two perpendicular axes meet at the origin O (0, 0)
  • A point is (x, y): x is the abscissa and y the ordinate
  • The quadrants are I (+,+), II (-,+), III (-,-), IV (+,-)
Read the full explanation

Cartesian plane. Two perpendicular axes meet at the origin O (0, 0). A point is (x, y): x is the abscissa and y the ordinate. The quadrants are I (+,+), II (-,+), III (-,-), IV (+,-). Points on the x-axis have y = 0; points on the y-axis have x = 0. Distance formula. PQ = sqrt ((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2). Distance from the origin to (x, y) is sqrt (x^2 + y^2). Use it to test shapes: an isosceles triangle has two equal sides; a right triangle satisfies Pythagoras; a parallelogram has equal opposite sides and bisecting diagonals; a rhombus has four equal sides; a rectangle has equal diagonals; three points are collinear when the sum of two distances equals the third. Section formula. The point dividing A (x1, y1) and B (x2, y2) internally in the ratio m : n is ((m x2 + n x1)/(m + n), (m y2 + n y1)/(m + n)). The midpoint is ((x1 + x2)/2, (y1 + y2)/2). The centroid of a triangle is ((x1 + x2 + x3)/3, (y1 + y2 + y3)/3). To find the ratio in which a line divides a segment, let the ratio be k : 1 and solve. Area of a triangle. Area = (1/2) |x1 (y2 - y3) + x2 (y3 - y1) + x3 (y1 - y2)|. Three points are collinear when this area is 0. The area of a quadrilateral is found by splitting it into two triangles.

📐

Similar triangles and circles

  • Similar triangles
  • Two triangles are similar if their angles are equal
  • Then corresponding sides are proportional
  • Criteria: AAA (or AA), SSS (sides in the same ratio) and SAS (two sides in the same ratio and the included angle equal)
Read the full explanation

Similar triangles. Two triangles are similar if their angles are equal; then corresponding sides are proportional. Criteria: AAA (or AA), SSS (sides in the same ratio) and SAS (two sides in the same ratio and the included angle equal). The ratio of areas is the square of the ratio of corresponding sides. The basic proportionality (Thales) theorem: a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio. Tangents. A tangent touches a circle at exactly one point, the point of contact. The tangent is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact. From an external point exactly two tangents can be drawn and they are equal in length. If the distance from the centre to the external point is d and the radius r then the tangent length is sqrt (d^2 - r^2). A circle has infinitely many tangents; from a point inside it none.

blocks.x: **দূরত্ব সূত্র:** d = √((x2 - x1)² + (y2 - y1)²); যেমন (0, 0) থেকে (3, 4) পর্যন্ত দূরত্ব **5**। **বিভাজন সূত্র:** (x1, y1) ও (x2, y2) বিন্দুকে m:n অনুপাতে বিভক্তকারী বিন্দু = ((m x2 + n x1)/(m + n), (m y2 + n y1)/(m + n)); মধ্যবিন্দু হলো m = n হলে। ত্রিভুজের ক্ষেত্রফল = (1/2)|x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2)|। **সদৃশ ত্রিভুজ:** অনুরূপ বাহুগুলি সমানুপাতিক; ক্ষেত্রফলের অনুপাত বাহুর বর্গের অনুপাতের সমান। **বৃত্ত:** স্পর্শক স্পর্শবিন্দুতে ব্যাসার্ধের উপর লম্ব; বাইরের বিন্দু থেকে অঙ্কিত দুটি স্পর্শক সমান। স্পর্শকের দৈর্ঘ্য 12 ও ব্যাসার্ধ 5 হলে কেন্দ্র থেকে দূরত্ব √(144 + 25) = **13**।
বাইরের বিন্দু থেকে অঙ্কিত স্পর্শকগুলির দৈর্ঘ্য সমান।

de.title: Analytische Geometrie, Kreise und ähnliche Dreiecke

blocks.x: **Abstandsformel:** d = √((x2 - x1)² + (y2 - y1)²); zum Beispiel ist der Abstand von (0, 0) nach (3, 4) gleich **5**. **Teilungsformel:** Der Punkt, der die Strecke (x1, y1) bis (x2, y2) im Verhältnis m:n teilt = ((m x2 + n x1)/(m + n), (m y2 + n y1)/(m + n)); der Mittelpunkt ist der Fall m = n. Flächeninhalt eines Dreiecks = (1/2)|x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2)|. **Ähnliche Dreiecke:** Entsprechende Seiten stehen im gleichen Verhältnis; die Flächen stehen im Verhältnis der Quadrate der Seiten. **Kreis:** Die Tangente steht im Berührpunkt senkrecht auf dem Radius; Tangenten von einem äußeren Punkt aus sind gleich lang. Ist die Tangentenlänge 12 und der Radius 5, beträgt der Abstand zum Mittelpunkt √(144 + 25) = **13**.
Tangenten von einem äußeren Punkt an einen Kreis sind gleich lang.

es.title: Geometría analítica, circunferencias y triángulos semejantes

blocks.x: **Fórmula de la distancia:** d = √((x2 - x1)² + (y2 - y1)²); por ejemplo, de (0, 0) a (3, 4) la distancia es **5**. **Fórmula de la sección:** el punto que divide (x1, y1) y (x2, y2) en la razón m:n = ((m x2 + n x1)/(m + n), (m y2 + n y1)/(m + n)); el punto medio es el caso m = n. Área de un triángulo = (1/2)|x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2)|. **Triángulos semejantes:** los lados correspondientes están en la misma razón; las áreas están en la razón de los cuadrados de los lados. **Circunferencia:** la tangente es perpendicular al radio en el punto de contacto; las tangentes desde un punto exterior son iguales. Si la tangente mide 12 y el radio 5, la distancia al centro es √(144 + 25) = **13**.
Las tangentes trazadas desde un punto exterior tienen la misma longitud.

fr.title: Géométrie analytique, cercles et triangles semblables

blocks.x: **Formule de la distance :** d = √((x2 - x1)² + (y2 - y1)²) ; par exemple, de (0, 0) à (3, 4) la distance est **5**. **Formule de section :** le point qui partage (x1, y1) et (x2, y2) dans le rapport m:n = ((m x2 + n x1)/(m + n), (m y2 + n y1)/(m + n)) ; le milieu correspond à m = n. Aire d'un triangle = (1/2)|x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2)|. **Triangles semblables :** les côtés correspondants sont dans le même rapport ; les aires sont dans le rapport des carrés des côtés. **Cercle :** la tangente est perpendiculaire au rayon au point de contact ; les tangentes issues d'un point extérieur sont égales. Si la longueur de la tangente est 12 et le rayon 5, la distance au centre est √(144 + 25) = **13**.
Les tangentes issues d'un point extérieur ont la même longueur.

(0, 0) થી (3, 4) સુધીનું અંતર **5**. **વિભાજન સૂત્ર:** (x1, y1) અને (x2, y2) ને m:n ગુણોત્તરમાં વહેંચતો બિંદુ = ((m x2 + n x1)/(m + n), (m y2 + n y1)/(m + n)); m = n હોય ત્યારે તે મધ્યબિંદુ. ત્રિકોણનું ક્ષેત્રફળ = (1/2)|x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2)|. **સમરૂપ ત્રિકોણ:** અનુરૂપ બાજુઓ સમાન ગુણોત્તરમાં; ક્ષેત્રફળનો ગુણોત્તર બાજુઓના વર્ગના ગુણોત્તર જેટલો. **વર્તુળ:** સ્પર્શક સ્પર્શબિંદુએ ત્રિજ્યાને લંબ હોય છે; બહારના બિંદુથી દોરેલા સ્પર્શકો સમાન હોય છે. સ્પર્શકની લંબાઈ 12 અને ત્રિજ્યા 5 હોય તો કેન્દ્રથી અંતર √(144 + 25) = **13**.

blocks.x: **దూర సూత్రం:** d = √((x2 - x1)² + (y2 - y1)²); ఉదా. (0, 0) నుండి (3, 4) వరకు దూరం **5**. **విభజన సూత్రం:** (x1, y1), (x2, y2) బిందువులను m:n నిష్పత్తిలో విభజించే బిందువు = ((m x2 + n x1)/(m + n), (m y2 + n y1)/(m + n)); m = n అయితే అది మధ్య బిందువు. త్రిభుజ వైశాల్యం = (1/2)|x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2)|. **సరూప త్రిభుజాలు:** సంబంధిత భుజాలు ఒకే నిష్పత్తిలో ఉంటాయి; వైశాల్యాల నిష్పత్తి భుజాల వర్గాల నిష్పత్తికి సమానం. **వృత్తం:** స్పర్శరేఖ స్పర్శ బిందువు వద్ద వ్యాసార్ధానికి లంబంగా ఉంటుంది; బాహ్య బిందువు నుండి గీసిన స్పర్శరేఖలు సమానం. స్పర్శరేఖ పొడవు 12, వ్యాసార్ధం 5 అయితే కేంద్రం నుండి దూరం √(144 + 25) = **13**.
బాహ్య బిందువు నుండి గీసిన స్పర్శరేఖల పొడవులు సమానం.

qa.a: స్పర్శ బిందువు వద్ద అవి పరస్పరం లంబంగా ఉంటాయి.

భుజాల నిష్పత్తి 1:2 ఉన్న సరూప త్రిభుజాల వైశాల్యాల నిష్పత్తి

blocks.x: **فاصلے کا کلیہ:** d = √((x2 - x1)² + (y2 - y1)²)؛ مثلاً (0, 0) سے (3, 4) تک فاصلہ **5** ہے۔ **تقسیم کا کلیہ:** (x1, y1) اور (x2, y2) کو m:n کی نسبت سے تقسیم کرنے والا نقطہ = ((m x2 + n x1)/(m + n), (m y2 + n y1)/(m + n))؛ m = n ہو تو یہ وسطی نقطہ ہے۔ مثلث کا رقبہ = (1/2)|x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2)|۔ **مماثل مثلثیں:** متناظر اضلاع ایک ہی نسبت میں ہوتے ہیں؛ رقبوں کی نسبت اضلاع کے مربعوں کی نسبت کے برابر ہوتی ہے۔ **دائرہ:** مماس نقطۂ تماس پر رداس پر عمود ہوتا ہے؛ بیرونی نقطے سے کھینچے گئے مماس برابر ہوتے ہیں۔ مماس کی لمبائی 12 اور رداس 5 ہو تو مرکز سے فاصلہ √(144 + 25) = **13** ہے۔
بیرونی نقطے سے کھینچے گئے مماسوں کی لمبائی برابر ہوتی ہے۔

qa.q: (0, 0) اور (3, 4) کے درمیان فاصلہ کتنا ہے؟
(2, 4) اور (6, 8) کا وسطی نقطہ کیا ہے؟
مماس اور رداس کا تعلق کیا ہے؟
qa.a: نقطۂ تماس پر وہ ایک دوسرے پر عمود ہوتے ہیں۔

qa.q: مماثل مثلثوں کے رقبوں کی نسبت کیا ہے؟
qa.a: متناظر اضلاع کی نسبت کا مربع۔

blocks.x: **Euclid division lemma:** for positive integers a and b there are unique q and r with a = b q + r, 0 <= r < b. Euclid algorithm finds HCF by repeating this. **Fundamental theorem of arithmetic:** every composite number is a product of primes in a unique way (apart from order). Example: 140 = 2^2 x 5 x 7.
Deep dive: Euclid division lemma and algorithm

**Lemma.** For any positive integers a (dividend) and b (divisor) there exist unique whole numbers q and r with a = b q + r and 0 <= r < b. When r = 0, b divides a. **Algorithm for HCF.** To find HCF (c, d) with c > d: divide c by d to get remainder r; if r = 0 the HCF is d; otherwise replace (c, d) by (d, r) and repeat. Example: HCF (455, 42): 455 = 42 x 10 + 35; 42 = 35 x 1 + 7; 35 = 7 x 5 + 0, so HCF = 7. Uses: show that every positive odd integer is 2q + 1 and every even integer 2q; any positive integer is of the form 3q, 3q + 1 or 3q + 2; the square of any positive integer is of the form 3m or 3m + 1; the cube is of the form 9m, 9m + 1 or 9m + 8.
Deep dive: fundamental theorem of arithmetic

**Statement.** Every composite number can be expressed as a product of primes, and this factorisation is unique except for the order of the primes. Example: 32760 = 2^3 x 3^2 x 5 x 7 x 13. **HCF and LCM by prime factorisation.** HCF = product of the smallest power of each common prime. LCM = product of the greatest power of each prime that appears. For two numbers: HCF x LCM = product of the numbers (this does not hold for three numbers). Numbers of the form 4^n can never end in 0 because 4^n = 2^(2n) has no factor 5. **Irrational numbers.** If a prime p divides a^2 then p divides a. Using this, sqrt 2, sqrt 3, sqrt 5 and every sqrt p (p prime) are irrational (proof by contradiction). The sum or difference of a rational and an irrational is irrational; so are the product and quotient of a non-zero rational and an irrational. Example: 3 + 2 sqrt 5 is irrational. The sum of two irrationals can be rational: (2 + sqrt 3) + (2 - sqrt 3) = 4. **Decimal expansions.** A rational number p/q (in lowest terms) has a terminating decimal if and only if q = 2^m x 5^n; otherwise the decimal is non-terminating and repeating. An irrational number has a non-terminating, non-repeating decimal. The number of decimal places in the terminating expansion is the larger of m and n. **Common mistakes.** Forgetting that the factorisation must be into primes (1 is not prime); taking the larger power of each prime for the HCF (that is for LCM); applying HCF x LCM = product to three numbers.

qa.q: State Euclid's division lemma.
qa.a: For positive integers a and b there are unique q and r with a = bq + r, 0 <= r < b.

qa.q: What is Euclid's division algorithm used for?
qa.a: To find the HCF of two positive integers.

qa.q: What is a composite number?
qa.a: A number with more than two factors.

qa.q: Is 1 prime?
qa.a: No. 1 is neither prime nor composite.

qa.q: State the fundamental theorem of arithmetic.
qa.a: Every composite number is a product of primes, uniquely apart from the order.

qa.q: How do you find the HCF by prime factorisation?
qa.a: Multiply the smallest power of each common prime.

qa.q: How do you find the LCM by prime factorisation?
qa.a: Multiply the greatest power of every prime that appears.

qa.q: State the product rule for HCF and LCM.
qa.a: HCF x LCM = product of the two numbers.

qa.q: Does HCF x LCM = product hold for three numbers?
What is an irrational number?
qa.a: A number that cannot be written as p/q; its decimal never ends or repeats.

qa.q: Prove that sqrt 3 is irrational.
qa.a: Assume sqrt 3 = a/b in lowest terms. Then 3b^2 = a^2, so 3 divides a, a = 3c, giving b^2 = 3c^2, so 3 divides b. This contradicts lowest terms.

qa.q: Show that 5 - sqrt 3 is irrational.
qa.a: If it were rational r then sqrt 3 = 5 - r would be rational, which is false.

qa.q: Show that 3 + 2 sqrt 5 is irrational.
qa.a: If it were rational r then sqrt 5 = (r - 3)/2 would be rational, which is false.

qa.q: Show that 1/sqrt 2 is irrational.
qa.a: It equals sqrt 2 / 2; if rational then sqrt 2 would be rational, which is false.

qa.q: Show that any positive odd integer is of the form 4q + 1 or 4q + 3.
qa.a: Dividing by 4 gives remainders 0, 1, 2, 3; remainders 0 and 2 give even numbers.

qa.q: Show that the square of any positive integer is of the form 3m or 3m + 1.
Show that n^2 - n is divisible by 2 for every positive integer n.
qa.a: n (n - 1) is a product of consecutive integers, so one factor is even.

🔑

Big idea

  • Euclid division lemma: for positive integers a and b there are unique q and r with a = b q + r, 0 <= r < b
  • Euclid algorithm finds HCF by repeating this
  • Fundamental theorem of arithmetic: every composite number is a product of primes in a unique way (apart from order)
  • Example: 140 = 22 x 5 x 7
📌

Euclid division lemma and algorithm

  • For any positive integers a (dividend) and b (divisor) there exist unique whole numbers q and r with a = b q + r and 0 <= r < b
  • When r = 0, b divides a
  • Algorithm for HCF
  • To find HCF (c, d) with c > d: divide c by d to get remainder r
Read the full explanation

Lemma. For any positive integers a (dividend) and b (divisor) there exist unique whole numbers q and r with a = b q + r and 0 <= r < b. When r = 0, b divides a. Algorithm for HCF. To find HCF (c, d) with c > d: divide c by d to get remainder r; if r = 0 the HCF is d; otherwise replace (c, d) by (d, r) and repeat. Example: HCF (455, 42): 455 = 42 x 10 + 35; 42 = 35 x 1 + 7; 35 = 7 x 5 + 0, so HCF = 7. Uses: show that every positive odd integer is 2q + 1 and every even integer 2q; any positive integer is of the form 3q, 3q + 1 or 3q + 2; the square of any positive integer is of the form 3m or 3m + 1; the cube is of the form 9m, 9m + 1 or 9m + 8.

⚖️

Fundamental theorem of arithmetic

  • Every composite number can be expressed as a product of primes, and this factorisation is unique except for the order of the primes
  • Example: 32760 = 23 x 32 x 5 x 7 x 13
  • HCF and LCM by prime factorisation
  • HCF = product of the smallest power of each common prime
Read the full explanation

Statement. Every composite number can be expressed as a product of primes, and this factorisation is unique except for the order of the primes. Example: 32760 = 2^3 x 3^2 x 5 x 7 x 13. HCF and LCM by prime factorisation. HCF = product of the smallest power of each common prime. LCM = product of the greatest power of each prime that appears. For two numbers: HCF x LCM = product of the numbers (this does not hold for three numbers). Numbers of the form 4^n can never end in 0 because 4^n = 2^(2n) has no factor 5. Irrational numbers. If a prime p divides a^2 then p divides a. Using this, sqrt 2, sqrt 3, sqrt 5 and every sqrt p (p prime) are irrational (proof by contradiction). The sum or difference of a rational and an irrational is irrational; so are the product and quotient of a non-zero rational and an irrational. Example: 3 + 2 sqrt 5 is irrational. The sum of two irrationals can be rational: (2 + sqrt 3) + (2 - sqrt 3) = 4. Decimal expansions. A rational number p/q (in lowest terms) has a terminating decimal if and only if q = 2^m x 5^n; otherwise the decimal is non-terminating and repeating. An irrational number has a non-terminating, non-repeating decimal. The number of decimal places in the terminating expansion is the larger of m and n. Common mistakes. Forgetting that the factorisation must be into primes (1 is not prime); taking the larger power of each prime for the HCF (that is for LCM); applying HCF x LCM = product to three numbers.

lessons.title: Areas related to circles
yt: class 10 areas related to circles

blocks.x: Circumference of a circle is 2 pi r and area is pi r^2. A sector with angle theta has arc length (theta/360) x 2 pi r and area (theta/360) x pi r^2. Area of segment = area of sector - area of triangle. Use pi = 22/7 unless told otherwise.
Deep dive: circle, sector, segment

Circumference C = 2 pi r = pi d. Area A = pi r^2. For a sector of angle theta at the centre: arc length l = (theta/360) x 2 pi r and area = (theta/360) x pi r^2 = (1/2) l r. A minor segment is the region between a chord and its arc: area = area of sector - area of triangle formed by the radii and the chord = (theta/360) pi r^2 - (1/2) r^2 sin theta. The major segment area = pi r^2 - minor segment area.
Deep dive: special figures

Ring (annulus) between radii R and r: area = pi (R^2 - r^2). Distance moved by a wheel in one rotation = circumference; in n rotations = n x 2 pi r. A minute hand of length l sweeps an angle of 6 degrees per minute, so in t minutes it sweeps area (6t/360) pi l^2. An equilateral triangle of side a has area (sqrt 3 / 4) a^2; a square of side a inscribed in a circle has diagonal a sqrt 2 = 2r. Combined figures: find each area separately, then add or subtract. **Common mistakes:** using diameter instead of radius, forgetting to subtract the triangle for a segment, mixing units (cm and m).
Hindi saransh
Parridhi 2 pi r, kshetrafal pi r^2. Sector = (theta/360) x circle.
Segment = sector - triangle.

Big idea

  • Circumference of a circle is 2 pi r and area is pi r2
  • A sector with angle theta has arc length (theta/360) x 2 pi r and area (theta/360) x pi r2
  • Area of segment = area of sector - area of triangle

📐

Circle, sector, segment

  • Circumference C = 2 pi r = pi d
  • Area A = pi r2
  • For a sector of angle theta at the centre: arc length l = (theta/360) x 2 pi r and area = (theta/360) x pi r2 = (1/2) l r
  • A minor segment is the region between a chord and its arc: area = area of sector - area of triangle formed by the radii and the chord = (theta/360)…
Read the full explanation

Circumference C = 2 pi r = pi d. Area A = pi r^2. For a sector of angle theta at the centre: arc length l = (theta/360) x 2 pi r and area = (theta/360) x pi r^2 = (1/2) l r. A minor segment is the region between a chord and its arc: area = area of sector - area of triangle formed by the radii and the chord = (theta/360) pi r^2 - (1/2) r^2 sin theta. The major segment area = pi r^2 - minor segment area.

🧠

Special figures

  • Ring (annulus) between radii R and r: area = pi (R2 - r2)
  • Distance moved by a wheel in one rotation = circumference
  • In n rotations = n x 2 pi r
  • A minute hand of length l sweeps an angle of 6 degrees per minute, so in t minutes it sweeps area (6t/360) pi l2
Read the full explanation

Ring (annulus) between radii R and r: area = pi (R^2 - r^2). Distance moved by a wheel in one rotation = circumference; in n rotations = n x 2 pi r. A minute hand of length l sweeps an angle of 6 degrees per minute, so in t minutes it sweeps area (6t/360) pi l^2. An equilateral triangle of side a has area (sqrt 3 / 4) a^2; a square of side a inscribed in a circle has diagonal a sqrt 2 = 2r. Combined figures: find each area separately, then add or subtract. yt: class 10 surface areas and volumes

blocks.x: Combine solids such as cone on cylinder, hemisphere on cylinder, and find the frustum of a cone. Curved surface area of cylinder 2 pi r h, cone pi r l, sphere 4 pi r^2, hemisphere 2 pi r^2. Volumes: cylinder pi r^2 h, cone one-third pi r^2 h, sphere (4/3) pi r^3, hemisphere (2/3) pi r^3.
Deep dive: standard solids

Cylinder (radius r, height h): CSA 2 pi r h, TSA 2 pi r (r + h), volume pi r^2 h. Cone: slant height l = sqrt (r^2 + h^2), CSA pi r l, TSA pi r (l + r), volume (1/3) pi r^2 h. Sphere: surface 4 pi r^2, volume (4/3) pi r^3. Hemisphere: CSA 2 pi r^2, TSA 3 pi r^2, volume (2/3) pi r^3.
Deep dive: combination of solids

For a toy made of a cone on a hemisphere, or a tent made of a cylinder and a cone, find the total surface area by adding the curved surfaces only for the joined parts (the circular faces that are joined are hidden). Total volume is the sum of volumes. For a capsule (cylinder with two hemispheres): TSA = 2 pi r h + 4 pi r^2 and volume = pi r^2 h + (4/3) pi r^3.
Deep dive: conversion of solids and frustum

When a solid is melted and recast into another, the volume stays the same: a sphere of radius R recast into n small spheres of radius r gives n = R^3/r^3. For a frustum of a cone with radii r1 > r2 and height h: slant height l = sqrt (h^2 + (r1 - r2)^2); volume (1/3) pi h (r1^2 + r2^2 + r1 r2); CSA pi (r1 + r2) l; TSA = CSA + pi r1^2 + pi r2^2. **Common mistakes:** using height instead of slant height in CSA of a cone, forgetting the joined faces are not exposed, and mixing units (cm to m means cubic factors).

  • Hemisphere: CSA 2 pi r2, TSA 3 pi r2, volume (2/3) pi r3

Combination of solids

For a toy made of a cone on a hemisphere, or a tent made of a cylinder and a cone, find the total surface area by adding the curved surfaces only for the joined parts (the circular faces that are joined are hidden). Total volume is the sum of volumes. For a capsule (cylinder with two hemispheres): TSA = 2 pi r h + 4 pi r^2 and volume = pi r^2 h + (4/3) pi r^3.

🌟

Conversion of solids and frustum

  • When a solid is melted and recast into another, the volume stays the same: a sphere of radius R recast into n small spheres of radius r gives n =…
  • For a frustum of a cone with radii r1 > r2 and height h: slant height l = sqrt (h2 + (r1 - r2)2)
  • Volume (1/3) pi h (r12 + r22 + r1 r2)
  • CSA pi (r1 + r2) l
Read the full explanation

When a solid is melted and recast into another, the volume stays the same: a sphere of radius R recast into n small spheres of radius r gives n = R^3/r^3. For a frustum of a cone with radii r1 > r2 and height h: slant height l = sqrt (h^2 + (r1 - r2)^2); volume (1/3) pi h (r1^2 + r2^2 + r1 r2); CSA pi (r1 + r2) l; TSA = CSA + pi r1^2 + pi r2^2. blocks.x: For grouped data, mean = sum(f x) / sum f using class marks x. Median = l + ((n/2 - cf)/f) x h. Mode = l + ((f1 - f0)/(2 f1 - f0 - f2)) x h. Empirical relation: 3 median = mode + 2 mean. Cumulative frequency curves (ogives) give the median graphically.
Deep dive: mean of grouped data

Direct method: x = class mark, mean = sum (f x)/sum f. Assumed mean method: d = x - a, mean = a + sum (f d)/sum f. Step-deviation: u = (x - a)/h, mean = a + h x sum (f u)/sum f. All three give the same answer.
Deep dive: mode and median

Modal class is the class with the highest frequency. Mode = l + ((f1 - f0)/(2 f1 - f0 - f2)) x h, where l is the lower limit of the modal class, f1 its frequency, f0 and f2 the frequencies of the classes before and after, and h the class size. Median class is the class whose cumulative frequency first exceeds n/2. Median = l + ((n/2 - cf)/f) x h where cf is the cumulative frequency of the class before it. Relationship: Mode = 3 Median - 2 Mean.
Deep dive: ogives

A less-than ogive plots upper class limits against cumulative frequency (less than type); a more-than ogive plots lower limits against cumulative frequency (more than type). The x-coordinate of the intersection of the two ogives is the median; so is the x-value for n/2 on either curve. **Common mistakes:** using class limits instead of class marks, forgetting to make classes continuous, and taking cf of the median class rather than the class before it.

lessons.title: Probability
yt: class 10 maths probability

blocks.x: Probability measures how likely an event is. For equally likely outcomes, P(E) = number of favourable outcomes / total number of outcomes. It always lies between 0 and 1: 0 for an impossible event and 1 for a sure event. The sum of the probabilities of all elementary outcomes of an experiment is 1, and P(E) + P(not E) = 1. Typical experiments are tossing coins, throwing dice, drawing cards from a pack of 52 and picking balls from a bag.
Deep dive: Classical definition

P(E) = favourable / total. Outcomes must be equally likely. For one coin the sample space is {H, T}; for one die it is {1,2,3,4,5,6}; for two dice there are 36 outcomes; for two coins 4; for three coins 8.
Deep dive: Complementary events

The complement of E is not E, with P(not E) = 1 - P(E). It is the quickest route for questions with the words at least, at most or not. For example P(at least one head in two tosses) = 1 - P(TT) = 3/4.
Deep dive: Playing cards

A pack has 52 cards: 4 suits (spades, clubs black; hearts, diamonds red) of 13 cards each. There are 12 face cards (J, Q, K), 4 aces, 26 red and 26 black cards. Remember that the probability of a king is 4/52 = 1/13.
Deep dive: Two dice
The sample space has 36 pairs. Sum 7 has 6 ways, the most likely sum. Sum 2 and 12 have 1 way each. A doublet (same number) has 6 outcomes. Number of ways for sum s is 6 - |s - 7|.
Hindi saransh
Probability = anukul parinam / kul parinam. Ye 0 se 1 ke beech hoti hai. P(E) + P(E nahi) = 1. Ek paase ke 6 parinam, do paason ke 36, taash ke 52 patte.
At least one means 1 minus none. Always count the total first.

Define probability of an event.
qa.a: P(E) = number of outcomes favourable to E divided by the total number of equally likely outcomes of the experiment.

qa.q: Why can probability never exceed 1?
qa.a: Favourable outcomes cannot be more than the total outcomes, so the ratio is at most 1; it equals 1 only for a sure event.

qa.q: What does a probability of 0 mean?
qa.a: The event can never happen. For example getting 7 on a single die.

qa.q: State the complementary event rule.
qa.a: P(E) + P(not E) = 1. So P(not E) = 1 - P(E).

qa.q: How do you handle at least one questions?
qa.a: Compute the probability of none and subtract from 1. For two coins, P(at least one head) = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4.

qa.q: Write the sample space of tossing two coins.
qa.a: {HH, HT, TH, TT}, four equally likely outcomes.

qa.q: How many cards are in a pack and how are they divided?
qa.a: 52 cards in 4 suits of 13: spades and clubs are black, hearts and diamonds are red. Each suit has A, 2 to 10, J, Q, K.

qa.q: Are the outcomes of a biased coin equally likely?
qa.a: No. The classical formula applies only to equally likely outcomes.

qa.q: Difference between experimental and theoretical probability?
qa.a: Experimental probability comes from repeated trials; theoretical comes from reasoning with equally likely outcomes. Class 10 deals with the theoretical type.

qa.q: Why is the sum 7 most likely with two dice?
qa.a: It has 6 favourable pairs out of 36, more than any other sum.

problems.q: A bag has 5 red, 3 blue and 2 green balls. One ball is drawn at random. Find the probability that it is not blue.
problems.a: Total = 10. P(blue) = 3/10 so P(not blue) = 1 - 3/10 = 7/10.

A card is drawn from a well shuffled pack of 52 cards. Find the probability that it is neither a king nor a red card.
problems.a: Red cards 26 and kings 4, of which 2 are red, so red or king = 26 + 2 = 28. Neither = 52 - 28 = 24. P = 24/52 = 6/13.

rubric.t: Count red or king without double counting

Probability measures how likely an event is. For equally likely outcomes, P(E) = number of favourable outcomes / total number of outcomes. It always lies between 0 and 1: 0 for an impossible event and 1 for a sure event. The sum of the probabilities of all elementary outcomes of an experiment is 1, and P(E) + P(not E) = 1. Typical experiments are tossing coins, throwing dice, drawing cards from a pack of 52 and picking balls from a bag.

📘

Classical definition

  • P(E) = favourable / total
  • Outcomes must be equally likely
  • For one coin the sample space is {H, T}
  • For one die it is {1,2,3,4,5,6}
Read the full explanation

P(E) = favourable / total. Outcomes must be equally likely. For one coin the sample space is {H, T}; for one die it is {1,2,3,4,5,6}; for two dice there are 36 outcomes; for two coins 4; for three coins 8.

🧠

Complementary events

  • The complement of E is not E, with P(not E) = 1 - P(E)
  • It is the quickest route for questions with the words at least, at most or not
  • For example P(at least one head in two tosses) = 1 - P(TT) = 3/4
🌟

Playing cards

  • A pack has 52 cards: 4 suits (spades, clubs black
  • Hearts, diamonds red) of 13 cards each
  • There are 12 face cards (J, Q, K), 4 aces, 26 red and 26 black cards
  • Remember that the probability of a king is 4/52 = 1/13
🔬

Two dice

  • The sample space has 36 pairs
  • Sum 7 has 6 ways, the most likely sum
  • Sum 2 and 12 have 1 way each
  • A doublet (same number) has 6 outcomes
Read the full explanation

The sample space has 36 pairs. Sum 7 has 6 ways, the most likely sum. Sum 2 and 12 have 1 way each. A doublet (same number) has 6 outcomes. Number of ways for sum s is 6 - |s - 7|.

lessons.title: Triangles
yt: class 10 maths triangles similarity

blocks.x: Two figures with the same shape but not necessarily the same size are similar. Two triangles are similar if corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are in the same ratio. The Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales) says that a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio. The criteria AA, SSS and SAS prove similarity. The areas of similar triangles are in the ratio of the squares of corresponding sides. The Pythagoras theorem says that in a right triangle the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.
Deep dive: Basic Proportionality Theorem

If DE is parallel to BC in triangle ABC with D on AB and E on AC, then AD/DB = AE/EC. The converse is also true: if a line divides two sides in the same ratio, it is parallel to the third side. Use it to find unknown lengths: write the ratio of the segments on one side and equate it to the matching ratio on the other.
Deep dive: Criteria for similarity

AA: two equal angles are enough, because the third is then equal. SSS: all three side ratios are equal. SAS: one angle equal and the including sides in the same ratio. Always match vertices in order, write the similarity as triangle ABC ~ triangle PQR, and then the corresponding sides are AB/PQ = BC/QR = CA/RP.
Deep dive: Areas of similar triangles

If triangle ABC ~ triangle PQR then area(ABC)/area(PQR) = (AB/PQ)^2 = (BC/QR)^2 = (CA/RP)^2. The ratio of the areas is the square of the ratio of sides, and the ratio of perimeters, medians, altitudes and angle bisectors equals the ratio of sides. A scale factor k on lengths gives k squared on areas.
Deep dive: Pythagoras theorem

In a right triangle with hypotenuse c and other sides a and b, a^2 + b^2 = c^2. The converse says that if the square of the longest side equals the sum of the squares of the other two, the angle opposite the longest side is a right angle. Common triples are 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17 and 7-24-25. An altitude on the hypotenuse makes two triangles similar to the whole.
Hindi saransh

Do tribhuj similar hote hain jab unke kon barabar hon aur bhujaon ka anupat same ho. BPT: DE || BC to AD/DB = AE/EC. Kshetrafal ka anupat bhujaon ke anupat ka varg hota hai. Pythagoras: a^2 + b^2 = c^2.
Ratio of areas = (ratio of sides) squared. Check ratio of perimeters = ratio of sides.

State and prove the Basic Proportionality Theorem.
qa.a: If DE || BC in triangle ABC, then AD/DB = AE/EC. Proof: join BE and CD. ar(ADE)/ar(BDE) = AD/DB (same height), ar(ADE)/ar(CDE) = AE/EC (same height), and ar(BDE) = ar(CDE) as they lie on the same base DE between parallels. Hence AD/DB = AE/EC.

qa.q: State and prove the converse of BPT.
qa.a: If AD/DB = AE/EC, then DE || BC. Suppose not and draw DE' || BC meeting AC at E'. By BPT AD/DB = AE'/E'C, so AE/EC = AE'/E'C, which makes E and E' coincide, a contradiction. So DE || BC.

qa.q: How do you prove the AA criterion?
qa.a: Take triangles ABC and DEF with angle A = angle D and angle B = angle E. Cut DP = AB and DQ = AC on DE and DF. Then triangle ABC is congruent to DPQ by SAS and PQ is parallel to EF, so DP/DE = DQ/DF by BPT, giving AB/DE = AC/DF. Equal angles then give the third ratio.

qa.q: Prove that the ratio of areas of two similar triangles is the square of the ratio of their sides.
qa.a: Draw altitudes AM and PN in similar triangles ABC and PQR. ar(ABC)/ar(PQR) = (BC x AM)/(QR x PN). Triangles ABM and PQN are similar by AA, so AM/PN = AB/PQ = BC/QR. Substituting gives (BC/QR)^2.

qa.q: Prove the Pythagoras theorem using similar triangles.
qa.a: In right triangle ABC with right angle at B, draw BD perpendicular to AC. Triangles ADB, BDC and ABC are similar. From ADB ~ ABC, AB^2 = AD x AC. From BDC ~ ABC, BC^2 = DC x AC. Adding gives AB^2 + BC^2 = AC(AD + DC) = AC^2.

qa.q: Prove the converse of the Pythagoras theorem.
qa.a: Given AC^2 = AB^2 + BC^2, construct a right triangle PQR with PQ = AB and QR = BC and right angle at Q. Then PR^2 = AB^2 + BC^2 = AC^2, so PR = AC. Triangles ABC and PQR are congruent by SSS, so angle B = 90 degrees.

qa.q: What is the difference between similar and congruent triangles?
qa.a: Congruent triangles have equal corresponding sides and angles. Similar triangles have equal angles and proportional sides. Every congruent pair is similar but not the reverse.

qa.q: What are the common mistakes in similarity problems?
qa.a: Matching vertices wrongly, using the ratio of sides as ratio of areas, forgetting to square or take the square root, and applying Pythagoras to a triangle that is not right-angled.

qa.q: How do you decide which side is the hypotenuse?
qa.a: It is the side opposite the right angle and is always the longest. In the converse test, square the longest side and compare it with the sum of squares of the other two.

qa.q: If two triangles have equal angles, are their sides equal?
qa.a: No. Equal angles only prove similarity (AA). Sides are proportional, and they are equal only when the scale factor is 1.

qa.q: What is the ratio of medians of similar triangles?
qa.a: It equals the ratio of the corresponding sides, as do altitudes, angle bisectors and perimeters.

qa.q: What is the midpoint theorem and how does it follow from BPT?
qa.a: The line joining the midpoints of two sides is parallel to the third side and half of it. With AD/DB = AE/EC = 1 the converse of BPT gives DE || BC and similar triangles give DE = BC/2.

problems.a: AD/DB = AE/EC, so 4/6 = 6/EC and EC = 6 x 6 / 4 = 9 cm.

problems.q: Two similar triangles have areas 81 cm^2 and 144 cm^2. If a side of the smaller triangle is 6 cm, find the corresponding side of the larger one.

rubric.t: Area ratio equals square of side ratio

problems.q: Prove that if a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle to intersect the other two sides in distinct points, the other two sides are divided in the same ratio.
problems.a: In triangle ABC, DE || BC. Join BE and CD. Triangles ADE and BDE share the same height from E, so ar(ADE)/ar(BDE) = AD/DB. Triangles ADE and CDE share the height from D, so ar(ADE)/ar(CDE) = AE/EC. Triangles BDE and CDE are on the same base DE and between the same parallels, so ar(BDE) = ar(CDE). Hence AD/DB = AE/EC.

Visual lesson

Two figures with the same shape but not necessarily the same size are similar

1Big idea›2Basic Proportionality…›3Criteria for similarity›4Areas of similar triangles›5Pythagoras theorem
🔑

Big idea

  • Two figures with the same shape but not necessarily the same size are similar
  • Two triangles are similar if corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are in the same ratio
  • The Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales) says that a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio
  • The criteria AA, SSS and SAS prove similarity
Read the full explanation

Two figures with the same shape but not necessarily the same size are similar. Two triangles are similar if corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are in the same ratio. The Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales) says that a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides in the same ratio. The criteria AA, SSS and SAS prove similarity. The areas of similar triangles are in the ratio of the squares of corresponding sides. The Pythagoras theorem says that in a right triangle the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.

📘

Basic Proportionality Theorem

  • If DE is parallel to BC in triangle ABC with D on AB and E on AC, then AD/DB = AE/EC
  • The converse is also true: if a line divides two sides in the same ratio, it is parallel to the third side
  • Use it to find unknown lengths: write the ratio of the segments on one side and equate it to the matching ratio on the other
🧠

Criteria for similarity

  • AA: two equal angles are enough, because the third is then equal
  • SSS: all three side ratios are equal
  • SAS: one angle equal and the including sides in the same ratio
  • Always match vertices in order, write the similarity as triangle ABC ~ triangle PQR, and then the corresponding sides are AB/PQ = BC/QR = CA/RP
📐

Areas of similar triangles

  • If triangle ABC ~ triangle PQR then area(ABC)/area(PQR) = (AB/PQ)2 = (BC/QR)2 = (CA/RP)2
  • The ratio of the areas is the square of the ratio of sides, and the ratio of perimeters, medians, altitudes and angle bisectors equals the ratio of…
  • A scale factor k on lengths gives k squared on areas
⚖️

Pythagoras theorem

  • In a right triangle with hypotenuse c and other sides a and b, a2 + b2 = c2
  • The converse says that if the square of the longest side equals the sum of the squares of the other two, the angle opposite the longest side is a…
  • Common triples are 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17 and 7-24-25
  • An altitude on the hypotenuse makes two triangles similar to the whole
Read the full explanation

In a right triangle with hypotenuse c and other sides a and b, a^2 + b^2 = c^2. The converse says that if the square of the longest side equals the sum of the squares of the other two, the angle opposite the longest side is a right angle. Common triples are 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17 and 7-24-25. An altitude on the hypotenuse makes two triangles similar to the whole.

lessons.title: Power-sharing
yt: class 10 political science power sharing

blocks.x: Power-sharing is the idea that power should be divided among different organs of government and social groups so that no one holds all of it. Belgium and Sri Lanka show two contrasting stories. Belgium accommodated the Dutch-speaking, French-speaking and German-speaking communities through a community government and equal representation, while Sri Lanka's majoritarian measures such as the 1956 Sinhala Only Act deepened Tamil alienation and led to civil war. Power-sharing is good because it reduces conflict between social groups (prudential reason) and because it is the very spirit of democracy (moral reason). It takes four forms: horizontal, vertical, between social groups, and between political parties and movements.
Deep dive: Belgium

Belgium is a small European country with 59 per cent Dutch-speaking people in the Flemish region, 40 per cent French-speaking in Wallonia, and one per cent German-speaking. In the capital Brussels, 80 per cent speak French and 20 per cent Dutch. The Dutch-speaking community was economically poorer earlier, which caused tension. The Belgian leaders amended the constitution four times from 1970 to 1993: equal number of Dutch and French-speaking ministers in the central government, state governments not subordinate to the central government, Brussels with a separate government where both communities have equal representation, and a separate community government for each language community with power over cultural, educational and language issues.
Deep dive: Sri Lanka

Sri Lanka became independent in 1948. The major community is Sinhala-speakers (74 per cent), Tamil-speakers are 18 per cent, including Sri Lankan Tamils (13 per cent) in the north and east and Indian Tamils (5 per cent) of the plantation areas; Muslims are about 7 per cent. In 1956 an Act recognised Sinhala as the only official language, disregarding Tamil. Preference was given to Sinhala applicants for jobs and Buddhism was given state protection. The Tamils felt discriminated against, the relations turned bitter, and a civil war broke out in the 1980s, with the LTTE demanding Tamil Eelam. The war ended in 2009.
Deep dive: Forms of power-sharing

Horizontal power-sharing spreads power among legislature, executive and judiciary, so each checks the others (checks and balances). Vertical power-sharing divides power among governments at different levels: the union, state and local government, called federal division. Power can also be shared among social groups, e.g. community government in Belgium and reserved constituencies for SC and ST in India. Finally power is shared among political parties, pressure groups and movements which compete for power, as in coalition governments.
Deep dive: Why power-sharing is desirable

The prudential reason: it helps reduce the possibility of conflict between social groups, and since social conflict leads to violence and political instability, power-sharing ensures stability of the political order. Imposing the will of the majority may look attractive in the short run but undermines the unity of the nation in the long run. The moral reason: power-sharing is the very spirit of democracy because people have a right to be consulted on how they are to be governed. A legitimate government is one where citizens acquire a stake in the system.
Hindi saransh

Satta ka batwara loktantra ka mool tattva hai. Belgium mein community government aur barabar pratinidhitva se sangharsh kam hua. Sri Lanka mein 1956 ke Sinhala Only Act se Tamil log alag-thalag pade aur gruh yuddh hua. Power-sharing ke chaar roop: kshaitij, uddhwadhar, samajik samuh aur rajnitik dal.
Remember the pairs: Belgium = accommodation; Sri Lanka = majoritarianism; 1956 = Sinhala Only Act.

qa.q: In which year did Sri Lanka become independent?
In which year was the Sinhala Only Act passed?
In which year did the Belgian constitution see its last amendment in the series of four?
In which year did the Sri Lankan civil war end?
Why did Belgium not break up despite linguistic diversity?
qa.a: It chose accommodation: equal Dutch and French ministers in the centre, community governments and a separate Brussels government gave each community a stake in the country.

qa.q: Why did Belgian leaders choose a separate government for Brussels?
qa.a: Because the city has French and Dutch speakers and neither wished to be dominated, so equal representation was given.

qa.q: What does the Sri Lankan example teach about democracy?
qa.a: That majority rule without respect for minorities can destroy unity and cause violence.

qa.q: What does the Belgian example teach?
qa.a: That power-sharing and accommodation can keep a diverse country peaceful and united.

qa.q: How does the independent judiciary help power-sharing?
qa.a: It can strike down laws and executive acts that exceed constitutional limits, protecting the balance among organs.

qa.q: Why is the federal division an example of power-sharing?
qa.a: The constitution gives states and the centre separate powers so the central government cannot take all authority.

qa.q: How do pressure groups share power?
qa.a: They do not contest elections but influence decisions through lobbying, campaigns and agitations.

qa.q: What was the Belgian model of power-sharing?
qa.a: It rested on community governments elected by language groups, equal representation in the centre and Brussels, and state governments not subordinate to the centre.

qa.q: Why were the Sri Lankan Tamils unhappy?
qa.a: The Sinhala Only Act, preference to Sinhalas in jobs and university and state protection to Buddhism made them feel discriminated against.

qa.q: How did the Sri Lankan conflict turn violent?
qa.a: Peaceful demands by Tamil parties were ignored, trust broke down and the demand for Tamil Eelam by LTTE led to a civil war from the 1980s, ending in 2009.

qa.q: Give an example of horizontal power-sharing in India.
qa.a: The legislature, executive and judiciary have separate powers and the courts can check the executive and legislature by judicial review.

qa.q: Give an example of vertical power-sharing in India.
qa.a: Power is divided between the Union government, state governments and local bodies like panchayats and municipalities.

qa.q: Why is power-sharing called the spirit of democracy?
qa.a: Democracy means people rule themselves, so they have a right to be consulted in how they are governed and power must be shared with them.

qa.q: Why is majoritarianism dangerous?
qa.a: It ignores minorities, creates resentment and can lead to conflict and break-up of the country.

qa.q: How is power shared among social groups in India?
qa.a: Through reserved constituencies for SC and ST in legislatures and in some states for women in local bodies.

qa.q: How is power shared among political parties?
qa.a: Through competition for power, coalition governments and pressure groups and movements that influence policy.

qa.q: Who were the main communities in Sri Lanka?
qa.a: Sinhala-speakers, Sri Lankan Tamils, Indian Tamils and Muslims.

qa.q: Why is a legitimate government one that shares power?
qa.a: Citizens feel they have a stake in the system and accept its decisions.

problems.q: Distinguish between the prudential and moral reasons for power-sharing.
problems.a: Prudential: power-sharing reduces conflict between social groups and so ensures political stability and unity. Moral: power-sharing is the spirit of democracy; people have a right to be consulted in how they are governed, giving the government legitimacy.

problems.q: Explain the steps taken by Belgium to accommodate regional and linguistic differences.
problems.a: Belgium amended its constitution four times between 1970 and 1993. Dutch and French-speaking ministers are equal in the central government; state governments are not subordinate to the centre; Brussels has a separate government with equal representation; community governments exist for each language group with control over culture, education and language. This reduced the conflict.

problems.q: Compare the approaches of Belgium and Sri Lanka to ethnic diversity and evaluate which is more democratic.
problems.a: Belgium shared power with Dutch, French and German communities through community governments and equal representation, giving each a stake and keeping the country united. Sri Lanka imposed Sinhala as the only official language in 1956, favoured Sinhalas in jobs and gave state protection to Buddhism, which alienated Tamils, led to civil war from the 1980s and lasting damage. Belgium is more democratic as it respects minority rights and consultation; majoritarianism undermines national unity.

Visual lesson

Power-sharing

Power-sharing is the idea that power should be divided among different organs of government and social groups so that no one holds all of it

Read the full explanation

Power-sharing is the idea that power should be divided among different organs of government and social groups so that no one holds all of it. Belgium and Sri Lanka show two contrasting stories. Belgium accommodated the Dutch-speaking, French-speaking and German-speaking communities through a community government and equal representation, while Sri Lanka's majoritarian measures such as the 1956 Sinhala Only Act deepened Tamil alienation and led to civil war. Power-sharing is good because it reduces conflict between social groups (prudential reason) and because it is the very spirit of democracy (moral reason). It takes four forms: horizontal, vertical, between social groups, and between political parties and movements.

📌

  • In the capital Brussels, 80 per cent speak French and 20 per cent Dutch
  • The Dutch-speaking community was economically poorer earlier, which caused tension
  • The Belgian leaders amended the constitution four times from 1970 to 1993: equal number of Dutch and French-speaking ministers in the central…
Read the full explanation

Belgium is a small European country with 59 per cent Dutch-speaking people in the Flemish region, 40 per cent French-speaking in Wallonia, and one per cent German-speaking. In the capital Brussels, 80 per cent speak French and 20 per cent Dutch. The Dutch-speaking community was economically poorer earlier, which caused tension. The Belgian leaders amended the constitution four times from 1970 to 1993: equal number of Dutch and French-speaking ministers in the central government, state governments not subordinate to the central government, Brussels with a separate government where both communities have equal representation, and a separate community government for each language community with power over cultural, educational and language issues.

🧠

Sri Lanka

  • Sri Lanka became independent in 1948
  • The major community is Sinhala-speakers (74 per cent), Tamil-speakers are 18 per cent, including Sri Lankan Tamils (13 per cent) in the north and…
  • Muslims are about 7 per cent
  • In 1956 an Act recognised Sinhala as the only official language, disregarding Tamil
Read the full explanation

Sri Lanka became independent in 1948. The major community is Sinhala-speakers (74 per cent), Tamil-speakers are 18 per cent, including Sri Lankan Tamils (13 per cent) in the north and east and Indian Tamils (5 per cent) of the plantation areas; Muslims are about 7 per cent. In 1956 an Act recognised Sinhala as the only official language, disregarding Tamil. Preference was given to Sinhala applicants for jobs and Buddhism was given state protection. The Tamils felt discriminated against, the relations turned bitter, and a civil war broke out in the 1980s, with the LTTE demanding Tamil Eelam. The war ended in 2009.

🚀

Forms of power-sharing

  • Horizontal power-sharing spreads power among legislature, executive and judiciary, so each checks the others (checks and balances)
  • Vertical power-sharing divides power among governments at different levels: the union, state and local government, called federal division
  • Power can also be shared among social groups, e.g. community government in Belgium and reserved constituencies for SC and ST in India
  • Finally power is shared among political parties, pressure groups and movements which compete for power, as in coalition governments
Read the full explanation

Horizontal power-sharing spreads power among legislature, executive and judiciary, so each checks the others (checks and balances). Vertical power-sharing divides power among governments at different levels: the union, state and local government, called federal division. Power can also be shared among social groups, e.g. community government in Belgium and reserved constituencies for SC and ST in India. Finally power is shared among political parties, pressure groups and movements which compete for power, as in coalition governments.

🚀

Why power-sharing is desirable

  • The prudential reason: it helps reduce the possibility of conflict between social groups, and since social conflict leads to violence and political…
  • Imposing the will of the majority may look attractive in the short run but undermines the unity of the nation in the long run
  • The moral reason: power-sharing is the very spirit of democracy because people have a right to be consulted on how they are to be governed
  • A legitimate government is one where citizens acquire a stake in the system
Read the full explanation

The prudential reason: it helps reduce the possibility of conflict between social groups, and since social conflict leads to violence and political instability, power-sharing ensures stability of the political order. Imposing the will of the majority may look attractive in the short run but undermines the unity of the nation in the long run. The moral reason: power-sharing is the very spirit of democracy because people have a right to be consulted on how they are to be governed. A legitimate government is one where citizens acquire a stake in the system.
