lessons.title: Federalism
yt: class 10 political science federalism

blocks.x: Federalism is a system of government in which power is divided between a central authority and various constituent units of the country. It has two or more levels of government, each with its own jurisdiction, whose existence and authority are guaranteed by the constitution, which cannot be unilaterally changed by one level. Courts act as umpires in disputes. India has a three-tier structure: Union, States and local governments. The Constitution has a Union List (97 subjects), State List (66) and Concurrent List (47). Federalism is practised by coming together (USA, Switzerland, Australia) or holding together (India, Spain, Belgium). Linguistic states, language policy, centre-state relations and decentralisation through the 73rd and 74th Amendments (1992) strengthen Indian federalism.
Deep dive: Features of federalism

There are two or more levels of government. Different tiers govern the same citizens but have their own jurisdiction in specific matters of legislation, taxation and administration. The jurisdictions of the respective levels are specified in the constitution, so their existence and authority are constitutionally guaranteed. Fundamental provisions of the constitution cannot be unilaterally changed by one level of government; such changes require the consent of both. Courts have the power to interpret the constitution and the powers of different levels. Sources of revenue for each level are clearly specified. The dual objectives are to safeguard and promote unity of the country while accommodating regional diversity.
Deep dive: Coming together and holding together

In coming together federations, independent states come together on their own to form a bigger unit to pool their sovereignty and retain identity, e.g. USA, Switzerland and Australia; all states usually have equal power. In holding together federations, a large country decides to divide its power between the national government and states, e.g. India, Spain and Belgium; the central government is usually more powerful and different constituent units may have unequal powers, as in India where some states have special status.
Deep dive: Division of powers in India

The Union List includes subjects of national importance such as defence, foreign affairs, banking, communications and currency, on which only the Union can legislate. The State List includes police, trade, commerce, agriculture and irrigation, on which states legislate. The Concurrent List includes education, forests, trade unions, marriage, adoption and succession, where both can legislate, and if there is a conflict the Union law prevails. Residuary subjects, those not in any list such as computer software, are with the Union. Not all states have identical powers: Jammu and Kashmir had special status under Article 370 till 2019, and Union Territories such as Chandigarh are administered by the Centre.
Deep dive: How federalism is practised

Linguistic states: from 1950 several old states were reorganised on linguistic lines, the State Reorganisation Commission (1956) producing 14 states and 6 Union Territories. Language policy: Hindi is the official language but spoken by only about 40 per cent; there are 22 scheduled languages and English is also used; no language was declared national. Centre-state relations: after 1990, regional parties and coalition governments strengthened federalism and Article 356 was used less after the S. R. Bommai case (1994). Decentralisation: the 73rd and 74th Amendments (1992) made local governments third tier; elections are regular, reservation of at least one third for women, and State Election Commissions conduct elections; Gram Sabha is the foundation.
Hindi saransh

Union 97, State 66, Concurrent 47. Hindi is not the national language; there are 22 scheduled languages.

problems.q: List any four features of federalism.
problems.a: Two or more levels of government; each with its own jurisdiction; constitutionally guaranteed powers that cannot be changed unilaterally; courts as umpires; clear revenue sources; aim of unity with diversity.

problems.q: How is power divided between the Union and the States in India? Explain with the three lists.
problems.a: Union List (97 subjects) like defence and foreign affairs; State List (66) like police and agriculture; Concurrent List (47) like education and marriage where Union law prevails in conflict; residuary subjects with the Union.

problems.q: Explain how decentralisation strengthened democracy in India after 1992.
problems.a: 73rd and 74th Amendments made local governments a constitutional third tier; regular elections by State Election Commissions, reservation for SC, ST, OBC and one third for women, devolution of powers and resources, Gram Sabha participation, bringing decisions closer to people, though states often don't transfer enough funds.

Visual lesson

Federalism

Federalism is a system of government in which power is divided between a central authority and various constituent units of the country

🔑

Big idea

  • Federalism is a system of government in which power is divided between a central authority and various constituent units of the country
  • It has two or more levels of government, each with its own jurisdiction, whose existence and authority are guaranteed by the constitution, which…
  • Courts act as umpires in disputes
  • India has a three-tier structure: Union, States and local governments
Read the full explanation

Federalism is a system of government in which power is divided between a central authority and various constituent units of the country. It has two or more levels of government, each with its own jurisdiction, whose existence and authority are guaranteed by the constitution, which cannot be unilaterally changed by one level. Courts act as umpires in disputes. India has a three-tier structure: Union, States and local governments. The Constitution has a Union List (97 subjects), State List (66) and Concurrent List (47). Federalism is practised by coming together (USA, Switzerland, Australia) or holding together (India, Spain, Belgium). Linguistic states, language policy, centre-state relations and decentralisation through the 73rd and 74th Amendments (1992) strengthen Indian federalism.

📌

Features of federalism

  • There are two or more levels of government
  • Different tiers govern the same citizens but have their own jurisdiction in specific matters of legislation, taxation and administration
  • The jurisdictions of the respective levels are specified in the constitution, so their existence and authority are constitutionally guaranteed
  • Fundamental provisions of the constitution cannot be unilaterally changed by one level of government
Read the full explanation

There are two or more levels of government. Different tiers govern the same citizens but have their own jurisdiction in specific matters of legislation, taxation and administration. The jurisdictions of the respective levels are specified in the constitution, so their existence and authority are constitutionally guaranteed. Fundamental provisions of the constitution cannot be unilaterally changed by one level of government; such changes require the consent of both. Courts have the power to interpret the constitution and the powers of different levels. Sources of revenue for each level are clearly specified. The dual objectives are to safeguard and promote unity of the country while accommodating regional diversity.

🧠

Coming together and holding together

  • In coming together federations, independent states come together on their own to form a bigger unit to pool their sovereignty and retain identity…
  • All states usually have equal power
  • In holding together federations, a large country decides to divide its power between the national government and states, e.g. India, Spain and Belgium
  • The central government is usually more powerful and different constituent units may have unequal powers, as in India where some states have special…
Read the full explanation

In coming together federations, independent states come together on their own to form a bigger unit to pool their sovereignty and retain identity, e.g. USA, Switzerland and Australia; all states usually have equal power. In holding together federations, a large country decides to divide its power between the national government and states, e.g. India, Spain and Belgium; the central government is usually more powerful and different constituent units may have unequal powers, as in India where some states have special status.

🚀

Division of powers in India

  • The Union List includes subjects of national importance such as defence, foreign affairs, banking, communications and currency, on which only the…
  • The State List includes police, trade, commerce, agriculture and irrigation, on which states legislate
  • The Concurrent List includes education, forests, trade unions, marriage, adoption and succession, where both can legislate, and if there is a…
  • Residuary subjects, those not in any list such as computer software, are with the Union
Read the full explanation

The Union List includes subjects of national importance such as defence, foreign affairs, banking, communications and currency, on which only the Union can legislate. The State List includes police, trade, commerce, agriculture and irrigation, on which states legislate. The Concurrent List includes education, forests, trade unions, marriage, adoption and succession, where both can legislate, and if there is a conflict the Union law prevails. Residuary subjects, those not in any list such as computer software, are with the Union. Not all states have identical powers: Jammu and Kashmir had special status under Article 370 till 2019, and Union Territories such as Chandigarh are administered by the Centre.

🔬

How federalism is practised

  • Linguistic states: from 1950 several old states were reorganised on linguistic lines, the State Reorganisation Commission (1956) producing 14 states…
  • Language policy: Hindi is the official language but spoken by only about 40 per cent
  • There are 22 scheduled languages and English is also used
  • No language was declared national
Read the full explanation

Linguistic states: from 1950 several old states were reorganised on linguistic lines, the State Reorganisation Commission (1956) producing 14 states and 6 Union Territories. Language policy: Hindi is the official language but spoken by only about 40 per cent; there are 22 scheduled languages and English is also used; no language was declared national. Centre-state relations: after 1990, regional parties and coalition governments strengthened federalism and Article 356 was used less after the S. R. Bommai case (1994). Decentralisation: the 73rd and 74th Amendments (1992) made local governments third tier; elections are regular, reservation of at least one third for women, and State Election Commissions conduct elections; Gram Sabha is the foundation.

lessons.title: Gender, Religion and Caste
yt: class 10 political science gender religion caste

blocks.x: Social differences of gender, religion and caste affect Indian politics. Gender: the sexual division of labour keeps women in the private sphere; women's movements demanded the vote and equal pay; women's representation in Lok Sabha is below 15 per cent. Reserved seats for women exist only in local bodies (one third). Religion: communalism treats religion as the basis of the nation and politics; secular India has no state religion. Caste: caste inequalities persist but caste politics also helped dalits and OBCs gain voice; elections are not decided only by caste. Politics should not be divided on these lines, but a healthy democracy can use social differences to bring about equality.
Deep dive: Gender and politics

Public/private division: women do most of the housework but it is unpaid and unrecognised. Women's movements in many countries demanded the right to vote and equality in education and careers. Sex ratio in India fell to 940 (1,000 men) in 2011 census; literacy of women is 54 per cent vs 76 per cent for men in 2011; the average woman earns less for equal work. Violence against women is widespread. In India, women are only 14.4 per cent of members in the Lok Sabha and less than 5 per cent in state assemblies. In Scandinavian countries like Sweden, Norway and Finland the participation of women in public life is very high. A bill for one third reservation in the Lok Sabha and assemblies was pending for years and was passed in 2023 as the Women's Reservation Act.
Deep dive: Religion and politics

Gandhi said that religion can never be separated from politics, meaning ethical values drawn from religion should guide politics. Communalism means using religion in politics: one religion's followers constitute one community, interests are the same, and different religious communities cannot live as equal citizens. Forms include everyday beliefs and stereotypes, seeking majority dominance, political mobilisation on religious lines, and at the extreme violence, riots and massacre such as Partition in 1947. A secular state does not have an official religion, grants freedom to practise any faith, prohibits discrimination on religion, and permits the state to intervene to ensure equality within communities, e.g. banning untouchability.
Deep dive: Caste and politics

Caste inequalities persist: earlier, castes were hierarchically ordered with occupations fixed, and the upper castes were ahead in literacy and income. Social and religious reformers like Jyotiba Phule, Gandhiji, B. R. Ambedkar and Periyar Ramaswami Naicker worked to establish a society free of caste. Economic development, urbanisation, literacy, occupational mobility and the weakening of landlords have reduced the hold of caste. Caste in politics: parties choose candidates and make appeals keeping caste in mind, and universal adult franchise gave a voice to dalits and backward classes. But no parliamentary constituency has a clear majority of one caste, and no party wins all the votes of a community, so caste does not decide everything. Caste politics can also lead to tension and violence and may divert attention from issues like development and poverty.
Deep dive: Why differences matter

Social differences take different political forms. When overlapping social differences are cumulative, as with black and poor in the US, conflict is likelier; when cross-cutting, as in Northern Ireland where religion and class differ across groups, conflict is easier to handle. The politics of social divisions depends on how people perceive their identities, how political leaders raise the demands, and how the government responds. Democracy works best when demands are within the constitutional framework and do not threaten national unity.

Gender, dharm aur jati ko rajniti mein shamil karna loktantra ko gehra bana sakta hai par samprdayikta khatarnak hai. Lok Sabha mein mahilayen sirf 14.4%. Bharat dharmnirpeksh hai. Jati ke aadhar par sabhi chunav nahi jeete jaate.

problems.q: What is communalism? Mention any two ways in which it appears.
problems.a: Communalism is using religion as the basis of politics, believing that followers of one religion form one community with common interests. Forms: everyday stereotypes and majority dominance beliefs, political mobilisation along religious lines, violence and riots.

problems.q: Explain how caste influences politics in India. Is it the only factor?
problems.a: Parties choose candidates by caste and appeal to caste sentiment; leaders mobilise caste groups and universal franchise gave voice to dalits and OBCs. But it is not the only factor: no constituency has a majority of one caste, voters consider performance, voters of a caste vote for different parties and many candidates lose despite caste appeal.

problems.q: Discuss the status of women in India and what measures have been taken to improve their political participation.
problems.a: Women face the sexual division of labour, lower literacy and wages, a falling sex ratio and violence. Their share in legislatures is low. One third seats are reserved in panchayats and municipalities since 1992 and the Women's Reservation Act 2023 reserves one third in Lok Sabha and assemblies. Further needs are enforcement of equal wages, education and safety.

Visual lesson

Gender, Religion and Caste

Social differences of gender, religion and caste affect Indian politics

🔑

Big idea

  • Social differences of gender, religion and caste affect Indian politics
  • Gender: the sexual division of labour keeps women in the private sphere
  • Women's movements demanded the vote and equal pay
  • Women's representation in Lok Sabha is below 15 per cent
Read the full explanation

Social differences of gender, religion and caste affect Indian politics. Gender: the sexual division of labour keeps women in the private sphere; women's movements demanded the vote and equal pay; women's representation in Lok Sabha is below 15 per cent. Reserved seats for women exist only in local bodies (one third). Religion: communalism treats religion as the basis of the nation and politics; secular India has no state religion. Caste: caste inequalities persist but caste politics also helped dalits and OBCs gain voice; elections are not decided only by caste. Politics should not be divided on these lines, but a healthy democracy can use social differences to bring about equality.

🏛️

Gender and politics

  • Public/private division: women do most of the housework but it is unpaid and unrecognised
  • Women's movements in many countries demanded the right to vote and equality in education and careers
  • Sex ratio in India fell to 940 (1,000 men) in 2011 census
  • Literacy of women is 54 per cent vs 76 per cent for men in 2011
Read the full explanation

Public/private division: women do most of the housework but it is unpaid and unrecognised. Women's movements in many countries demanded the right to vote and equality in education and careers. Sex ratio in India fell to 940 (1,000 men) in 2011 census; literacy of women is 54 per cent vs 76 per cent for men in 2011; the average woman earns less for equal work. Violence against women is widespread. In India, women are only 14.4 per cent of members in the Lok Sabha and less than 5 per cent in state assemblies. In Scandinavian countries like Sweden, Norway and Finland the participation of women in public life is very high. A bill for one third reservation in the Lok Sabha and assemblies was pending for years and was passed in 2023 as the Women's Reservation Act.

🏛️

Religion and politics

  • Gandhi said that religion can never be separated from politics, meaning ethical values drawn from religion should guide politics
  • Communalism means using religion in politics: one religion's followers constitute one community, interests are the same, and different religious…
  • Forms include everyday beliefs and stereotypes, seeking majority dominance, political mobilisation on religious lines, and at the extreme violence…
  • A secular state does not have an official religion, grants freedom to practise any faith, prohibits discrimination on religion, and permits the state…
Read the full explanation

Gandhi said that religion can never be separated from politics, meaning ethical values drawn from religion should guide politics. Communalism means using religion in politics: one religion's followers constitute one community, interests are the same, and different religious communities cannot live as equal citizens. Forms include everyday beliefs and stereotypes, seeking majority dominance, political mobilisation on religious lines, and at the extreme violence, riots and massacre such as Partition in 1947. A secular state does not have an official religion, grants freedom to practise any faith, prohibits discrimination on religion, and permits the state to intervene to ensure equality within communities, e.g. banning untouchability.

🏛️

Caste and politics

  • Caste inequalities persist: earlier, castes were hierarchically ordered with occupations fixed, and the upper castes were ahead in literacy and income
  • Social and religious reformers like Jyotiba Phule, Gandhiji, B
  • Ambedkar and Periyar Ramaswami Naicker worked to establish a society free of caste
  • Economic development, urbanisation, literacy, occupational mobility and the weakening of landlords have reduced the hold of caste
Read the full explanation

Caste inequalities persist: earlier, castes were hierarchically ordered with occupations fixed, and the upper castes were ahead in literacy and income. Social and religious reformers like Jyotiba Phule, Gandhiji, B. R. Ambedkar and Periyar Ramaswami Naicker worked to establish a society free of caste. Economic development, urbanisation, literacy, occupational mobility and the weakening of landlords have reduced the hold of caste. Caste in politics: parties choose candidates and make appeals keeping caste in mind, and universal adult franchise gave a voice to dalits and backward classes. But no parliamentary constituency has a clear majority of one caste, and no party wins all the votes of a community, so caste does not decide everything. Caste politics can also lead to tension and violence and may divert attention from issues like development and poverty.

🔬

Why differences matter

  • Social differences take different political forms
  • When overlapping social differences are cumulative, as with black and poor in the US, conflict is likelier
  • When cross-cutting, as in Northern Ireland where religion and class differ across groups, conflict is easier to handle
  • The politics of social divisions depends on how people perceive their identities, how political leaders raise the demands, and how the government…
Read the full explanation

Social differences take different political forms. When overlapping social differences are cumulative, as with black and poor in the US, conflict is likelier; when cross-cutting, as in Northern Ireland where religion and class differ across groups, conflict is easier to handle. The politics of social divisions depends on how people perceive their identities, how political leaders raise the demands, and how the government responds. Democracy works best when demands are within the constitutional framework and do not threaten national unity.

lessons.title: Political Parties
yt: class 10 political science political parties

blocks.x: A political party is a group of people who come together to contest elections and hold power in the government. Parties have three components: the leaders, the active members and the followers. Their functions are contesting elections, putting forward policies and programmes, making laws, forming and running governments, playing the role of opposition, shaping public opinion and providing access to government machinery. Party systems can be one-party, two-party or multi-party; India has a multi-party system with national and state parties recognised by the Election Commission. Challenges: lack of internal democracy, dynastic succession, money and muscle power, and meaningful choice. Remedies: anti-defection law (2003 amendment), affidavits, mandatory organisational elections and state funding of elections.
Deep dive: Functions of parties

Parties contest elections, in most democracies election is fought mainly among candidates put up by political parties. They put forward policies and programmes, and voters choose from them. Parties play a decisive role in making laws; though legislators decide, they are bound by the party line. Parties form and run governments. Parties not in power play the role of opposition, criticising the government for failures and wrong policies. Parties shape public opinion by raising and highlighting issues, and have lakhs of members and activists. Parties provide people access to government machinery and welfare schemes.
Deep dive: Necessity of parties

Without parties, every candidate in the elections would be independent, so no one would be responsible for how the country is run and no promises about major policies could be made. Parties are a political institution that gets people together to agree on some policies and programmes for the society, and is therefore necessary for representative democracy in large, complex societies.
Deep dive: Party systems and national parties

Where one party is allowed to control and run the government, it is a one-party system, e.g. China. In some countries power usually changes between two main parties, a two-party system, e.g. the USA and the UK. If several parties compete for power and more than two have a reasonable chance, it is a multi-party system; when a number of parties form an alliance it is called a coalition (e.g. NDA, UPA). India has a multiparty system. A party that secures at least six per cent of the total votes in Lok Sabha or assembly elections in four states and wins at least four seats in Lok Sabha is recognised as a national party. A state party must secure at least six per cent of votes in the state assembly and win at least two seats. Examples of national parties include INC (1885), BJP (1980), BSP (1984), CPI(M) (1964), AAP, and others.
Deep dive: Challenges and reforms

Challenges: lack of internal democracy (power concentrated in a few leaders, no organisational elections), dynastic succession, growing role of money and muscle power, and not offering a meaningful choice to voters as the parties are similar. Reforms: the Constitution was amended to prevent elected legislators from changing parties (anti-defection law, 91st Amendment 2003 to limit the size of ministries and tighten defection rules); the Supreme Court ordered all candidates to file affidavits on property and criminal cases; the Election Commission made it mandatory for parties to hold organisational elections and file income tax returns. Suggestions: law to regulate internal affairs, quota for women (one third), state funding of elections, and public pressure.

Why are political parties necessary in a democracy?
qa.a: They organise candidates, bring consensus on policies and make governments accountable; without them, all candidates would be independent and no one responsible.

qa.q: How does a coalition differ from a single party government?
qa.a: A coalition has several parties sharing power, so decisions require compromise.

qa.q: What is the role of an opposition party?
qa.a: It criticises the government, exposes failures, offers alternatives and mobilises opinion.

qa.q: How does the Election Commission recognise parties?
qa.a: By rules on vote share and seats; it also allots symbols to national and state parties.

qa.q: What are the benefits of a multi-party system for India?
qa.a: It gives representation to diverse interests, though it can cause unstable coalitions.

qa.q: Why is a two-party system limited?
qa.a: It gives voters only two choices and may ignore minority viewpoints.

qa.q: Why is a one-party system undemocratic?
qa.a: It gives no choice to voters and no legal opposition.

qa.q: What is meant by lack of internal democracy?
qa.a: The party has no regular elections or open decision-making; decisions are taken by a few leaders.

qa.q: Why is dynastic succession a problem?
qa.a: Leaders favour family members instead of capable workers, which weakens fairness within parties.

qa.q: How does money power harm elections?
qa.a: Rich candidates and parties get an unfair advantage and depend on donors, so common voters get less choice.

qa.q: What did the Supreme Court order about candidates?
qa.a: They must file affidavits declaring property and pending criminal cases.

qa.q: How did the anti-defection law help?
qa.a: It disqualifies legislators who change party and so brings stability.

qa.q: What can citizens do to reform parties?
qa.a: Pressure through petitions, protests, media, voting wisely and joining parties.

qa.q: What is the role of parties in making laws?
qa.a: Legislators vote according to party line so laws are made by party majorities.

qa.q: What is a party symbol used for?
qa.a: To help illiterate voters recognise a party on the voting machine.

qa.q: What does the term programme mean for a party?
qa.a: The promises it makes in its manifesto that guide governance.

🔑

Big idea

  • A political party is a group of people who come together to contest elections and hold power in the government
  • Parties have three components: the leaders, the active members and the followers
  • Their functions are contesting elections, putting forward policies and programmes, making laws, forming and running governments, playing the role of…
  • Party systems can be one-party, two-party or multi-party
Read the full explanation

A political party is a group of people who come together to contest elections and hold power in the government. Parties have three components: the leaders, the active members and the followers. Their functions are contesting elections, putting forward policies and programmes, making laws, forming and running governments, playing the role of opposition, shaping public opinion and providing access to government machinery. Party systems can be one-party, two-party or multi-party; India has a multi-party system with national and state parties recognised by the Election Commission. Challenges: lack of internal democracy, dynastic succession, money and muscle power, and meaningful choice. Remedies: anti-defection law (2003 amendment), affidavits, mandatory organisational elections and state funding of elections.

📌

Functions of parties

  • Parties contest elections, in most democracies election is fought mainly among candidates put up by political parties
  • They put forward policies and programmes, and voters choose from them
  • Parties play a decisive role in making laws
  • Though legislators decide, they are bound by the party line
Read the full explanation

Parties contest elections, in most democracies election is fought mainly among candidates put up by political parties. They put forward policies and programmes, and voters choose from them. Parties play a decisive role in making laws; though legislators decide, they are bound by the party line. Parties form and run governments. Parties not in power play the role of opposition, criticising the government for failures and wrong policies. Parties shape public opinion by raising and highlighting issues, and have lakhs of members and activists. Parties provide people access to government machinery and welfare schemes.

🧠

Necessity of parties

  • Without parties, every candidate in the elections would be independent, so no one would be responsible for how the country is run and no promises…
  • Parties are a political institution that gets people together to agree on some policies and programmes for the society, and is therefore necessary…
Read the full explanation

Without parties, every candidate in the elections would be independent, so no one would be responsible for how the country is run and no promises about major policies could be made. Parties are a political institution that gets people together to agree on some policies and programmes for the society, and is therefore necessary for representative democracy in large, complex societies.

🌟

Party systems and national parties

  • Where one party is allowed to control and run the government, it is a one-party system, e.g. China
  • In some countries power usually changes between two main parties, a two-party system, e.g. the USA and the UK
  • If several parties compete for power and more than two have a reasonable chance, it is a multi-party system
  • When a number of parties form an alliance it is called a coalition (e.g. NDA, UPA)
Read the full explanation

Where one party is allowed to control and run the government, it is a one-party system, e.g. China. In some countries power usually changes between two main parties, a two-party system, e.g. the USA and the UK. If several parties compete for power and more than two have a reasonable chance, it is a multi-party system; when a number of parties form an alliance it is called a coalition (e.g. NDA, UPA). India has a multiparty system. A party that secures at least six per cent of the total votes in Lok Sabha or assembly elections in four states and wins at least four seats in Lok Sabha is recognised as a national party. A state party must secure at least six per cent of votes in the state assembly and win at least two seats. Examples of national parties include INC (1885), BJP (1980), BSP (1984), CPI(M) (1964), AAP, and others.

🔬

Challenges and reforms

  • Challenges: lack of internal democracy (power concentrated in a few leaders, no organisational elections), dynastic succession, growing role of money…
  • Reforms: the Constitution was amended to prevent elected legislators from changing parties (anti-defection law, 91st Amendment 2003 to limit the size…
  • The Supreme Court ordered all candidates to file affidavits on property and criminal cases
  • The Election Commission made it mandatory for parties to hold organisational elections and file income tax returns
Read the full explanation

Challenges: lack of internal democracy (power concentrated in a few leaders, no organisational elections), dynastic succession, growing role of money and muscle power, and not offering a meaningful choice to voters as the parties are similar. Reforms: the Constitution was amended to prevent elected legislators from changing parties (anti-defection law, 91st Amendment 2003 to limit the size of ministries and tighten defection rules); the Supreme Court ordered all candidates to file affidavits on property and criminal cases; the Election Commission made it mandatory for parties to hold organisational elections and file income tax returns. Suggestions: law to regulate internal affairs, quota for women (one third), state funding of elections, and public pressure.

lessons.title: Outcomes of Democracy
yt: class 10 political science outcomes of democracy

blocks.x: How do we assess democracy's outcomes? Democracy is better than other forms of government because it promotes equality among citizens, enhances the dignity of the individual, improves the quality of decision making, provides a method to resolve conflicts, and allows room to correct mistakes. A democratic government is accountable, responsive and legitimate. Democracy produces a government that follows procedures and is accountable to the people, but it does not guarantee faster economic growth; it does reduce inequality in some respects, though economic inequality persists. Democracy accommodates social diversity and is legitimate because it is people's own. Challenges remain in poverty, inequality, and need for more participation.
Deep dive: Accountable, responsive and legitimate government

Democracy is based on the idea of deliberation and negotiation, so decisions are slower but follow norms and procedures. Citizens have the right to know whether decisions followed procedure, and to see the working of the government (right to information, 2005). A democratic government is accountable to the citizens and responsive to the needs and expectations of citizens. Elections allow citizens to throw out leaders. Even if democracy does not always give the best decisions, it is a legitimate government: it may be slow and inefficient but it is people's own government, which is why there is a continuing support for it all over the world.
Deep dive: Economic growth and inequality

Between 1950 and 2000, dictatorships had slightly higher economic growth rates (4.42 per cent) than democracies (3.95 per cent); but the difference between rich and poor democracies is large, as is the difference among dictatorships. So democracy is not guaranteed to deliver growth; the economic performance depends on population growth, global situation, cooperation from other countries and the economic priorities adopted. Democracies are not necessarily better at reducing economic disparities: in South Africa, the white minority holds most wealth even though democracy arrived in 1994; in India the top 20 per cent holds a larger share of the national income than the bottom 20 per cent, and poverty persists, with the poor contributing a large share of votes in India. Some democratic countries including Brazil show sharp inequalities.
Deep dive: Social diversity and dignity

Democracies usually develop a procedure to conduct their competition, which reduces the possibility of tension becoming explosive or violent. Belgium and Sri Lanka examples show success where the majority listens to the minority; Yugoslavia, which broke up violently, shows the danger of a lack of accommodation. Democracy stands much superior to any other form of government in promoting dignity and freedom of the individual, as all citizens are equal. The achievement is the recognition of the principle of equality, though in practice caste and gender discrimination persist; Dalits and women have fought for a dignified place.
Deep dive: Expectations from democracy

Democracy is a better form because it improves the quality of decisions through consultation and discussion, provides a method to deal with differences and conflicts, and enhances dignity. It allows room to correct mistakes because the rulers can be changed. Democracy is better judged by its outcomes in comparison with other systems, and by citizens' own expectations. The people want democracies to produce better outcomes, so complaints are a sign of the success of democracy: it has taught citizens to question and not be satisfied. Democracy is a continuing project.

problems.q: Why is democracy considered a legitimate form of government?
problems.a: Because it is people's own government, based on their consent and elections; even if it is slow and imperfect, people feel it is theirs and support it.

problems.q: Does democracy lead to economic development? Discuss with evidence.
problems.a: Dictatorships had slightly higher growth (4.42 per cent) than democracies (3.95 per cent) in 1950-2000, but poor democracies and poor dictatorships differ greatly. Growth depends on population growth, global conditions, priorities, so democracy does not guarantee growth.

problems.q: How far does democracy reduce inequality and promote dignity? Support your answer.
problems.a: Democracy does not eliminate economic inequality: top 20 per cent income share is far higher than the bottom 20 per cent in India; South Africa has white minority wealth. But it recognises equality and dignity through equal vote, laws against discrimination and movements by dalits and women. Complaints show citizens have learned to question.

lessons.html:
Visual lesson

Outcomes of Democracy

How do we assess democracy's outcomes?

minutes
formulas
Q&A
quiz
Flat concept map (2D)
1Big idea›2Accountable, responsive and…›3Economic growth and…›4Social diversity and dignity›5Expectations from democracy
RTI Act2005
Growth dictatorships4.42%
Growth democracies3.95%
South Africa democracy1994
🔑

Big idea

  • How do we assess democracy's outcomes?
  • Democracy is better than other forms of government because it promotes equality among citizens, enhances the dignity of the individual, improves the…
  • A democratic government is accountable, responsive and legitimate
  • Democracy produces a government that follows procedures and is accountable to the people, but it does not guarantee faster economic growth
Read the full explanation

How do we assess democracy's outcomes? Democracy is better than other forms of government because it promotes equality among citizens, enhances the dignity of the individual, improves the quality of decision making, provides a method to resolve conflicts, and allows room to correct mistakes. A democratic government is accountable, responsive and legitimate. Democracy produces a government that follows procedures and is accountable to the people, but it does not guarantee faster economic growth; it does reduce inequality in some respects, though economic inequality persists. Democracy accommodates social diversity and is legitimate because it is people's own. Challenges remain in poverty, inequality, and need for more participation.

🏛️

Accountable, responsive and legitimate government

  • Democracy is based on the idea of deliberation and negotiation, so decisions are slower but follow norms and procedures
  • Citizens have the right to know whether decisions followed procedure, and to see the working of the government (right to information, 2005)
  • A democratic government is accountable to the citizens and responsive to the needs and expectations of citizens
  • Elections allow citizens to throw out leaders
Read the full explanation

Democracy is based on the idea of deliberation and negotiation, so decisions are slower but follow norms and procedures. Citizens have the right to know whether decisions followed procedure, and to see the working of the government (right to information, 2005). A democratic government is accountable to the citizens and responsive to the needs and expectations of citizens. Elections allow citizens to throw out leaders. Even if democracy does not always give the best decisions, it is a legitimate government: it may be slow and inefficient but it is people's own government, which is why there is a continuing support for it all over the world.

🏛️

Economic growth and inequality

  • Between 1950 and 2000, dictatorships had slightly higher economic growth rates (4.42 per cent) than democracies (3.95 per cent)
  • But the difference between rich and poor democracies is large, as is the difference among dictatorships
  • So democracy is not guaranteed to deliver growth
  • The economic performance depends on population growth, global situation, cooperation from other countries and the economic priorities adopted
Read the full explanation

Between 1950 and 2000, dictatorships had slightly higher economic growth rates (4.42 per cent) than democracies (3.95 per cent); but the difference between rich and poor democracies is large, as is the difference among dictatorships. So democracy is not guaranteed to deliver growth; the economic performance depends on population growth, global situation, cooperation from other countries and the economic priorities adopted. Democracies are not necessarily better at reducing economic disparities: in South Africa, the white minority holds most wealth even though democracy arrived in 1994; in India the top 20 per cent holds a larger share of the national income than the bottom 20 per cent, and poverty persists, with the poor contributing a large share of votes in India. Some democratic countries including Brazil show sharp inequalities.

🌟

Social diversity and dignity

  • Democracies usually develop a procedure to conduct their competition, which reduces the possibility of tension becoming explosive or violent
  • Belgium and Sri Lanka examples show success where the majority listens to the minority
  • Yugoslavia, which broke up violently, shows the danger of a lack of accommodation
  • Democracy stands much superior to any other form of government in promoting dignity and freedom of the individual, as all citizens are equal
Read the full explanation

Democracies usually develop a procedure to conduct their competition, which reduces the possibility of tension becoming explosive or violent. Belgium and Sri Lanka examples show success where the majority listens to the minority; Yugoslavia, which broke up violently, shows the danger of a lack of accommodation. Democracy stands much superior to any other form of government in promoting dignity and freedom of the individual, as all citizens are equal. The achievement is the recognition of the principle of equality, though in practice caste and gender discrimination persist; Dalits and women have fought for a dignified place.

🏛️

Expectations from democracy

  • Democracy is a better form because it improves the quality of decisions through consultation and discussion, provides a method to deal with…
  • It allows room to correct mistakes because the rulers can be changed
  • Democracy is better judged by its outcomes in comparison with other systems, and by citizens' own expectations
  • The people want democracies to produce better outcomes, so complaints are a sign of the success of democracy: it has taught citizens to question and…
Read the full explanation

Democracy is a better form because it improves the quality of decisions through consultation and discussion, provides a method to deal with differences and conflicts, and enhances dignity. It allows room to correct mistakes because the rulers can be changed. Democracy is better judged by its outcomes in comparison with other systems, and by citizens' own expectations. The people want democracies to produce better outcomes, so complaints are a sign of the success of democracy: it has taught citizens to question and not be satisfied. Democracy is a continuing project.

blocks.x: सन्धिः नाम वर्णयोः मेलनम्। सन्धिः त्रिविधः अस्ति: स्वरसन्धिः, व्यञ्जनसन्धिः, विसर्गसन्धिः। स्वरसन्धौ दीर्घः (अ/आ+अ/आ=आ), गुणः (अ/आ+इ/ई=ए, उ/ऊ=ओ, ऋ=अर्), वृद्धिः (अ/आ+ए/ऐ=ऐ, ओ/औ=औ), यण् (इ/ई+असमान स्वर = य्, उ/ऊ=व्, ऋ=र्), अयादिः (ए=अय्, ऐ=आय्, ओ=अव्, औ=आव्), पूर्वरूपम्, पररूपम्। व्यञ्जनसन्धौ श्चुत्वम्, ष्टुत्वम्, जश्त्वम्, अनुस्वारः, परसवर्णः, म् का अनुस्वारः। विसर्गसन्धौ उत्वम्, रुत्वम्, सत्वम्, शत्वम्, ओत्वम्, लोपः।
Deep dive: स्वरसन्धिः

दीर्घसन्धिः: विद्या + आलयः = विद्यालयः। गुणसन्धिः: महा + ईशः = महेशः, सूर्य + उदयः = सूर्योदयः, देव + ऋषिः = देवर्षिः। वृद्धिसन्धिः: एक + एकम् = एकैकम्, सदा + एव = सदैव, महा + ओघः = महौघः। यण्सन्धिः: इति + आदि = इत्यादि, सु + आगतम् = स्वागतम्, पितृ + आज्ञा = पित्राज्ञा। अयादिसन्धिः: ने + अनम् = नयनम्, नौ + इकः = नाविकः, पो + अनः = पवनः, पौ + अकः = पावकः।
Deep dive: व्यञ्जनसन्धिः

जश्त्वसन्धिः: वाक् + ईशः = वागीशः, दिक् + गजः = दिग्गजः, षट् + आननः = षडाननः। अनुस्वारः: म् + व्यञ्जनम् = अनुस्वारः, यथा – सम् + सारः = संसारः। श्चुत्वम्: सत् + चरित्रम् = सच्चरित्रम्। ष्टुत्वम्: तत् + टीका = तट्टीका। परसवर्णः: जगत् + नाथः = जगन्नाथः। तुगागमः: छ से पूर्व: वृक्ष + छाया = वृक्षच्छाया।
Deep dive: विसर्गसन्धिः

उत्वम्: शिवः + वन्दे = शिवो वन्दे (अः + अ = ओ ऽ)। रुत्वम्: पुनः + अपि = पुनरपि। सत्वम्: नमः + ते = नमस्ते। शत्वम्: निः + चलः = निश्चलः। ओत्वम्: मनः + हरः = मनोहरः। विसर्गलोपः: देवः + एति = देव एति। रेफ: निः + रोगः = नीरोगः (र् का लोप और दीर्घ)।
Deep dive: अभ्यासविधिः
सन्धि विच्छेद करते समय पहले दोनों शब्दों के अन्त और आदि वर्ण देखें, फिर नियम की पहचान करें। संयोग में बने वर्ण से पहले वर्ण का मूल रूप पहचानें।
Hindi saransh
दो वर्णों के मेल को संधि कहते हैं। स्वर संधि में दीर्घ, गुण, वृद्धि, यण्, अयादि आदि आते हैं। विसर्ग संधि में नमः+ते=नमस्ते, पुनः+अपि=पुनरपि जैसे उदाहरण याद रखें।
सूत्र: अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः, आद्गुणः, वृद्धिरेचि, इको यणचि, एचोऽयवायावः।

problems.a: दीर्घ में सवर्ण स्वर मिलकर दीर्घ बनते हैं (विद्यालयः, रवीन्द्रः, गिरीशः)। गुण में अ/आ के बाद इ/उ/ऋ आने पर ए/ओ/अर् होता है (महेशः, सूर्योदयः, देवर्षिः)। वृद्धि में अ/आ के बाद ए/ऐ/ओ/औ आने पर ऐ/औ होता है (सदैव, एकैकम्, महौषधिः)।

सन्धिः नाम वर्णयोः मेलनम्। सन्धिः त्रिविधः अस्ति: स्वरसन्धिः, व्यञ्जनसन्धिः, विसर्गसन्धिः। स्वरसन्धौ दीर्घः (अ/आ+अ/आ=आ), गुणः (अ/आ+इ/ई=ए, उ/ऊ=ओ, ऋ=अर्), वृद्धिः (अ/आ+ए/ऐ=ऐ, ओ/औ=औ), यण् (इ/ई+असमान स्वर = य्, उ/ऊ=व्, ऋ=र्), अयादिः (ए=अय्, ऐ=आय्, ओ=अव्, औ=आव्), पूर्वरूपम्, पररूपम्। व्यञ्जनसन्धौ श्चुत्वम्, ष्टुत्वम्, जश्त्वम्, अनुस्वारः, परसवर्णः, म् का अनुस्वारः। विसर्गसन्धौ उत्वम्, रुत्वम्, सत्वम्, शत्वम्, ओत्वम्, लोपः।

📌

स्वरसन्धिः

  • दीर्घसन्धिः: विद्या + आलयः = विद्यालयः। गुणसन्धिः: महा + ईशः = महेशः, सूर्य + उदयः = सूर्योदयः, देव + ऋषिः = देवर्षिः। वृद्धिसन्धिः: एक + एकम् =…
🧠

व्यञ्जनसन्धिः

  • जश्त्वसन्धिः: वाक् + ईशः = वागीशः, दिक् + गजः = दिग्गजः, षट् + आननः = षडाननः। अनुस्वारः: म् + व्यञ्जनम् = अनुस्वारः, यथा – सम् + सारः = संसारः।…
🌟

विसर्गसन्धिः

  • उत्वम्: शिवः + वन्दे = शिवो वन्दे (अः + अ = ओ ऽ)। रुत्वम्: पुनः + अपि = पुनरपि। सत्वम्: नमः + ते = नमस्ते। शत्वम्: निः + चलः = निश्चलः। ओत्वम्: मनः +…
🔬

अभ्यासविधिः

  • सन्धि विच्छेद करते समय पहले दोनों शब्दों के अन्त और आदि वर्ण देखें, फिर नियम की पहचान करें। संयोग में बने वर्ण से पहले वर्ण का मूल रूप पहचानें।
🧮

Formula tiles

दीर्घःअ/आ+अ/आ=आविद्या+आलयः=विद्यालयः
गुणःअ/आ+इ=एमहा+ईशः=महेशः
वृद्धिःअ/आ+ए=ऐसदा+एव=सदैव
यण्इ+अ=यइति+आदि=इत्यादि
अयादिःए=अय्ने+अनम्=नयनम्
जश्त्वम्क्=ग्वाक्+ईशः=वागीशः
विसर्गःनमः+तेनमस्ते
🎯 Remember सूत्र: अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः, आद्गुणः, वृद्धिरेचि, इको यणचि, एचोऽयवायावः।
🇮🇳

हिंदी सार

दो वर्णों के मेल को संधि कहते हैं। स्वर संधि में दीर्घ, गुण, वृद्धि, यण्, अयादि आदि आते हैं। विसर्ग संधि में नमः+ते=नमस्ते, पुनः+अपि=पुनरपि जैसे उदाहरण याद रखें।

blocks.x: समासः नाम अनेकपदानाम् एकपदीभवनम्। समासस्य प्रमुखाः भेदाः: अव्ययीभावः, तत्पुरुषः, कर्मधारयः, द्विगुः, द्वन्द्वः, बहुव्रीहिः। विग्रहवाक्येन अर्थः ज्ञायते। तत्पुरुषे उत्तरपदम् प्रधानम्; अव्ययीभावे पूर्वपदम् अव्ययम्; कर्मधारये विशेषणविशेष्यभावः; द्विगौ पूर्वपदं संख्यावाचकम्; द्वन्द्वे उभयपदप्रधानम्; बहुव्रीहौ अन्यपदार्थप्रधानम्।
Deep dive: भेदपरिचयः

तत्पुरुषः (राजपुरुषः = राज्ञः पुरुषः) – उत्तरपद की प्रधानता। कर्मधारयः (नीलकमलम्) – विशेषण + विशेष्य। द्विगुः (त्रिलोकी) – संख्या + संज्ञा। द्वन्द्वः (रामलक्ष्मणौ) – दोनों प्रधान, च से जुड़े। बहुव्रीहिः (पीताम्बरः) – किसी अन्य का बोध। अव्ययीभावः (यथाशक्ति) – पहला पद अव्यय।
Deep dive: विग्रहपद्धतिः
विग्रह करते समय पहले समस्तपद के पदों को पहचानें, फिर विभक्ति/अर्थ के अनुसार वाक्य बनाएँ। बहुव्रीहि में अन्त में "यस्य सः" या "यस्याः सा" लगाएँ।
Deep dive: पहचान की युक्ति
यदि पद किसी अन्य के विशेषण की तरह प्रयुक्त हो तो बहुव्रीहि। यदि पूर्वपद संख्या हो तो द्विगु। यदि "च" से जुड़ सकें तो द्वन्द्व। यदि पूर्वपद अव्यय हो तो अव्ययीभाव।
Hindi saransh
अनेक पदों के एकपद होने को समास कहते हैं। तत्पुरुष में उत्तरपद प्रधान, द्वन्द्व में दोनों, बहुव्रीहि में अन्य पद तथा अव्ययीभाव में पूर्वपद प्रधान होता है।
द्विगु में संख्या; द्वन्द्व में च; बहुव्रीहि में यस्य सः।

समासः नाम अनेकपदानाम् एकपदीभवनम्। समासस्य प्रमुखाः भेदाः: अव्ययीभावः, तत्पुरुषः, कर्मधारयः, द्विगुः, द्वन्द्वः, बहुव्रीहिः। विग्रहवाक्येन अर्थः ज्ञायते। तत्पुरुषे उत्तरपदम् प्रधानम्; अव्ययीभावे पूर्वपदम् अव्ययम्; कर्मधारये विशेषणविशेष्यभावः; द्विगौ पूर्वपदं संख्यावाचकम्; द्वन्द्वे उभयपदप्रधानम्; बहुव्रीहौ अन्यपदार्थप्रधानम्।

📌

भेदपरिचयः

  • तत्पुरुषः (राजपुरुषः = राज्ञः पुरुषः) – उत्तरपद की प्रधानता। कर्मधारयः (नीलकमलम्) – विशेषण + विशेष्य। द्विगुः (त्रिलोकी) – संख्या + संज्ञा। द्वन्द्वः…
🧠

विग्रहपद्धतिः

  • विग्रह करते समय पहले समस्तपद के पदों को पहचानें, फिर विभक्ति/अर्थ के अनुसार वाक्य बनाएँ। बहुव्रीहि में अन्त में "यस्य सः" या "यस्याः सा" लगाएँ।
🌟

पहचान की युक्ति

  • यदि पद किसी अन्य के विशेषण की तरह प्रयुक्त हो तो बहुव्रीहि। यदि पूर्वपद संख्या हो तो द्विगु। यदि "च" से जुड़ सकें तो द्वन्द्व। यदि पूर्वपद अव्यय हो…
🧮

Formula tiles

अव्ययीभावःपूर्वपद अव्यययथाशक्ति
तत्पुरुषःउत्तरपद प्रधानराजपुरुषः
कर्मधारयःविशेषण-विशेष्यनीलोत्पलम्
द्विगुःसंख्या पूर्वपदत्रिलोकी
द्वन्द्वःदोनों प्रधानरामलक्ष्मणौ
बहुव्रीहिःअन्यपद प्रधानपीताम्बरः
🎯 Remember द्विगु में संख्या; द्वन्द्व में च; बहुव्रीहि में यस्य सः।
🇮🇳

हिंदी सार

अनेक पदों के एकपद होने को समास कहते हैं। तत्पुरुष में उत्तरपद प्रधान, द्वन्द्व में दोनों, बहुव्रीहि में अन्य पद तथा अव्ययीभाव में पूर्वपद प्रधान होता है।

lessons.title: प्रत्ययाः
yt: class 10 sanskrit pratyaya

blocks.x: प्रत्ययाः धातुषु शब्देषु वा संयुज्य नूतनार्थं जनयन्ति। कृत् प्रत्ययाः: क्त (भूतकालिकः कर्मवाच्य/भाववाच्य), क्तवतु (कर्तरि भूत), क्त्वा (पूर्वकालिक क्रिया), ल्यप् (उपसर्गसहित धातु से क्त्वा के स्थान पर), तुमुन् (प्रयोजनार्थक), शतृ (वर्तमान कर्तरि), शानच्, तव्यत्, अनीयर् (चाहिए अर्थ में), ण्वुल्, तृच्, ल्युट्। तद्धित प्रत्ययाः: मतुप्, तरप्, तमप्, इनि, ठक्।
Deep dive: कृत् प्रत्यय
क्त्वा – असमापिका क्रिया: सः पठित्वा गच्छति। तुमुन् – सः पठितुम् गच्छति। क्त – रामः ग्रामं गतः। क्तवतु – रामः ग्रामं गतवान्। शतृ – बालकः पठन् अस्ति।
Deep dive: ल्यप् तथा क्त्वा
जब धातु से पहले उपसर्ग हो तो क्त्वा के स्थान पर ल्यप् होता है। प्र + नम् + क्त्वा = प्रणम्य; आ + गम् = आगत्य; वि + हा = विहाय।
Deep dive: तव्यत् और अनीयर्
तव्यत् तथा अनीयर् का अर्थ है "चाहिए"। कर्तव्यम् = करना चाहिए; पठनीयम् = पढ़ने योग्य। दोनों कर्मवाच्य/भाववाच्य में।
Deep dive: तद्धित प्रत्यय
तरप् (तुलना में दो): लघुतरः; तमप् (बहुतों में श्रेष्ठ): लघुतमः; मतुप्: श्रीमान्, बुद्धिमान्, गुणवान्; इनि: धनी, गुणी; ठक्: ऐतिहासिक
Hindi saransh
प्रत्यय शब्द के अन्त में जुड़कर नया अर्थ देते हैं। क्त्वा से पूर्वकालिक, तुमुन् से प्रयोजन, शतृ से वर्तमान, क्त से भूतकाल तथा तव्यत्/अनीयर् से चाहिए का भाव आता है।
उपसर्ग हो तो क्त्वा नहीं, ल्यप् लगता है।

problems.a: बालकः पठित्वा गच्छति। सः ग्रामं गत्वा आगच्छति। रामः कार्यं कृत्वा विश्राम्यति।

problems.q: क्त्वा तथा ल्यप् में अन्तर बताइए तथा तीन उदाहरण दीजिए।
problems.a: क्त्वा उपसर्ग रहित धातु से (पठित्वा, गत्वा, कृत्वा); ल्यप् उपसर्ग सहित धातु से (प्रणम्य, आगत्य, विहाय)।

problems.q: कर्तव्यम्, पठनीयम्, गन्तुम् तथा गच्छन् का प्रत्यय और अर्थ बताइए।
problems.a: कर्तव्यम् – तव्यत्, करना चाहिए; पठनीयम् – अनीयर्, पढ़ने योग्य; गन्तुम् – तुमुन्, जाने के लिए; गच्छन् – शतृ, जाता हुआ।

  • प्रत्ययाः धातुषु शब्देषु वा संयुज्य नूतनार्थं जनयन्ति। कृत् प्रत्ययाः: क्त (भूतकालिकः कर्मवाच्य/भाववाच्य), क्तवतु (कर्तरि भूत), क्त्वा (पूर्वकालिक…
📌

कृत् प्रत्यय

  • क्त्वा – असमापिका क्रिया: सः पठित्वा गच्छति। तुमुन् – सः पठितुम् गच्छति। क्त – रामः ग्रामं गतः। क्तवतु – रामः ग्रामं गतवान्। शतृ – बालकः पठन् अस्ति।
🧠

ल्यप् तथा क्त्वा

  • जब धातु से पहले उपसर्ग हो तो क्त्वा के स्थान पर ल्यप् होता है। प्र + नम् + क्त्वा = प्रणम्य
  • आ + गम् = आगत्य
  • वि + हा = विहाय।
🌟

तव्यत् और अनीयर्

  • तव्यत् तथा अनीयर् का अर्थ है "चाहिए"। कर्तव्यम् = करना चाहिए
  • पठनीयम् = पढ़ने योग्य। दोनों कर्मवाच्य/भाववाच्य में।
🔬

तद्धित प्रत्यय

  • तरप् (तुलना में दो): लघुतरः
  • तमप् (बहुतों में श्रेष्ठ): लघुतमः
  • मतुप्: श्रीमान्, बुद्धिमान्, गुणवान्
  • इनि: धनी, गुणी

हिंदी सार

प्रत्यय शब्द के अन्त में जुड़कर नया अर्थ देते हैं। क्त्वा से पूर्वकालिक, तुमुन् से प्रयोजन, शतृ से वर्तमान, क्त से भूतकाल तथा तव्यत्/अनीयर् से चाहिए का भाव आता है।

yt: class 10 sanskrit dhatu roop lakar

blocks.x: संस्कृते क्रियापदानां रूपाणि धातुः, लकारः, पुरुषः, वचनं च अनुसृत्य भवन्ति। लकाराः दश सन्ति; कक्षा दशमीपाठ्यक्रमे लट् (वर्तमान), लृट् (भविष्य), लङ् (अनद्यतन भूत), लोट् (आज्ञा/प्रार्थना), विधिलिङ् (चाहिए/सम्भावना) च अपेक्ष्यन्ते। पुरुषः त्रयः – प्रथमः, मध्यमः, उत्तमः; वचनानि त्रीणि – एकवचनम्, द्विवचनम्, बहुवचनम्। धातवः परस्मैपदिनः आत्मनेपदिनः उभयपदिनः च।
Deep dive: लट् लकार
पठ् धातु: पठति, पठतः, पठन्ति (प्रथम); पठसि, पठथः, पठथ (मध्यम); पठामि, पठावः, पठामः (उत्तम)। अर्थ: वर्तमान काल।
Deep dive: लृट्, लङ्, लोट्, विधिलिङ्
लृट् में स्य/ष्य जुड़ता है – पठिष्यति। लङ् में अ का आगम – अपठत्। लोट् – पठतु, पठ, पठानि। विधिलिङ् – पठेत्, पठेः, पठेयम्।
Deep dive: पुरुष व्यवस्था
प्रथम पुरुष में नाम/सः, मध्यम में त्वम्/यूयम्, उत्तम में अहम्/वयम्। संस्कृत में पुरुष का क्रम हिन्दी से उलटा माना जाता है।
Deep dive: अस् धातु
अस्मि, असि, अस्ति; स्वः, स्थः, स्तः; स्मः, स्थ, सन्ति – ये लट् लकार के रूप हैं।
Hindi saransh
धातु के रूप लकार, पुरुष और वचन के अनुसार बदलते हैं। लट् वर्तमान, लृट् भविष्य, लङ् भूत, लोट् आज्ञा तथा विधिलिङ् चाहिए/संभावना के लिए प्रयुक्त होता है।
लृट् में स्य, लङ् में अ का आगम, लोट् में तु, विधिलिङ् में एत्।

Visual lesson

धातुरूपाणि – लकाराः

संस्कृते क्रियापदानां रूपाणि धातुः, लकारः, पुरुषः, वचनं च अनुसृत्य भवन्ति। लकाराः दश सन्ति

🔑

Big idea

  • संस्कृते क्रियापदानां रूपाणि धातुः, लकारः, पुरुषः, वचनं च अनुसृत्य भवन्ति। लकाराः दश सन्ति
  • कक्षा दशमीपाठ्यक्रमे लट् (वर्तमान), लृट् (भविष्य), लङ् (अनद्यतन भूत), लोट् (आज्ञा/प्रार्थना), विधिलिङ् (चाहिए/सम्भावना) च अपेक्ष्यन्ते। पुरुषः त्रयः…
  • वचनानि त्रीणि – एकवचनम्, द्विवचनम्, बहुवचनम्। धातवः परस्मैपदिनः आत्मनेपदिनः उभयपदिनः च।
📌

लट् लकार

  • पठ् धातु: पठति, पठतः, पठन्ति (प्रथम)
  • पठसि, पठथः, पठथ (मध्यम)
  • पठामि, पठावः, पठामः (उत्तम)। अर्थ: वर्तमान काल।
🧠

लृट्, लङ्, लोट्, विधिलिङ्

  • लृट् में स्य/ष्य जुड़ता है – पठिष्यति। लङ् में अ का आगम – अपठत्। लोट् – पठतु, पठ, पठानि। विधिलिङ् – पठेत्, पठेः, पठेयम्।
🌟

पुरुष व्यवस्था

  • प्रथम पुरुष में नाम/सः, मध्यम में त्वम्/यूयम्, उत्तम में अहम्/वयम्। संस्कृत में पुरुष का क्रम हिन्दी से उलटा माना जाता है।
🔬

अस् धातु

  • अस्मि, असि, अस्ति
  • स्वः, स्थः, स्तः
  • स्मः, स्थ, सन्ति – ये लट् लकार के रूप हैं।
🧮

Formula tiles

लट्वर्तमानपठति
लृट्भविष्यपठिष्यति
लङ्भूतअपठत्
लोट्आज्ञापठतु
विधिलिङ्चाहिएपठेत्
प्रथमसःपठति
मध्यमत्वम्पठसि
उत्तमअहम्पठामि
🎯 Remember लृट् में स्य, लङ् में अ का आगम, लोट् में तु, विधिलिङ् में एत्।
🇮🇳

हिंदी सार

धातु के रूप लकार, पुरुष और वचन के अनुसार बदलते हैं। लट् वर्तमान, लृट् भविष्य, लङ् भूत, लोट् आज्ञा तथा विधिलिङ् चाहिए/संभावना के लिए प्रयुक्त होता है।

lessons.title: कारकम् – विभक्तयः – उपपदविभक्तयः
yt: class 10 sanskrit karak vibhakti

blocks.x: कारकम् नाम क्रियया सह सम्बन्धः। संस्कृते सप्त विभक्तयः – प्रथमा (कर्ता), द्वितीया (कर्म), तृतीया (करण), चतुर्थी (सम्प्रदान), पञ्चमी (अपादान), षष्ठी (सम्बन्ध), सप्तमी (अधिकरण), सम्बोधनम्। कुछ शब्दों के योग में विशेष विभक्ति होती है, जिसे उपपद विभक्ति कहते हैं – नमः, स्वस्ति, स्वाहा (चतुर्थी); सह, साकम् (तृतीया); अभितः, परितः, उभयतः, सर्वतः, धिक्, प्रति (द्वितीया); ऋते (पञ्चमी)।
Deep dive: कारक एवं विभक्ति

कर्ता – जो क्रिया करे (प्रथमा); कर्म – जिस पर क्रिया का फल पड़े (द्वितीया); करण – साधन (तृतीया); सम्प्रदान – जिसे दिया जाए (चतुर्थी); अपादान – अलगाव (पञ्चमी); सम्बन्ध – षष्ठी (कारक नहीं); अधिकरण – आधार (सप्तमी)।
Deep dive: उपपद विभक्तियाँ
नमः शिवाय। स्वस्ति गणेशाय। रामेण सह सीता गच्छति। ग्रामम् अभितः वृक्षाः सन्ति। बालकं धिक्। ज्ञानेन विना जीवनं व्यर्थम्। धनात् ऋते सुखं न।
Deep dive: रूपमाला
राम (अकारान्त पुल्लिङ्ग): रामः, रामौ, रामाः; रामम्, रामौ, रामान्; रामेण, रामाभ्याम्, रामैः; रामाय, रामाभ्याम्, रामेभ्यः; रामात्, रामाभ्याम्, रामेभ्यः; रामस्य, रामयोः, रामाणाम्; रामे, रामयोः, रामेषु।
Deep dive: हिन्दी चिह्न
ने (प्रथमा), को (द्वितीया), से/द्वारा (तृतीया), के लिए (चतुर्थी), से अलग (पञ्चमी), का/की/के (षष्ठी), में/पर (सप्तमी)।
Hindi saransh
कारक सात हैं। प्रथमा से कर्ता, द्वितीया से कर्म, तृतीया से करण, चतुर्थी से सम्प्रदान, पञ्चमी से अपादान और सप्तमी से अधिकरण का बोध होता है। उपपद के योग में विशेष विभक्ति होती है।
नमः-स्वस्ति-स्वाहा के साथ चतुर्थी; सह-साकम् के साथ तृतीया।

problems.q: कारक किसे कहते हैं? प्रत्येक विभक्ति का नाम, कारक और उदाहरण लिखिए।
problems.a: क्रिया से सीधे सम्बन्ध वाले पद को कारक कहते हैं। प्रथमा – कर्ता (रामः पठति), द्वितीया – कर्म (फलं खादति), तृतीया – करण (लेखन्या लिखति), चतुर्थी – सम्प्रदान (विप्राय गां ददाति), पञ्चमी – अपादान (वृक्षात् पर्णं पतति), षष्ठी – सम्बन्ध (रामस्य गृहम्), सप्तमी – अधिकरण (वने सिंहः तिष्ठति)।

कारकम् – विभक्तयः – उपपदविभक्तयः

कारकम् नाम क्रियया सह सम्बन्धः। संस्कृते सप्त विभक्तयः – प्रथमा (कर्ता), द्वितीया (कर्म), तृतीया (करण), चतुर्थी (सम्प्रदान), पञ्चमी (अपादान), षष्ठी (सम्बन्ध), सप्तमी…

Big idea

  • कारकम् नाम क्रियया सह सम्बन्धः। संस्कृते सप्त विभक्तयः – प्रथमा (कर्ता), द्वितीया (कर्म), तृतीया (करण), चतुर्थी (सम्प्रदान), पञ्चमी (अपादान), षष्ठी…
  • सह, साकम् (तृतीया)
  • अभितः, परितः, उभयतः, सर्वतः, धिक्, प्रति (द्वितीया)
  • ऋते (पञ्चमी)।
Read the full explanation

कारकम् नाम क्रियया सह सम्बन्धः। संस्कृते सप्त विभक्तयः – प्रथमा (कर्ता), द्वितीया (कर्म), तृतीया (करण), चतुर्थी (सम्प्रदान), पञ्चमी (अपादान), षष्ठी (सम्बन्ध), सप्तमी (अधिकरण), सम्बोधनम्। कुछ शब्दों के योग में विशेष विभक्ति होती है, जिसे उपपद विभक्ति कहते हैं – नमः, स्वस्ति, स्वाहा (चतुर्थी); सह, साकम् (तृतीया); अभितः, परितः, उभयतः, सर्वतः, धिक्, प्रति (द्वितीया); ऋते (पञ्चमी)।

📌

कारक एवं विभक्ति

  • कर्ता – जो क्रिया करे (प्रथमा)
  • कर्म – जिस पर क्रिया का फल पड़े (द्वितीया)
  • करण – साधन (तृतीया)
  • सम्प्रदान – जिसे दिया जाए (चतुर्थी)
Read the full explanation

कर्ता – जो क्रिया करे (प्रथमा); कर्म – जिस पर क्रिया का फल पड़े (द्वितीया); करण – साधन (तृतीया); सम्प्रदान – जिसे दिया जाए (चतुर्थी); अपादान – अलगाव (पञ्चमी); सम्बन्ध – षष्ठी (कारक नहीं); अधिकरण – आधार (सप्तमी)।

🧠

उपपद विभक्तियाँ

  • नमः शिवाय। स्वस्ति गणेशाय। रामेण सह सीता गच्छति। ग्रामम् अभितः वृक्षाः सन्ति। बालकं धिक्। ज्ञानेन विना जीवनं व्यर्थम्। धनात् ऋते सुखं न।
🌟

रूपमाला

  • राम (अकारान्त पुल्लिङ्ग): रामः, रामौ, रामाः
  • रामम्, रामौ, रामान्
  • रामेण, रामाभ्याम्, रामैः
  • रामाय, रामाभ्याम्, रामेभ्यः
Read the full explanation

राम (अकारान्त पुल्लिङ्ग): रामः, रामौ, रामाः; रामम्, रामौ, रामान्; रामेण, रामाभ्याम्, रामैः; रामाय, रामाभ्याम्, रामेभ्यः; रामात्, रामाभ्याम्, रामेभ्यः; रामस्य, रामयोः, रामाणाम्; रामे, रामयोः, रामेषु।

🔬

हिन्दी चिह्न

  • ने (प्रथमा), को (द्वितीया), से/द्वारा (तृतीया), के लिए (चतुर्थी), से अलग (पञ्चमी), का/की/के (षष्ठी), में/पर (सप्तमी)।
🧮

🇮🇳

हिंदी सार

कारक सात हैं। प्रथमा से कर्ता, द्वितीया से कर्म, तृतीया से करण, चतुर्थी से सम्प्रदान, पञ्चमी से अपादान और सप्तमी से अधिकरण का बोध होता है। उपपद के योग में विशेष विभक्ति होती है।

lessons.title: वाच्यम् – संख्या – समयः – अव्ययानि
yt: class 10 sanskrit vachya sankhya avyaya

blocks.x: वाच्यं त्रिविधम् – कर्तृवाच्यम्, कर्मवाच्यम्, भाववाच्यम्। कर्तृवाच्ये कर्ता प्रथमायां, कर्म द्वितीयायां; कर्मवाच्ये कर्ता तृतीयायां, कर्म प्रथमायां, धातोः आत्मनेपद + य प्रत्ययः (पठ्यते); भाववाच्ये कर्तृपदं तृतीयायां, क्रिया प्रथमपुरुषैकवचने (हस्यते)। संख्यावाचकानि विशेषणानि, समयवाचकानि पदानि, अव्ययानि (यदा-तदा, यत्र-तत्र, सदा, एव, अपि, च) अपि अपेक्षितानि।
Deep dive: वाच्य परिवर्तन
कर्तृवाच्य: रामः ग्रन्थं पठति। कर्मवाच्य: रामेण ग्रन्थः पठ्यते। भाववाच्य: रामेण हस्यते (अकर्मक धातु)।
Deep dive: संख्याएँ
1-10: एकम्, द्वे, त्रीणि, चत्वारि, पञ्च, षट्, सप्त, अष्ट, नव, दश। 11-19: एकादश से नवदश (उनविंशति भी)। 20: विंशतिः।
Deep dive: समय
सपाद = सवा; सार्ध = डेढ़/साढ़े; पादोन = पौन (पौने)। उदाहरण: सपादैकवादनम् = 1:15; सार्धैकवादनम् = 1:30; पादोनद्विवादनम् = 1:45।
Deep dive: अव्यय
अव्यय वे हैं जिनके रूप लिङ्ग, वचन, विभक्ति के कारण नहीं बदलते – यथा तथा, यदा तदा, अत्र तत्र, एव, अपि, च, वा, न।
Hindi saransh
कर्तृवाच्य, कर्मवाच्य और भाववाच्य के क्रियापद और कर्ता की विभक्तियाँ बदलती हैं। संख्या और समय के शब्द तथा अव्यय अवश्य याद रखें।
कर्मवाच्य में कर्ता तृतीया, कर्म प्रथमा; क्रिया कर्म के अनुसार।

problems.q: निम्नवाक्यानि कर्मवाच्ये परिवर्तयत – (क) रामः ग्रन्थं पठति (ख) सः कार्यं करोति।
problems.a: (क) रामेण ग्रन्थः पठ्यते। (ख) तेन कार्यं क्रियते।
सपादैकवादनम्, सार्धैकवादनम्, पादोनद्विवादनम्।

problems.q: कर्तृ, कर्म तथा भाववाच्य का अन्तर उदाहरण सहित लिखिए।
problems.a: कर्तृवाच्य में कर्ता प्रधान (बालकः फलं खादति); कर्मवाच्य में कर्म प्रधान (बालकेन फलं खाद्यते); भाववाच्य में क्रिया का भाव प्रधान, अकर्मक धातु (बालकेन हस्यते)।

Visual lesson

वाच्यम् – संख्या – समयः – अव्ययानि

वाच्यं त्रिविधम् – कर्तृवाच्यम्, कर्मवाच्यम्, भाववाच्यम्। कर्तृवाच्ये कर्ता प्रथमायां, कर्म द्वितीयायां

सपाद1/4 अधिक
सार्ध1/2 अधिक

🔑

Big idea

  • वाच्यं त्रिविधम् – कर्तृवाच्यम्, कर्मवाच्यम्, भाववाच्यम्। कर्तृवाच्ये कर्ता प्रथमायां, कर्म द्वितीयायां
  • कर्मवाच्ये कर्ता तृतीयायां, कर्म प्रथमायां, धातोः आत्मनेपद + य प्रत्ययः (पठ्यते)
  • भाववाच्ये कर्तृपदं तृतीयायां, क्रिया प्रथमपुरुषैकवचने (हस्यते)। संख्यावाचकानि विशेषणानि, समयवाचकानि पदानि, अव्ययानि (यदा-तदा, यत्र-तत्र, सदा, एव…
📌

वाच्य परिवर्तन

  • कर्तृवाच्य: रामः ग्रन्थं पठति। कर्मवाच्य: रामेण ग्रन्थः पठ्यते। भाववाच्य: रामेण हस्यते (अकर्मक धातु)।
🧠

संख्याएँ

  • 1-10: एकम्, द्वे, त्रीणि, चत्वारि, पञ्च, षट्, सप्त, अष्ट, नव, दश। 11-19: एकादश से नवदश (उनविंशति भी)। 20: विंशतिः।
🌟

समय

  • सार्ध = डेढ़/साढ़े
  • पादोन = पौन (पौने)। उदाहरण: सपादैकवादनम् = 1:15
  • सार्धैकवादनम् = 1:30
  • पादोनद्विवादनम् = 1:45।
🔬

अव्यय

  • अव्यय वे हैं जिनके रूप लिङ्ग, वचन, विभक्ति के कारण नहीं बदलते – यथा तथा, यदा तदा, अत्र तत्र, एव, अपि, च, वा, न।
🧮

Formula tiles

कर्तृवाच्यकर्ता प्रथमारामः पठति
कर्मवाच्यकर्ता तृतीयारामेण पाठः पठ्यते
भाववाच्यक्रिया एकवचनरामेण हस्यते
🎯 Remember कर्मवाच्य में कर्ता तृतीया, कर्म प्रथमा; क्रिया कर्म के अनुसार।
🇮🇳

हिंदी सार

कर्तृवाच्य, कर्मवाच्य और भाववाच्य के क्रियापद और कर्ता की विभक्तियाँ बदलती हैं। संख्या और समय के शब्द तथा अव्यय अवश्य याद रखें।

कर्ता-क्रिया में पुरुष एवं वचन का न मिलना, कर्म की विभक्ति द्वितीया न होना, उपपद के साथ गलत विभक्ति, अव्यय के प्रयोग की त्रुटि।

Visual lesson

अशुद्धिशोधनम्

अशुद्धिशोधनम् इत्यस्मिन् वाक्येषु वर्तमाना त्रुटिः परिमार्जनीया। मुख्यतः कर्तृक्रियासंवादः (पुरुष-वचन), विभक्तिः, लकारः, उपपदविभक्तिः च परीक्ष्यन्ते। पद्धतिः – प्रथमं…

blocks.x: अनुवादः नाम एकस्याः भाषायाः वाक्यस्य अन्यभाषायां रूपान्तरणम्। हिन्दीवाक्यानि संस्कृते अनूद्यन्ते। प्रक्रिया – कर्ता, कर्म, क्रिया, कालः, पुरुषः, वचनं च निश्चित्य उचितानि रूपाणि लेखनीयानि। सामान्यक्रम: कर्ता + कर्म + क्रिया। वाक्येषु कर्ता-क्रिया-संवादः आवश्यकः। भविष्यकाले लृट्, भूतकाले लङ् प्रयोज्यम्।
Deep dive: अनुवाद-विधि

x: वाक्य में कर्ता पहचानें। 2. कर्ता का पुरुष-वचन निश्चित करें। 3. क्रिया के लिए धातु तथा लकार चुनें। 4. कर्म में द्वितीया विभक्ति लगाएँ। 5. वाक्य को क्रम से लिखें।

blocks.x: Deep dive: उपयोगी शब्द
अहम् (मैं), त्वम् (तुम), सः (वह), वयम् (हम), यूयम् (तुम सब), ते (वे); गच्छति, पठति, खादति, पिबति, लिखति, पश्यति, वदति, करोति।
Deep dive: सावधानियाँ
कर्ता-क्रिया संवाद, विभक्ति, काल का ध्यान। भविष्यत् में -ष्यति, भूत में अ-आगम। आज्ञा में लोट् लकार।
Hindi saransh
हिन्दी वाक्य का संस्कृत में अनुवाद करते समय कर्ता, कर्म और क्रिया का मेल रखें। द्वितीया में कर्म, सप्तमी में आधार लिखें।
कर्ता + कर्म + क्रिया का क्रम रखें।

lessons.title: रचनात्मकं कार्यम् – पत्रम्, चित्रवर्णनम्, अनुच्छेदः
yt: class 10 sanskrit rachna patra anuchhed

blocks.x: रचनात्मकं कार्यं त्रिषु भागेषु विभक्तम् – पत्रलेखनम् (अनौपचारिकम्, औपचारिकम्), चित्रवर्णनम्, अनुच्छेदलेखनम्। पत्रे स्थान-तिथिः, सम्बोधनम्, विषयः, समाप्तिः, नाम च क्रमशः लेख्यानि। चित्रवर्णने चित्रे दृश्यमानानां वस्तूनां वाक्यानि लट् लकारे लेखनीयानि। अनुच्छेदे विषयस्य परिचयः, विस्तारः, सारः च भवति।
Deep dive: पत्र
अनौपचारिक: मित्र/पिता को – स्थान, तिथि, सम्बोधन, कुशल-क्षेम, मुख्य बात, समाप्ति (भवदीयः मित्रम्)। औपचारिक: प्रधानाचार्य को – सेवायाम्, सम्बोधन (श्रीमन्), विषय, निवेदन, भवदीयः शिष्यः।
Deep dive: चित्रवर्णन
पहले चित्र के स्थान का वर्णन करें, फिर मुख्य वस्तु, फिर पात्र/पशु-पक्षी, उनके कार्य और अंत में सन्देश। 5–8 वाक्य।
Deep dive: अनुच्छेद
विषय: मम विद्यालयः, गङ्गा नदी, पर्यावरणम्, विज्ञानम्, गौः, मम प्रियः खेलः। 8–10 वाक्य, सरल भाषा।
Hindi saransh
पत्र में स्थान-तिथि, सम्बोधन, विषय और समापन क्रम से लिखें। चित्र वर्णन लट् लकार में करें। अनुच्छेद सरल वाक्यों में लिखें।
पत्र = स्थान-तिथि, सम्बोधन, विषय, समाप्ति। चित्र = लट् लकार।

problems.q: अनौपचारिक पत्र का प्रारूप लिखिए।
problems.a: स्थान-तिथि; प्रिय मित्र; कुशलक्षेम और मुख्य बात; भवदीयः मित्रम्; नाम।

problems.q: प्रधानाचार्य को अवकाश पत्र लिखिए।
problems.a: सेवायाम्, श्रीमान् प्रधानाचार्यः, विद्यालयः; विषय – अवकाशार्थम् प्रार्थनापत्रम्; महोदय, निवेदनम् अस्ति यत् मम ज्वरः अस्ति, अतः अद्य अवकाशः दीयताम्; भवदीयः शिष्यः, नाम, कक्षा।

problems.q: "पर्यावरणम्" पर आठ वाक्यों का संस्कृत अनुच्छेद लिखिए।
problems.a: पर्यावरणं जीवनस्य आधारः। वृक्षाः प्राणवायुं ददति। जलं जीवनम्। वायुः शुद्धः भवेत्। नदीः स्वच्छाः रक्षेम। प्लास्टिकं न उपयुञ्ज्महे। वृक्षान् रोपयामः। पर्यावरणरक्षणं सर्वेषां कर्तव्यम्।

  • रचनात्मकं कार्यं त्रिषु भागेषु विभक्तम् – पत्रलेखनम् (अनौपचारिकम्, औपचारिकम्), चित्रवर्णनम्, अनुच्छेदलेखनम्। पत्रे स्थान-तिथिः, सम्बोधनम्, विषयः…
📌

पत्र

  • अनौपचारिक: मित्र/पिता को – स्थान, तिथि, सम्बोधन, कुशल-क्षेम, मुख्य बात, समाप्ति (भवदीयः मित्रम्)। औपचारिक: प्रधानाचार्य को – सेवायाम्, सम्बोधन…
🧠

चित्रवर्णन

  • पहले चित्र के स्थान का वर्णन करें, फिर मुख्य वस्तु, फिर पात्र/पशु-पक्षी, उनके कार्य और अंत में सन्देश। 5–8 वाक्य।
🌟

अनुच्छेद

  • विषय: मम विद्यालयः, गङ्गा नदी, पर्यावरणम्, विज्ञानम्, गौः, मम प्रियः खेलः। 8–10 वाक्य, सरल भाषा।
🧮

Formula tiles

🇮🇳

हिंदी सार

पत्र में स्थान-तिथि, सम्बोधन, विषय और समापन क्रम से लिखें। चित्र वर्णन लट् लकार में करें। अनुच्छेद सरल वाक्यों में लिखें।

blocks.x: अपठित-अवबोधनम् इत्यस्मिन् अज्ञातगद्यांशं पठित्वा प्रश्नानाम् उत्तराणि देयानि। प्रश्नेषु एकपदेन उत्तरम्, पूर्णवाक्येन उत्तरम्, निर्देशानुसारम्, शीर्षकम्, सत्यासत्यम्, विलोमपदम्, पर्यायपदम् च भवन्ति। प्रथमं गद्यांशं ध्यानेन पठित्वा सन्दर्भेण अर्थं ज्ञात्वा उत्तरं लिखेत्।
Deep dive: उत्तर देने की विधि
पूरा अनुच्छेद पढ़ें; प्रश्न देखें; उत्तर वाला वाक्य खोजें; प्रश्न के निर्देश (एकपदेन/पूर्णवाक्येन) के अनुसार उत्तर लिखें; कर्ता-क्रिया संवाद रखें।
Deep dive: शब्द-भंडार
विलोम शब्द (सुखम्-दुःखम्), पर्याय (जलम्-नीरम्), प्रत्यय पहचान, सन्धि विच्छेद इस भाग में पूछे जाते हैं। इसलिए शब्दकोश और व्याकरण अभ्यास करें।
Deep dive: नमूना गद्यांश
अहं ग्रामे वसामि। ग्रामे बहवः वृक्षाः सन्ति। प्रातःकाले खगाः कूजन्ति। जनाः क्षेत्रे कार्यं कुर्वन्ति।
Hindi saransh
अपठित गद्यांश को ध्यान से पढ़ें, प्रश्न देखें और अनुच्छेद से ही उत्तर खोजें। विलोम, पर्याय और व्याकरण के प्रश्न भी आते हैं।
उत्तर हमेशा अनुच्छेद से, निर्देश देखकर लिखें।

lessons.title: Electricity and light (Class 10)
yt: class 10 electricity light

blocks.x: **Ohm's law** V = IR; power P = VI = I^2 R. For V = 5 V and R = 10 ohm: I = **0.5 A**, P = **2.5 W**. Resistors in series add; in parallel 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2: 2 ohm and 3 ohm give **1.2 ohm**. Heating effect H = I^2 R t. **Light:** mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f; magnification m = -v/u. Concave mirror f = -15 cm, object at u = -30 cm: v = **-30 cm**, m = **-1** (real, inverted, same size). **Refraction:** Snell's law; refractive index n = c / v: if light travels at 2 x 10^8 m/s in glass, n = **1.5**. Lens power P = 1/f (metres), in dioptres. **Magnetic effects:** field around a current carrying wire; motor, generator, electromagnetic induction.
Deep dive: electricity

**Charge and current.** Current I is the rate of flow of charge: I = Q / t. One ampere is one coulomb per second. The charge of one electron is 1.6 x 10^-19 C, so 1 C is about 6.25 x 10^18 electrons. Conventional current flows from the positive to the negative terminal, opposite to the electron flow. **Potential difference.** V = W / Q: the work done to move one coulomb between two points. Unit: volt (1 V = 1 J/C). A voltmeter is connected in parallel across a component; an ammeter is connected in series. **Ohm's law.** At constant temperature V is proportional to I, so V = I R. The graph of V against I is a straight line through the origin whose slope is R. Resistance depends on length, area and material: R = rho L / A. Doubling the length doubles R; doubling the area halves R. Resistivity rho depends only on the material and temperature (metals: low, alloys: higher, insulators: very high). **Series and parallel.** Series: the same current passes through every resistor, R = R1 + R2 + ... and the voltages add. Parallel: every resistor has the same voltage, 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ... and the currents add; the combined resistance is smaller than the smallest. Household appliances are in parallel so each gets 220 V and works independently. **Heating effect.** H = I^2 R t = V I t = V^2 t / R (Joule's law). Used in heaters, geysers, irons and fuses. A fuse is a thin wire of low melting point in series with the appliance that melts when the current is too high. **Electric power and energy.** P = V I = I^2 R = V^2 / R, in watts. Energy E = P t. The commercial unit is the kilowatt hour: 1 kWh = 3.6 x 10^6 J = 1 unit of electricity.
Deep dive: light

**Reflection.** The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection; the incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in one plane. A plane mirror forms a virtual, erect image the same size as the object, as far behind the mirror as the object is in front. **Spherical mirrors.** Focal length f = R / 2. Sign convention (Cartesian): distances measured from the pole; in the direction of the incident light is positive, against it is negative. For a concave mirror f is negative; for a convex mirror f is positive. Mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. Magnification m = h'/h = -v/u. A concave mirror gives a real inverted image when the object is beyond f; with the object between pole and f it gives a virtual, erect, enlarged image (shaving mirror, dentist's mirror). A convex mirror always gives a virtual, erect, diminished image (rear-view mirrors). **Refraction.** Light bends when it passes from one medium to another because its speed changes. Snell's law: sin i / sin r = n21 = constant. Absolute refractive index n = c / v with c = 3 x 10^8 m/s. Going into a denser medium the ray bends towards the normal. Glass slab: the emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray but shifted sideways. **Lenses.** Lens formula: 1/v - 1/u = 1/f. Magnification m = v/u. Power P = 1/f with f in metres; the unit is the dioptre. Convex lens: f positive, converging, P positive. Concave lens: f negative, diverging, P negative. Lenses placed in contact add their powers: P = P1 + P2. **Human eye.** Myopia (short sight) is corrected by a concave lens; hypermetropia (long sight) by a convex lens. Presbyopia comes with age and needs bifocal lenses. Dispersion by a prism splits white light into VIBGYOR; a rainbow is dispersion plus internal reflection in raindrops; the sky is blue because shorter wavelengths scatter most.
Hindi saransh
V = IR. Parallel mein 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2. n = c / v.
Real images are inverted and formed on the screen side.

qa.q: Equivalent of 2 ohm and 3 ohm in parallel?
Refractive index of glass if v = 2e8 m/s?
Image position for a concave mirror f = -15 cm and u = -30 cm?
qa.a: v = -30 cm at the centre of curvature, same size, inverted.

qa.q: Formula for electric power?
What is electric current?
qa.a: The rate of flow of electric charge: I = Q / t. Its unit is the ampere.

qa.q: Define one ampere.
qa.a: One ampere is a flow of one coulomb of charge per second.

qa.q: Define potential difference.
qa.a: The work done to move a unit charge between two points: V = W / Q. Unit: volt.

qa.q: State Ohm's law.
qa.a: At constant temperature, the current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across it: V = I R.

qa.q: What does the slope of a V-I graph show?
qa.a: The resistance R of the conductor.

qa.q: On what factors does the resistance of a wire depend?
qa.a: Its length, area of cross-section, the material, and the temperature.

qa.q: What is resistivity?
qa.a: The resistance of a wire of unit length and unit area of cross-section; it depends only on the material and temperature.

qa.q: Why are alloys used in heating elements?
qa.a: Alloys have high resistivity and do not oxidise easily at high temperature.

qa.q: Why is tungsten used for bulb filaments?
qa.a: It has a very high melting point (about 3380 C).

qa.q: How should an ammeter be connected?
qa.a: In series with the component, and it should have very low resistance.

qa.q: How should a voltmeter be connected?
qa.a: In parallel across the component, and it should have very high resistance.

qa.q: What is the effect of doubling the length of a wire on its resistance?
What is the effect of doubling the radius of a wire on its resistance?
qa.a: It becomes one quarter, since the area becomes four times larger.

qa.q: Why are household appliances connected in parallel?
qa.a: Each gets the same 220 V, can be switched independently, and the total current is shared.

qa.q: What is the use of a fuse?
qa.a: It protects circuits: its thin wire melts and breaks the circuit when the current is too high.

qa.q: State Joule's law of heating.
qa.a: H = I^2 R t: heat produced is proportional to the square of the current, the resistance and the time.

qa.q: What is the SI unit of electric power?
What is 1 kilowatt hour?
qa.a: The energy used by a 1 kW appliance in 1 hour: 3.6 x 10^6 J.

qa.q: Which effect of current is used in an electric heater?
Why does the filament of a bulb glow but the connecting wires do not?
qa.a: The filament has much higher resistance, so more heat is produced in it for the same current.

qa.q: Why do parallel resistors have a smaller combined resistance?
qa.a: More paths are available for the current, so the total opposition falls below the smallest single resistance.

qa.q: What is a short circuit?
qa.a: A path of almost zero resistance across the supply, causing a very large current and overheating.

qa.q: Why is the earth wire used?
qa.a: It carries leakage current to the ground and protects the user from shock.

qa.q: What colour is the live wire in India?
qa.a: Red (neutral is black, earth is green).

qa.q: What is the direction of conventional current?
qa.a: From the positive terminal to the negative terminal outside the cell.

qa.q: State the law of reflection.
qa.a: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, and the incident ray, reflected ray and normal lie in the same plane.

qa.q: What are the properties of an image in a plane mirror?
qa.a: Virtual, erect, same size, laterally inverted, as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

qa.q: What is the relation between focal length and radius of curvature?
State the mirror formula.
What does a negative magnification mean?
qa.a: The image is real and inverted.

qa.q: What is the sign of f for a concave mirror?
qa.a: Negative, by the Cartesian sign convention.

qa.q: What is the sign of f for a convex mirror?
Which mirror is used as a rear-view mirror and why?
qa.a: A convex mirror: it gives an erect, diminished image and a wider field of view.

qa.q: Which mirror is used by dentists and in shaving?
qa.a: A concave mirror: with the object within the focal length it gives an erect, enlarged, virtual image.

qa.q: What is refraction?
qa.a: The bending of light when it passes obliquely from one transparent medium to another because its speed changes.

qa.q: State Snell's law.
qa.a: The ratio sin i / sin r is a constant for a given pair of media and light colour.

qa.q: Define absolute refractive index.
qa.a: n = speed of light in vacuum / speed of light in the medium = c / v.

qa.q: Which medium is optically denser: water (n = 1.33) or glass (n = 1.5)?
qa.a: Glass, because it has the higher refractive index.

qa.q: In which direction does light bend entering a denser medium?
What happens to a ray passing through a rectangular glass slab?
qa.a: It emerges parallel to the incident ray but shifted sideways (lateral displacement).

qa.q: State the lens formula.
What is the power of a lens?
qa.a: P = 1/f with f in metres; the unit is the dioptre (D).

qa.q: What is the sign of power for a convex lens?
qa.a: Positive. A concave lens has negative power.

qa.q: How is myopia corrected?
qa.a: With a concave lens of suitable power.

qa.q: How is hypermetropia corrected?
What causes the blue colour of the sky?
qa.a: Scattering of light: the shorter blue wavelengths scatter most by air molecules.

qa.q: Why does the Sun appear red at sunrise and sunset?
qa.a: Light travels through more atmosphere, so blue is scattered away and red reaches the eye.

qa.q: How does a rainbow form?
qa.a: By dispersion, refraction and internal reflection of sunlight in water droplets.

qa.q: What is dispersion?
qa.a: The splitting of white light into its seven colours when passing through a prism.
