lessons.title: Binomial Theorem
yt: class 11 maths binomial theorem expansion general term pascal triangle

blocks.x: The binomial theorem gives the expansion of (a + b)^n for a positive integer n: (a + b)^n = nC0 a^n + nC1 a^(n-1) b + nC2 a^(n-2) b^2 + ... + nCn b^n, where nCr = n!/(r!(n - r)!). The expansion has n + 1 terms. The general term (r + 1)th is T(r+1) = nCr a^(n-r) b^r. The coefficients are the entries of Pascal's triangle, where each entry is the sum of the two above, and nCr = n-1Cr-1 + n-1Cr. Properties: nCr = nC(n-r); the sum of all coefficients is 2^n (put a = b = 1); the sum of coefficients with alternate signs is 0 (put a = 1, b = -1); the sum of the coefficients of odd terms equals the sum of even terms, each 2^(n-1). In (a - b)^n the signs alternate. Middle terms: if n is even there is one middle term, the (n/2 + 1)th; if n is odd there are two, the ((n+1)/2)th and ((n+3)/2)th. The coefficient of x^k in (x + 1/x)^n is found by setting the power of x in T(r+1) equal to k. The term independent of x has power zero. The greatest coefficient is the middle binomial coefficient. Special cases: (1 + x)^n = sum nCr x^r and (1 - x)^n. Applications: finding approximate values such as (1.01)^10, divisibility questions and remainders. The expansion of (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2 and (a + b)^3 = a^3 + 3a^2 b + 3ab^2 + b^3. Also nC0 + nC1 + ... + nCn = 2^n.
Deep dive: Expansion and general term

Write T(r+1) with the power of each part. For a term containing x^k solve the equation for r. r must be a whole number between 0 and n. For (a + b)^n the powers of a fall from n to 0 while those of b rise from 0 to n.
Deep dive: Properties
Coefficients are symmetric. Sum of coefficients is 2^n. Pascal triangle gives coefficients quickly. The middle term has the greatest coefficient.
Deep dive: Applications
Approximation: (1 + x)^n is about 1 + nx for small x. Divisibility: express a number as (1 + k)^n or similar. Remainder questions use the first terms of the expansion.
Hindi saransh
Dvipad prameya: (a+b)^n ke n+1 pad hote hain; samanya pad nCr a^(n-r) b^r; gunankon ka yog 2^n.
The (r+1)th term uses nCr, not nC(r+1).

Read the full explanation

The binomial theorem gives the expansion of (a + b)^n for a positive integer n: (a + b)^n = nC0 a^n + nC1 a^(n-1) b + nC2 a^(n-2) b^2 + ... + nCn b^n, where nCr = n!/(r!(n - r)!). The expansion has n + 1 terms. The general term (r + 1)th is T(r+1) = nCr a^(n-r) b^r. The coefficients are the entries of Pascal's triangle, where each entry is the sum of the two above, and nCr = n-1Cr-1 + n-1Cr. Properties: nCr = nC(n-r); the sum of all coefficients is 2^n (put a = b = 1); the sum of coefficients with alternate signs is 0 (put a = 1, b = -1); the sum of the coefficients of odd terms equals the sum of even terms, each 2^(n-1). In (a - b)^n the signs alternate. Middle terms: if n is even there is one middle term, the (n/2 + 1)th; if n is odd there are two, the ((n+1)/2)th and ((n+3)/2)th. The coefficient of x^k in (x + 1/x)^n is found by setting the power of x in T(r+1) equal to k. The term independent of x has power zero. The greatest coefficient is the middle binomial coefficient. Special cases: (1 + x)^n = sum nCr x^r and (1 - x)^n. Applications: finding approximate values such as (1.01)^10, divisibility questions and remainders. The expansion of (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2 and (a + b)^3 = a^3 + 3a^2 b + 3ab^2 + b^3. Also nC0 + nC1 + ... + nCn = 2^n.

🧬

Expansion and general term

  • Write T(r+1) with the power of each part
  • For a term containing x^k solve the equation for r
  • R must be a whole number between 0 and n
  • For (a + b)^n the powers of a fall from n to 0 while those of b rise from 0 to n
🧠

Properties

  • Coefficients are symmetric
  • Sum of coefficients is 2^n
  • Pascal triangle gives coefficients quickly
  • The middle term has the greatest coefficient
💡

Applications

  • Approximation: (1 + x)^n is about 1 + nx for small x
  • Divisibility: express a number as (1 + k)^n or similar
  • Remainder questions use the first terms of the expansion

lessons.title: Conic sections
yt: class 11 conic sections

blocks.x: A conic is the section of a double cone by a plane: a circle, ellipse, parabola or hyperbola. Standard forms: circle x^2 + y^2 = r^2; parabola y^2 = 4ax; ellipse x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1 with b^2 = a^2(1 - e^2); hyperbola x^2/a^2 - y^2/b^2 = 1 with b^2 = a^2(e^2 - 1).
Deep dive: how conics arise

Cutting a double-napped cone by a plane gives: a circle (plane perpendicular to the axis), an ellipse (tilted plane cutting one nappe), a parabola (plane parallel to a generator) and a hyperbola (plane cutting both nappes). Every conic is the locus of a point whose distance from a fixed point (the focus) is e times its distance from a fixed line (the directrix): e = 0 circle, e < 1 ellipse, e = 1 parabola, e > 1 hyperbola.
Deep dive: circle and parabola

Circle with centre (h, k) and radius r: (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2; the general form x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 has centre (-g, -f) and radius sqrt (g^2 + f^2 - c). Parabola y^2 = 4ax: vertex (0, 0), focus (a, 0), directrix x = -a, axis the x-axis, length of latus rectum 4a. Other forms: y^2 = -4ax (opens left), x^2 = 4ay (opens up), x^2 = -4ay (opens down).
Deep dive: ellipse and hyperbola

Ellipse x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1 (a > b): centre origin, vertices (+-a, 0), foci (+-ae, 0), major axis length 2a, minor axis 2b, eccentricity e = sqrt (1 - b^2/a^2), latus rectum 2b^2/a, directrices x = +-a/e. Hyperbola x^2/a^2 - y^2/b^2 = 1: vertices (+-a, 0), foci (+-ae, 0), transverse axis 2a, conjugate axis 2b, e = sqrt (1 + b^2/a^2), latus rectum 2b^2/a, asymptotes y = +- (b/a) x. For the ellipse the sum of focal distances is 2a; for the hyperbola their difference is 2a.

Cutting a double-napped cone by a plane gives: a circle (plane perpendicular to the axis), an ellipse (tilted plane cutting one nappe), a parabola (plane parallel to a generator) and a hyperbola (plane cutting both nappes). Every conic is the locus of a point whose distance from a fixed point (the focus) is e times its distance from a fixed line (the directrix): e = 0 circle, e < 1 ellipse, e = 1 parabola, e > 1 hyperbola.

📐

Circle and parabola

  • Circle with centre (h, k) and radius r: (x - h)2 + (y - k)2 = r2
  • The general form x2 + y2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 has centre (-g, -f) and radius sqrt (g2 + f2 - c)
  • Parabola y2 = 4ax: vertex (0, 0), focus (a, 0), directrix x = -a, axis the x-axis, length of latus rectum 4a
  • Other forms: y2 = -4ax (opens left), x2 = 4ay (opens up), x2 = -4ay (opens down)
Read the full explanation

Circle with centre (h, k) and radius r: (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2; the general form x^2 + y^2 + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0 has centre (-g, -f) and radius sqrt (g^2 + f^2 - c). Parabola y^2 = 4ax: vertex (0, 0), focus (a, 0), directrix x = -a, axis the x-axis, length of latus rectum 4a. Other forms: y^2 = -4ax (opens left), x^2 = 4ay (opens up), x^2 = -4ay (opens down).

🌟

Ellipse and hyperbola

  • Ellipse x2/a2 + y2/b2 = 1 (a > b): centre origin, vertices (+-a, 0), foci (+-ae, 0), major axis length 2a, minor axis 2b, eccentricity e = sqrt…
  • Hyperbola x2/a2 - y2/b2 = 1: vertices (+-a, 0), foci (+-ae, 0), transverse axis 2a, conjugate axis 2b, e = sqrt (1 + b2/a2), latus rectum…
  • For the ellipse the sum of focal distances is 2a
  • For the hyperbola their difference is 2a
Read the full explanation

Ellipse x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1 (a > b): centre origin, vertices (+-a, 0), foci (+-ae, 0), major axis length 2a, minor axis 2b, eccentricity e = sqrt (1 - b^2/a^2), latus rectum 2b^2/a, directrices x = +-a/e. blocks.x: Probability of an event E is P(E) = favourable outcomes / total outcomes for equally likely outcomes. 0 <= P(E) <= 1, P(not E) = 1 - P(E), P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B). Mutually exclusive events cannot occur together; exhaustive events cover the whole sample space.
Deep dive: sample space and events

An experiment has outcomes forming the sample space S. An event is a subset of S. A simple event has one outcome; a compound event has more. The complement of E is E-bar (not E); A or B is the union, A and B is the intersection. Events A and B are mutually exclusive if A and B cannot both happen (A intersect B is empty), and exhaustive if their union is S. Typical sample spaces: a coin (2 outcomes), a die (6), two coins (4), two dice (36), three coins (8), a pack of 52 cards (4 suits x 13 ranks).
Deep dive: rules of probability

For equally likely outcomes P(E) = n(E)/n(S). Axioms: P(E) >= 0, P(S) = 1, and for mutually exclusive events P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B). Addition law: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B). Complement: P(A-bar) = 1 - P(A). P(A but not B) = P(A) - P(A and B). P(neither A nor B) = 1 - P(A or B). Odds in favour of E = P(E) : P(E-bar).
Deep dive: counting methods in probability

Use the multiplication principle and combinations: choosing r objects from n gives C(n, r) = n!/(r!(n - r)!). Drawing 2 cards from 52: total C(52, 2) = 1326. Two dice: the sum 7 occurs in 6 of 36 ways. P(at least one) = 1 - P(none). Dice sums: 2 and 12 occur once each; 7 occurs 6 times, the most likely sum. **Common mistakes:** treating outcomes as equally likely when they are not (the sum of two dice), double-counting overlap in P(A or B), and forgetting to use combinations for selections.

blocks.x: A point in space is (x, y, z) in three mutually perpendicular axes forming eight octants. The distance between (x1, y1, z1) and (x2, y2, z2) is sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2 + (z2 - z1)^2). The section formula divides a segment in the ratio m:n.
Deep dive: coordinate system in space

Three mutually perpendicular axes X, Y, Z meet at the origin O. The coordinate planes XY, YZ, ZX divide space into eight octants. A point P (x, y, z) has distances |x|, |y|, |z| from the YZ, ZX and XY planes. Points on the x-axis are (x, 0, 0), on the y-axis (0, y, 0), on the z-axis (0, 0, z). Points in the XY plane have z = 0, in YZ plane x = 0, in ZX plane y = 0. The octant of a point is decided by the signs of x, y, z.
Deep dive: distance and section formulae

Distance between P (x1, y1, z1) and Q (x2, y2, z2) is PQ = sqrt ((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2 + (z2 - z1)^2). The distance of P from the origin is sqrt (x^2 + y^2 + z^2). The point dividing PQ internally in the ratio m : n is ((m x2 + n x1)/(m + n), (m y2 + n y1)/(m + n), (m z2 + n z1)/(m + n)); the mid-point is the average of the coordinates, and for external division change n to -n. The centroid of a triangle is the mean of the three vertices.
Deep dive: applications

Three points are collinear if the sum of two of the distances equals the third. Triangle shape: if all three sides are equal it is equilateral; two equal, isosceles; a^2 + b^2 = c^2, right-angled. The locus of points at a fixed distance r from a given point is a sphere.
Hindi saransh
Distance: sqrt of sum of three squares. Section formula: (m x2 + n x1)/(m + n).
Mid-point = average of coordinates.

lessons.title: Permutations and Combinations
yt: class 11 maths permutations and combinations fundamental principle counting nPr nCr

blocks.x: The Fundamental Principle of Counting has two parts. The multiplication principle: if one event occurs in m ways and another in n ways, together they occur in m x n ways. The addition principle: if either of two exclusive events can occur in m or n ways, the number is m + n. The factorial n! = n(n - 1)(n - 2) ... 1, with 0! = 1. A permutation is an arrangement where order matters: nPr = n!/(n - r)!. A combination is a selection where order does not matter: nCr = n!/(r!(n - r)!), and nPr = r! nCr. Properties: nCr = nC(n-r); nCr + nC(r-1) = (n+1)Cr; nC0 = nCn = 1; nP n = n!. Permutations with repetition: the number of r-letter arrangements from n objects with repetition allowed is n^r. Permutations when some objects are alike: n!/(p! q! r!). Circular permutations: n objects in a circle can be arranged in (n - 1)! ways. Restricted arrangements: treat together items as a single block and multiply by internal arrangements; for items never together subtract the together count from the total; for fixed positions fill those first. Number of 4-digit numbers, words from MATHEMATICS (11 letters with M, A, T repeated twice: 11!/(2!2!2!)) and arrangements of the word INDIA are typical. Selection problems: choosing a committee from men and women uses products of combinations; selecting at least one uses 2^n - 1 total selections; the number of diagonals in an n-sided polygon is nC2 - n; the number of triangles from n points with p collinear is nC3 - pC3. The number of ways to divide into groups uses factorials of group sizes. Handshakes among n people number nC2.
Deep dive: Counting principles
Use multiplication when tasks are done one after another. Use addition when choices are alternatives. Break difficult problems into cases. Always check whether repetition is allowed.
Deep dive: Permutations

nPr counts ordered arrangements of r from n distinct objects. When letters repeat divide by the factorials of the repeats. For circular tables fix one person to remove rotations. For necklaces with reflection divide by 2 further.
Deep dive: Combinations
nCr counts committees and selections. Multiply combinations for choosing from different groups. Use complement counting for at least one. Geometry uses nC2 for lines and nC3 for triangles.
Hindi saransh
Kramchay aur sanchay: order mahatvapurn ho to nPr, na ho to nCr; vritiya kramchay (n-1)! hota hai.
Ask first: does order matter? If yes use permutation, otherwise combination.

Visual lesson

Permutations and Combinations

The Fundamental Principle of Counting has two parts

minutes
formulas

Flat concept map (2D)
1Big idea›2Counting principles›3Permutations›4Combinations
Circular(n-1)!
Selections2^n - 1
🔑

Big idea

  • The Fundamental Principle of Counting has two parts
  • The multiplication principle: if one event occurs in m ways and another in n ways, together they occur in m x n ways
  • The addition principle: if either of two exclusive events can occur in m or n ways, the number is m + n
  • The factorial n!
Read the full explanation

The Fundamental Principle of Counting has two parts. The multiplication principle: if one event occurs in m ways and another in n ways, together they occur in m x n ways. The addition principle: if either of two exclusive events can occur in m or n ways, the number is m + n. The factorial n! = n(n - 1)(n - 2) ... 1, with 0! = 1. A permutation is an arrangement where order matters: nPr = n!/(n - r)!. A combination is a selection where order does not matter: nCr = n!/(r!(n - r)!), and nPr = r! nCr. Properties: nCr = nC(n-r); nCr + nC(r-1) = (n+1)Cr; nC0 = nCn = 1; nP n = n!. Permutations with repetition: the number of r-letter arrangements from n objects with repetition allowed is n^r. Permutations when some objects are alike: n!/(p! q! r!). Circular permutations: n objects in a circle can be arranged in (n - 1)! ways. Restricted arrangements: treat together items as a single block and multiply by internal arrangements; for items never together subtract the together count from the total; for fixed positions fill those first. Number of 4-digit numbers, words from MATHEMATICS (11 letters with M, A, T repeated twice: 11!/(2!2!2!)) and arrangements of the word INDIA are typical. Selection problems: choosing a committee from men and women uses products of combinations; selecting at least one uses 2^n - 1 total selections; the number of diagonals in an n-sided polygon is nC2 - n; the number of triangles from n points with p collinear is nC3 - pC3. The number of ways to divide into groups uses factorials of group sizes. Handshakes among n people number nC2.

⚖️

Counting principles

  • Use multiplication when tasks are done one after another
  • Use addition when choices are alternatives
  • Break difficult problems into cases
  • Always check whether repetition is allowed
🧠

Permutations

  • NPr counts ordered arrangements of r from n distinct objects
  • When letters repeat divide by the factorials of the repeats
  • For circular tables fix one person to remove rotations
  • For necklaces with reflection divide by 2 further
🌟

Combinations

  • NCr counts committees and selections
  • Multiply combinations for choosing from different groups
  • Use complement counting for at least one
  • Geometry uses nC2 for lines and nC3 for triangles
🧮

Formula tiles

Circular(n-1)!Distinct objects
With repeatsn!/(p!q!r!)Alike items
🎯 Remember Ask first: does order matter? If yes use permutation, otherwise combination.

blocks.x: Coordinate geometry studies figures using coordinates. The distance between (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2). The section formula for a point dividing the join in the ratio m:n internally is ((m x2 + n x1)/(m + n), (m y2 + n y1)/(m + n)); the midpoint is the average of coordinates. The centroid of a triangle is ((x1 + x2 + x3)/3, (y1 + y2 + y3)/3). The area of a triangle is half the modulus of x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2); three points are collinear if this is zero. The slope of a line is m = tan(theta) = (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1), where theta is the angle with the positive x-axis; the x-axis has slope 0 and a vertical line has undefined slope. Parallel lines have equal slopes m1 = m2; perpendicular lines satisfy m1 m2 = -1. The angle between two lines: tan(theta) = |(m1 - m2)/(1 + m1 m2)|. Equations: horizontal line y = b; vertical line x = a; point-slope y - y1 = m(x - x1); two-point form (y - y1) = (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1) (x - x1); slope-intercept y = mx + c; intercept form x/a + y/b = 1; normal form x cos(alpha) + y sin(alpha) = p. The general equation is Ax + By + C = 0 with slope -A/B, x-intercept -C/A and y-intercept -C/B. Distance of the point (x1, y1) from the line Ax + By + C = 0 is |A x1 + B y1 + C|/sqrt(A^2 + B^2). Distance between parallel lines Ax + By + C1 = 0 and Ax + By + C2 = 0 is |C1 - C2|/sqrt(A^2 + B^2). The family of lines through the intersection of L1 = 0 and L2 = 0 is L1 + k L2 = 0. Shifting the origin to (h, k) replaces x by x + h and y by y + k.
Deep dive: Basics
Slope measures steepness. Angles of inclination lie between 0 and 180 degrees. Collinear points have equal slopes between pairs. A line through the origin has no constant term.
Deep dive: Equations

Choose the form from the given data: point and slope, two points, or intercepts. Convert to the general form to compute slope and intercepts. Parallel and perpendicular lines need only a change of the slope or constant.
Deep dive: Distances and families
The perpendicular distance formula is used for heights and for tangents. Parallel lines have a fixed distance. L1 + k L2 = 0 gives all lines through a point of intersection.

🔑

Big idea

  • Coordinate geometry studies figures using coordinates
  • The distance between (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is sqrt((x2 - x1)2 + (y2 - y1)2)
  • The section formula for a point dividing the join in the ratio m:n internally is ((m x2 + n x1)/(m + n), (m y2 + n y1)/(m + n))
  • The midpoint is the average of coordinates
Read the full explanation

Coordinate geometry studies figures using coordinates. The distance between (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2). The section formula for a point dividing the join in the ratio m:n internally is ((m x2 + n x1)/(m + n), (m y2 + n y1)/(m + n)); the midpoint is the average of coordinates. The centroid of a triangle is ((x1 + x2 + x3)/3, (y1 + y2 + y3)/3). The area of a triangle is half the modulus of x1(y2 - y3) + x2(y3 - y1) + x3(y1 - y2); three points are collinear if this is zero. The slope of a line is m = tan(theta) = (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1), where theta is the angle with the positive x-axis; the x-axis has slope 0 and a vertical line has undefined slope. Parallel lines have equal slopes m1 = m2; perpendicular lines satisfy m1 m2 = -1. The angle between two lines: tan(theta) = |(m1 - m2)/(1 + m1 m2)|. Equations: horizontal line y = b; vertical line x = a; point-slope y - y1 = m(x - x1); two-point form (y - y1) = (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1) (x - x1); slope-intercept y = mx + c; intercept form x/a + y/b = 1; normal form x cos(alpha) + y sin(alpha) = p. The general equation is Ax + By + C = 0 with slope -A/B, x-intercept -C/A and y-intercept -C/B. Distance of the point (x1, y1) from the line Ax + By + C = 0 is |A x1 + B y1 + C|/sqrt(A^2 + B^2). Distance between parallel lines Ax + By + C1 = 0 and Ax + By + C2 = 0 is |C1 - C2|/sqrt(A^2 + B^2). The family of lines through the intersection of L1 = 0 and L2 = 0 is L1 + k L2 = 0. Shifting the origin to (h, k) replaces x by x + h and y by y + k.

📘

Basics

  • Slope measures steepness
  • Angles of inclination lie between 0 and 180 degrees
  • Collinear points have equal slopes between pairs
  • A line through the origin has no constant term
🧮

Equations

  • Choose the form from the given data: point and slope, two points, or intercepts
  • Convert to the general form to compute slope and intercepts
  • Parallel and perpendicular lines need only a change of the slope or constant
🌟

Distances and families

  • The perpendicular distance formula is used for heights and for tangents
  • Parallel lines have a fixed distance
  • L1 + k L2 = 0 gives all lines through a point of intersection
🧮

lessons.title: Limits and Derivatives
yt: class 11 maths limits and derivatives first principle standard limits

blocks.x: The limit of f(x) as x approaches a is L, written lim f(x) = L, if f(x) comes arbitrarily close to L as x approaches a from both sides. The limit exists if the left-hand limit equals the right-hand limit. Algebra of limits: the limit of a sum, difference, product and quotient (denominator limit not zero) equals the sum, difference, product and quotient of limits; the limit of a constant is the constant. Evaluating limits: direct substitution; factorising to remove a common factor when the form is 0/0; rationalising when roots appear; for polynomials as x tends to infinity divide by the highest power. Standard limits: lim (x^n - a^n)/(x - a) = n a^(n-1); lim sin x / x = 1 as x tends to 0; lim (1 - cos x)/x = 0; lim tan x / x = 1; lim (e^x - 1)/x = 1; lim log(1 + x)/x = 1; lim (a^x - 1)/x = log a. The derivative of f at x is f'(x) = lim h tends to 0 of [f(x + h) - f(x)]/h, called the first principle. It gives the slope of the tangent and the rate of change. Rules: derivative of a constant is 0; (c f)' = c f'; sum and difference rules; product rule (uv)' = u'v + uv'; quotient rule (u/v)' = (u'v - uv')/v^2. Standard derivatives: d/dx x^n = n x^(n-1); sin x gives cos x; cos x gives -sin x; tan x gives sec^2 x; cot x gives -cosec^2 x; sec x gives sec x tan x; cosec x gives -cosec x cot x; e^x gives e^x; log x gives 1/x. Derivatives are used for slope of tangent, velocity as ds/dt and rate problems. A function that is differentiable at a point is continuous there, but the converse is false.
Deep dive: Limits

Indeterminate forms such as 0/0 need algebra. Left and right limits are checked for piecewise functions. Limits at infinity compare the highest powers. Standard limits are used with substitution to adjust forms.
Deep dive: Derivative from first principles
Write f(x + h) - f(x), divide by h and take the limit. For x^n the binomial expansion gives n x^(n-1). The derivative is slope of tangent at the point.
Deep dive: Rules and meaning
Product and quotient rules combine standard derivatives. Velocity is the derivative of position. A sharp corner like |x| at 0 is continuous but not differentiable.
Hindi saransh
Seema aur avkalan: avkalaj f'(x) = lim [f(x+h) - f(x)]/h; sin x / x ka seema 1 hota hai.
Always try direct substitution first; use algebra only if you get 0/0.

Visual lesson

Limits and Derivatives

The limit of f(x) as x approaches a is L, written lim f(x) = L, if f(x) comes arbitrarily close to L as x approaches a from both sides

1Big idea›2Limits›3Derivative from first…›4Rules and meaning
x^nn x^(n-1)
sin x / x1
Quotient rule(u'v - uv')/v^2
🔑

Big idea

  • The limit of f(x) as x approaches a is L, written lim f(x) = L, if f(x) comes arbitrarily close to L as x approaches a from both sides
  • The limit exists if the left-hand limit equals the right-hand limit
  • Algebra of limits: the limit of a sum, difference, product and quotient (denominator limit not zero) equals the sum, difference, product and quotient…
  • The limit of a constant is the constant
Read the full explanation

The limit of f(x) as x approaches a is L, written lim f(x) = L, if f(x) comes arbitrarily close to L as x approaches a from both sides. The limit exists if the left-hand limit equals the right-hand limit. Algebra of limits: the limit of a sum, difference, product and quotient (denominator limit not zero) equals the sum, difference, product and quotient of limits; the limit of a constant is the constant. Evaluating limits: direct substitution; factorising to remove a common factor when the form is 0/0; rationalising when roots appear; for polynomials as x tends to infinity divide by the highest power. Standard limits: lim (x^n - a^n)/(x - a) = n a^(n-1); lim sin x / x = 1 as x tends to 0; lim (1 - cos x)/x = 0; lim tan x / x = 1; lim (e^x - 1)/x = 1; lim log(1 + x)/x = 1; lim (a^x - 1)/x = log a. The derivative of f at x is f'(x) = lim h tends to 0 of [f(x + h) - f(x)]/h, called the first principle. It gives the slope of the tangent and the rate of change. Rules: derivative of a constant is 0; (c f)' = c f'; sum and difference rules; product rule (uv)' = u'v + uv'; quotient rule (u/v)' = (u'v - uv')/v^2. Standard derivatives: d/dx x^n = n x^(n-1); sin x gives cos x; cos x gives -sin x; tan x gives sec^2 x; cot x gives -cosec^2 x; sec x gives sec x tan x; cosec x gives -cosec x cot x; e^x gives e^x; log x gives 1/x. Derivatives are used for slope of tangent, velocity as ds/dt and rate problems. A function that is differentiable at a point is continuous there, but the converse is false.

📌

Limits

  • Indeterminate forms such as 0/0 need algebra
  • Left and right limits are checked for piecewise functions
  • Limits at infinity compare the highest powers
  • Standard limits are used with substitution to adjust forms
⚖️

Derivative from first principles

  • Write f(x + h) - f(x), divide by h and take the limit
  • For x^n the binomial expansion gives n x^(n-1)
  • The derivative is slope of tangent at the point
📘

Rules and meaning

  • Product and quotient rules combine standard derivatives
  • Velocity is the derivative of position
  • A sharp corner like |x| at 0 is continuous but not differentiable
🧮

lessons.title: Statistics: measures of dispersion
yt: class 11 statistics measures of dispersion

blocks.x: Range, mean deviation, variance and standard deviation measure how spread out data are. Variance = (1/n) sum (x - mean)^2, standard deviation is its square root, and coefficient of variation = (s / mean) x 100.
Deep dive: measures of dispersion

Range = largest - smallest. Mean deviation about the mean = sum |x - mean| / n; about the median = sum |x - M| / n. Variance sigma^2 = sum (x - mean)^2 / n = (sum x^2)/n - mean^2. Standard deviation sigma = sqrt (variance). For a frequency table: sigma^2 = sum f (x - mean)^2 / N, N = sum f. For continuous data use class marks as x. Coefficient of variation CV = (sigma / mean) x 100 compares the variability of two series: the series with smaller CV is more consistent.
Deep dive: effect of change of origin and scale

If every value is increased by a constant, the mean increases by it but the variance and SD stay the same. If every value is multiplied by k, the mean and SD are multiplied by |k| and the variance by k^2. For a combined group of n1 and n2 items with means m1, m2, the combined mean is (n1 m1 + n2 m2)/(n1 + n2). The shortcut method: with a assumed mean, sigma^2 = (sum f d^2)/N - (sum f d / N)^2 where d = x - a. **Common mistakes:** dividing by n - 1 (not used in this syllabus), forgetting the square root, and comparing variability using SD instead of CV when the means differ.

lessons.title: Changing Trends and Career in Physical Education
yt: class 11 physical education changing trends career meaning aims khelo india fit india

blocks.x: Physical Education is education through physical activity for the all-round development of the individual: physical, mental, social and emotional. Its aims are to develop physical fitness, skills, healthy attitudes and character, and its objectives include physical development, mental development, social development, emotional development, and development of leadership and fair play. Evolution: in ancient Greece physical training was central, and the first ancient Olympic Games were held in 776 BCE at Olympia; the modern Olympic Games began in 1896 at Athens through the efforts of Pierre de Coubertin. In India the Asian Games were first held at New Delhi in 1951 and the Commonwealth Games at Delhi in 2010. Sports in India are promoted by the Sports Authority of India (SAI), the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, the Indian Olympic Association (founded 1927) and national federations. Government initiatives include Khelo India (launched 2018 to build a strong sports culture), the Fit India Movement (launched on 29 August 2019 on National Sports Day) and the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS). National Sports Day is observed on 29 August, the birthday of hockey wizard Major Dhyan Chand. Awards include the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award, Arjuna Award, Dronacharya Award and Dhyan Chand Award. Career options include physical education teacher, coach, sports administrator, sports journalist, sports psychologist, sports medicine doctor, physiotherapist, fitness trainer, referee or umpire, sports nutritionist and sports manager. Changing trends include use of technology, wearable devices, sports science, professional leagues, inclusive sports, health and wellness focus, and global competition. Adaptive PE and recreation expanded; yoga and fitness became part of the school curriculum, and National Education Policy 2020 stresses sports integration.
Deep dive: Aims and objectives

Aims are the general purposes; objectives are specific results. Physical education builds the body, mind and character. It teaches co-operation, discipline and sportsmanship. It promotes healthy living and leisure use.
Deep dive: Trends

Technology, analytics and sports science now guide training. Professional leagues and private academies have grown. Women participation has increased. Fitness is linked to well-being and prevention of lifestyle disease.
Deep dive: Careers
Careers are in teaching, coaching, sports medicine, media, management and fitness industry. Qualifications include B.P.Ed, M.P.Ed and NIS diplomas from Patiala. SAI centres train athletes.

Sharirik shiksha sampoorn vikas ka madhyam hai; Khelo India, Fit India aur kai career vikalp isse jude hain.
Remember: National Sports Day 29 August; Fit India launched 2019; Khelo India 2018.

Big idea

  • Physical Education is education through physical activity for the all-round development of the individual: physical, mental, social and emotional

Read the full explanation

Physical Education is education through physical activity for the all-round development of the individual: physical, mental, social and emotional. Its aims are to develop physical fitness, skills, healthy attitudes and character, and its objectives include physical development, mental development, social development, emotional development, and development of leadership and fair play. Evolution: in ancient Greece physical training was central, and the first ancient Olympic Games were held in 776 BCE at Olympia; the modern Olympic Games began in 1896 at Athens through the efforts of Pierre de Coubertin. In India the Asian Games were first held at New Delhi in 1951 and the Commonwealth Games at Delhi in 2010. Sports in India are promoted by the Sports Authority of India (SAI), the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, the Indian Olympic Association (founded 1927) and national federations. Government initiatives include Khelo India (launched 2018 to build a strong sports culture), the Fit India Movement (launched on 29 August 2019 on National Sports Day) and the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS). National Sports Day is observed on 29 August, the birthday of hockey wizard Major Dhyan Chand. Awards include the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award, Arjuna Award, Dronacharya Award and Dhyan Chand Award. Career options include physical education teacher, coach, sports administrator, sports journalist, sports psychologist, sports medicine doctor, physiotherapist, fitness trainer, referee or umpire, sports nutritionist and sports manager. Changing trends include use of technology, wearable devices, sports science, professional leagues, inclusive sports, health and wellness focus, and global competition. Adaptive PE and recreation expanded; yoga and fitness became part of the school curriculum, and National Education Policy 2020 stresses sports integration.

📌

Aims and objectives

  • Aims are the general purposes
  • Objectives are specific results
  • Physical education builds the body, mind and character
  • It teaches co-operation, discipline and sportsmanship
Read the full explanation

Aims are the general purposes; objectives are specific results. Physical education builds the body, mind and character. It teaches co-operation, discipline and sportsmanship. It promotes healthy living and leisure use.

🧠

Trends

  • Technology, analytics and sports science now guide training
  • Professional leagues and private academies have grown
  • Women participation has increased
  • Fitness is linked to well-being and prevention of lifestyle disease
🌟

Careers

  • Careers are in teaching, coaching, sports medicine, media, management and fitness industry
  • Qualifications include B.P.Ed, M.P.Ed and NIS diplomas from Patiala
  • SAI centres train athletes
🎯 Remember National Sports Day 29 August; Fit India launched 2019; Khelo India 2018.

lessons.title: Olympic Value Education
yt: class 11 physical education olympic value education olympism rings paralympics

blocks.x: Olympism is a philosophy of life that blends sport with culture and education, promoting harmony and respect. Olympic Value Education (OVE) teaches the values of the Olympic Movement: joy of effort, fair play, respect for others, pursuit of excellence, and balance between body, will and mind. The International Olympic Committee (IOC) was founded in 1894 by Pierre de Coubertin and is headquartered at Lausanne, Switzerland. The ancient Olympic Games were held every four years at Olympia in honour of Zeus and were banned about 393 CE by Emperor Theodosius. The first modern Games were held in 1896 at Athens. The Olympic motto is Citius, Altius, Fortius (faster, higher, stronger), to which Communiter (together) was added in 2021. The Olympic symbol consists of five interlocking rings (blue, yellow, black, green and red) on a white background, representing the union of five continents; the Olympic flag was introduced in 1914 and first flown in 1920 at Antwerp. The Olympic flame is lit at Olympia and carried by a torch relay to the host city; the torch relay began in 1936. The Olympic oath is taken by an athlete at the opening ceremony. The Olympic Charter is the codification of fundamental principles. The Winter Olympics began in 1924 at Chamonix. The Youth Olympic Games began in 2010 at Singapore. The Paralympic Games, begun by Ludwig Guttmann, were first held in Rome in 1960; the Special Olympics were founded by Eunice Kennedy Shriver in 1968; the Deaflympics began in Paris in 1924. India's Olympic history: Norman Pritchard won two silver medals in 1900, the Indian hockey team won gold in 1928 at Amsterdam, K D Jadhav won independent India's first individual medal (bronze) in 1952, Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual gold in shooting in 2008 at Beijing, and Neeraj Chopra won gold in javelin in 2021 at Tokyo. Values are applied in school: fair play, respect and excellence in sports. The Olympic Games are held every four years, and the cycle is called an Olympiad.
Deep dive: Olympism and values

Olympism puts sport at the service of humanity. OVE educates through joy of effort, fair play, respect, excellence and balance. It builds character, tolerance and international understanding. Olympic ideals fight discrimination.
Deep dive: Symbols and ceremonies
Rings, flag, flame, motto, oath, anthem and mascots are Olympic symbols. Ceremonies include the opening with the parade of nations and the closing ceremony. Medals are gold, silver and bronze.
Deep dive: Other Games and India

The Paralympics, Special Olympics and Deaflympics give opportunities to persons with disabilities. The IOA organises India's participation. The Olympic Games are the biggest sports event in the world.

Big idea

Read the full explanation

Olympism is a philosophy of life that blends sport with culture and education, promoting harmony and respect. Olympic Value Education (OVE) teaches the values of the Olympic Movement: joy of effort, fair play, respect for others, pursuit of excellence, and balance between body, will and mind. The International Olympic Committee (IOC) was founded in 1894 by Pierre de Coubertin and is headquartered at Lausanne, Switzerland. The ancient Olympic Games were held every four years at Olympia in honour of Zeus and were banned about 393 CE by Emperor Theodosius. The first modern Games were held in 1896 at Athens. The Olympic motto is Citius, Altius, Fortius (faster, higher, stronger), to which Communiter (together) was added in 2021. The Olympic symbol consists of five interlocking rings (blue, yellow, black, green and red) on a white background, representing the union of five continents; the Olympic flag was introduced in 1914 and first flown in 1920 at Antwerp. The Olympic flame is lit at Olympia and carried by a torch relay to the host city; the torch relay began in 1936. The Olympic oath is taken by an athlete at the opening ceremony. The Olympic Charter is the codification of fundamental principles. The Winter Olympics began in 1924 at Chamonix. The Youth Olympic Games began in 2010 at Singapore. The Paralympic Games, begun by Ludwig Guttmann, were first held in Rome in 1960; the Special Olympics were founded by Eunice Kennedy Shriver in 1968; the Deaflympics began in Paris in 1924. India's Olympic history: Norman Pritchard won two silver medals in 1900, the Indian hockey team won gold in 1928 at Amsterdam, K D Jadhav won independent India's first individual medal (bronze) in 1952, Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual gold in shooting in 2008 at Beijing, and Neeraj Chopra won gold in javelin in 2021 at Tokyo. Values are applied in school: fair play, respect and excellence in sports. The Olympic Games are held every four years, and the cycle is called an Olympiad.

📌

Olympism and values

  • Olympism puts sport at the service of humanity
  • OVE educates through joy of effort, fair play, respect, excellence and balance
  • It builds character, tolerance and international understanding
  • Olympic ideals fight discrimination
🧠

Symbols and ceremonies

  • Rings, flag, flame, motto, oath, anthem and mascots are Olympic symbols
  • Ceremonies include the opening with the parade of nations and the closing ceremony
  • Medals are gold, silver and bronze
🌟

Other Games and India

  • The Paralympics, Special Olympics and Deaflympics give opportunities to persons with disabilities
  • The IOA organises India's participation
  • The Olympic Games are the biggest sports event in the world

blocks.x: The word yoga comes from the Sanskrit root yuj, meaning to join or unite the individual self with the universal self. Patanjali, in his Yoga Sutras, defined yoga as the stilling of the fluctuations of the mind. The eight limbs (Ashtanga Yoga) of Patanjali are Yama (restraints), Niyama (observances), Asana (postures), Pranayama (breath control), Pratyahara (withdrawal of senses), Dharana (concentration), Dhyana (meditation) and Samadhi (absorption). The five yamas are ahimsa, satya, asteya, brahmacharya and aparigraha; the five niyamas are shaucha, santosha, tapas, svadhyaya and ishvara pranidhana. Types of yoga include Jnana yoga (knowledge), Bhakti yoga (devotion), Karma yoga (selfless action), Raja yoga (mind control) and Hatha yoga. Asanas are classified as standing (Tadasana, Vrikshasana, Trikonasana, Ardha Chakrasana, Padahastasana), sitting (Vajrasana, Padmasana, Sukhasana, Ardha Matsyendrasana, Paschimottanasana, Gomukhasana), prone (Bhujangasana, Shalabhasana, Dhanurasana, Makarasana) and supine (Shavasana, Setubandhasana, Halasana, Sarvangasana, Matsyasana, Naukasana). Benefits: Tadasana improves posture; Bhujangasana strengthens the back; Vajrasana helps digestion and can be done after meals; Shavasana relaxes. Pranayama has three stages: puraka (inhalation), kumbhaka (retention) and rechaka (exhalation). Types: Anulom-Vilom (alternate nostril breathing), Kapalabhati, Bhastrika, Bhramari, Ujjayi, Sheetali and Sheetkari. The six cleansing techniques (Shatkarma) are Neti, Dhauti, Nauli, Basti, Kapalabhati and Trataka. Meditation is concentration of the mind. Guidelines: practise on an empty stomach, in a clean airy place, on a mat, in comfortable clothes, and not when ill. International Day of Yoga is observed on 21 June, proposed by India's Prime Minister and adopted by the UN General Assembly in 2014; the first was observed in 2015. Yoga helps reduce stress and improves flexibility and concentration. The Ministry of AYUSH promotes yoga and the common yoga protocol is practised by many.
Deep dive: Yoga and its limbs
Yoga unites body, mind and spirit. Patanjali's eight limbs form a path from ethics to liberation. Yama and niyama are the moral foundation. Asana and pranayama train body and breath.
Deep dive: Asanas

Each asana has a method, benefit and precaution. Standing asanas improve balance and posture. Sitting asanas help flexibility and meditation. Prone and supine asanas strengthen the back and relax the body.
Deep dive: Pranayama and cleansing

Breath control calms the mind. Anulom-Vilom balances the breath through both nostrils. Kapalabhati is rapid exhalation. Shatkarma purify the body. Precautions: avoid strain and practise under guidance.

Read the full explanation

The word yoga comes from the Sanskrit root yuj, meaning to join or unite the individual self with the universal self. Patanjali, in his Yoga Sutras, defined yoga as the stilling of the fluctuations of the mind. The eight limbs (Ashtanga Yoga) of Patanjali are Yama (restraints), Niyama (observances), Asana (postures), Pranayama (breath control), Pratyahara (withdrawal of senses), Dharana (concentration), Dhyana (meditation) and Samadhi (absorption). The five yamas are ahimsa, satya, asteya, brahmacharya and aparigraha; the five niyamas are shaucha, santosha, tapas, svadhyaya and ishvara pranidhana. Types of yoga include Jnana yoga (knowledge), Bhakti yoga (devotion), Karma yoga (selfless action), Raja yoga (mind control) and Hatha yoga. Asanas are classified as standing (Tadasana, Vrikshasana, Trikonasana, Ardha Chakrasana, Padahastasana), sitting (Vajrasana, Padmasana, Sukhasana, Ardha Matsyendrasana, Paschimottanasana, Gomukhasana), prone (Bhujangasana, Shalabhasana, Dhanurasana, Makarasana) and supine (Shavasana, Setubandhasana, Halasana, Sarvangasana, Matsyasana, Naukasana). Benefits: Tadasana improves posture; Bhujangasana strengthens the back; Vajrasana helps digestion and can be done after meals; Shavasana relaxes. Pranayama has three stages: puraka (inhalation), kumbhaka (retention) and rechaka (exhalation). Types: Anulom-Vilom (alternate nostril breathing), Kapalabhati, Bhastrika, Bhramari, Ujjayi, Sheetali and Sheetkari. The six cleansing techniques (Shatkarma) are Neti, Dhauti, Nauli, Basti, Kapalabhati and Trataka. Meditation is concentration of the mind. Guidelines: practise on an empty stomach, in a clean airy place, on a mat, in comfortable clothes, and not when ill. International Day of Yoga is observed on 21 June, proposed by India's Prime Minister and adopted by the UN General Assembly in 2014; the first was observed in 2015. Yoga helps reduce stress and improves flexibility and concentration. The Ministry of AYUSH promotes yoga and the common yoga protocol is practised by many.

📌

Yoga and its limbs

  • Yoga unites body, mind and spirit
  • Patanjali's eight limbs form a path from ethics to liberation
  • Yama and niyama are the moral foundation
  • Asana and pranayama train body and breath
🧠

Asanas

  • Each asana has a method, benefit and precaution
  • Standing asanas improve balance and posture
  • Sitting asanas help flexibility and meditation
  • Prone and supine asanas strengthen the back and relax the body
🌟

Pranayama and cleansing

  • Breath control calms the mind
  • Anulom-Vilom balances the breath through both nostrils
  • Kapalabhati is rapid exhalation
  • Shatkarma purify the body

Breath control calms the mind. Anulom-Vilom balances the breath through both nostrils. Kapalabhati is rapid exhalation. Shatkarma purify the body. Precautions: avoid strain and practise under guidance.

lessons.title: Physical Education and Sports for CWSN
yt: class 11 physical education sports for children with special needs disability inclusion paralympics

blocks.x: CWSN means Children With Special Needs. Disability is a condition that limits a person's physical, sensory or mental functions. The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (RPwD Act) recognises 21 disabilities and replaced the 1995 Act. Types of disability: locomotor disability (limited movement of limbs, as in cerebral palsy or amputation), visual impairment (blindness and low vision), hearing impairment (deaf and hard of hearing), intellectual disability (low intelligence quotient and adaptive skills), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), specific learning disabilities (dyslexia, dysgraphia, dyscalculia), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and cerebral palsy. Causes include heredity, birth complications, accidents, diseases and malnutrition. Concepts: inclusion (all children learn together with support), integration, segregation and adaptive physical education, which modifies activities for the needs of the child. Aims of adaptive PE: improve fitness, build confidence, develop social skills, reduce dependence and give a sense of achievement. Strategies: use simple clear instructions, modify rules, equipment and space, provide assistive devices, use peer help, offer individual attention, set achievable goals and give positive reinforcement. Sports organisations: the Paralympic Games (first held in Rome, 1960; Sir Ludwig Guttmann), Special Olympics (founded 1968 by Eunice Kennedy Shriver; for intellectual disability) and the Deaflympics (first held 1924 in Paris). In India the Paralympic Committee of India and Special Olympics Bharat promote these sports. Indian para-athletes include Devendra Jhajharia (javelin), Deepa Malik (shot put, silver in 2016), Mariyappan Thangavelu (high jump, gold 2016) and Avani Lekhara (shooting, gold 2020). Role of the teacher: identify the need, plan activities, ensure safety, motivate and encourage participation. Barriers: negative attitudes, lack of facilities, lack of trained teachers and inaccessible buildings. Children with special needs have the right to education and sports under the Right to Education Act and the RPwD Act. Posture and fitness of CWSN can be improved by exercise, and physical activity helps their mental health.
Deep dive: Types and causes
Locomotor, visual, hearing, intellectual, autism, learning disabilities and ADHD each need different support. Early identification helps. Causes may be before, during or after birth.
Deep dive: Inclusion and adaptive PE
Inclusion gives equal opportunity. Adaptive PE modifies rules, equipment and goals. The teacher uses demonstration, touch cues, signs and extra time as needed. Safety and encouragement are vital.
Deep dive: Sports and law

The Paralympics are for physical disabilities; Special Olympics for intellectual disabilities; Deaflympics for hearing impaired athletes. The RPwD Act 2016 recognises 21 disabilities and promotes inclusive education and sports.

CWSN means Children With Special Needs

Read the full explanation

CWSN means Children With Special Needs. Disability is a condition that limits a person's physical, sensory or mental functions. The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 (RPwD Act) recognises 21 disabilities and replaced the 1995 Act. Types of disability: locomotor disability (limited movement of limbs, as in cerebral palsy or amputation), visual impairment (blindness and low vision), hearing impairment (deaf and hard of hearing), intellectual disability (low intelligence quotient and adaptive skills), autism spectrum disorder (ASD), specific learning disabilities (dyslexia, dysgraphia, dyscalculia), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and cerebral palsy. Causes include heredity, birth complications, accidents, diseases and malnutrition. Concepts: inclusion (all children learn together with support), integration, segregation and adaptive physical education, which modifies activities for the needs of the child. Aims of adaptive PE: improve fitness, build confidence, develop social skills, reduce dependence and give a sense of achievement. Strategies: use simple clear instructions, modify rules, equipment and space, provide assistive devices, use peer help, offer individual attention, set achievable goals and give positive reinforcement. Sports organisations: the Paralympic Games (first held in Rome, 1960; Sir Ludwig Guttmann), Special Olympics (founded 1968 by Eunice Kennedy Shriver; for intellectual disability) and the Deaflympics (first held 1924 in Paris). In India the Paralympic Committee of India and Special Olympics Bharat promote these sports. Indian para-athletes include Devendra Jhajharia (javelin), Deepa Malik (shot put, silver in 2016), Mariyappan Thangavelu (high jump, gold 2016) and Avani Lekhara (shooting, gold 2020). Role of the teacher: identify the need, plan activities, ensure safety, motivate and encourage participation. Barriers: negative attitudes, lack of facilities, lack of trained teachers and inaccessible buildings. Children with special needs have the right to education and sports under the Right to Education Act and the RPwD Act. Posture and fitness of CWSN can be improved by exercise, and physical activity helps their mental health.

💡

Types and causes

  • Locomotor, visual, hearing, intellectual, autism, learning disabilities and ADHD each need different support
  • Early identification helps
  • Causes may be before, during or after birth
🧠

Inclusion and adaptive PE

  • Inclusion gives equal opportunity
  • Adaptive PE modifies rules, equipment and goals
  • The teacher uses demonstration, touch cues, signs and extra time as needed
  • Safety and encouragement are vital
⚖️

Sports and law

  • The Paralympics are for physical disabilities
  • Special Olympics for intellectual disabilities
  • Deaflympics for hearing impaired athletes
  • The RPwD Act 2016 recognises 21 disabilities and promotes inclusive education and sports

lessons.title: Physical Fitness, Wellness and Lifestyle
yt: class 11 physical education physical fitness wellness lifestyle components nutrition posture

blocks.x: Physical fitness is the ability to carry out daily tasks vigorously and alertly without undue fatigue and with energy left for leisure. Health-related fitness components are cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility and body composition. Skill-related components are agility, balance, coordination, power, speed and reaction time. Wellness is a state of positive health involving physical, mental, social, emotional, spiritual, environmental, occupational and intellectual dimensions; health is not only the absence of disease but complete physical, mental and social well-being (WHO). Lifestyle is the way a person lives. A sedentary lifestyle leads to hypokinetic diseases such as obesity, diabetes, hypertension, heart disease and back pain. Active lifestyle includes regular exercise, balanced diet, adequate sleep, stress management and avoiding tobacco, alcohol and drugs. Body composition is measured by Body Mass Index (BMI = weight in kg divided by height in m squared); normal BMI is about 18.5 to 24.9. Nutrition: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water and fibre; a balanced diet gives all in right proportion. Carbohydrates and fats provide energy, proteins build tissues, vitamins and minerals regulate body functions. Postural deformities include kyphosis (rounded upper back), lordosis (inward curve of lower back), scoliosis (sideways curve), flat foot, knock knees, bow legs and round shoulders; corrective exercises and good posture help. Sports and games develop fitness and self-confidence. Yoga and relaxation reduce stress. Obesity is excess body fat causing health problems; regular exercise and diet control help. Sports persons need more energy and protein. Physical activity guidelines recommend at least 60 minutes of moderate to vigorous activity daily for children.
Deep dive: Fitness

Health-related fitness is needed by everyone; skill-related fitness by athletes. Cardiovascular endurance is the capacity of the heart and lungs to supply oxygen. Strength is the force a muscle can exert. Flexibility is the range of motion at a joint.
Deep dive: Wellness and lifestyle
Wellness is a multi-dimensional balance. Lifestyle diseases are caused by inactivity, poor diet and stress. Healthy habits prevent them. Sleep of 7 to 9 hours helps recovery.
Deep dive: Nutrition and posture
Balanced diet provides all nutrients. Water is vital. Postural deformities can be corrected by exercise and awareness. Good posture reduces strain on muscles and bones.

Sharirik kshamta, swasthya aur jeevanshaili: niyamit vyayam, santulit aahar aur sahi mudra se rogon se bachav hota hai.

Visual lesson

Physical Fitness, Wellness and Lifestyle

Physical fitness is the ability to carry out daily tasks vigorously and alertly without undue fatigue and with energy left for leisure

🔑

Big idea

  • Physical fitness is the ability to carry out daily tasks vigorously and alertly without undue fatigue and with energy left for leisure
  • Health-related fitness components are cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility and body composition
  • Skill-related components are agility, balance, coordination, power, speed and reaction time
  • Wellness is a state of positive health involving physical, mental, social, emotional, spiritual, environmental, occupational and intellectual…
Read the full explanation

Physical fitness is the ability to carry out daily tasks vigorously and alertly without undue fatigue and with energy left for leisure. Health-related fitness components are cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility and body composition. Skill-related components are agility, balance, coordination, power, speed and reaction time. Wellness is a state of positive health involving physical, mental, social, emotional, spiritual, environmental, occupational and intellectual dimensions; health is not only the absence of disease but complete physical, mental and social well-being (WHO). Lifestyle is the way a person lives. A sedentary lifestyle leads to hypokinetic diseases such as obesity, diabetes, hypertension, heart disease and back pain. Active lifestyle includes regular exercise, balanced diet, adequate sleep, stress management and avoiding tobacco, alcohol and drugs. Body composition is measured by Body Mass Index (BMI = weight in kg divided by height in m squared); normal BMI is about 18.5 to 24.9. Nutrition: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water and fibre; a balanced diet gives all in right proportion. Carbohydrates and fats provide energy, proteins build tissues, vitamins and minerals regulate body functions. Postural deformities include kyphosis (rounded upper back), lordosis (inward curve of lower back), scoliosis (sideways curve), flat foot, knock knees, bow legs and round shoulders; corrective exercises and good posture help. Sports and games develop fitness and self-confidence. Yoga and relaxation reduce stress. Obesity is excess body fat causing health problems; regular exercise and diet control help. Sports persons need more energy and protein. Physical activity guidelines recommend at least 60 minutes of moderate to vigorous activity daily for children.

📌

  • Health-related fitness is needed by everyone
  • Skill-related fitness by athletes
  • Cardiovascular endurance is the capacity of the heart and lungs to supply oxygen
  • Strength is the force a muscle can exert

Health-related fitness is needed by everyone; skill-related fitness by athletes. Cardiovascular endurance is the capacity of the heart and lungs to supply oxygen. Strength is the force a muscle can exert. Flexibility is the range of motion at a joint.

Wellness and lifestyle

  • Wellness is a multi-dimensional balance
  • Lifestyle diseases are caused by inactivity, poor diet and stress
  • Healthy habits prevent them
  • Sleep of 7 to 9 hours helps recovery
🌟

Nutrition and posture

  • Balanced diet provides all nutrients
  • Water is vital
  • Postural deformities can be corrected by exercise and awareness
  • Good posture reduces strain on muscles and bones

lessons.title: Test and Measurement in Sports
yt: class 11 physical education test measurement evaluation harvard step test rockport barrow

blocks.x: A test is a tool or procedure used to collect information about a quality; measurement is the process of collecting numerical data using a test; evaluation is interpreting the data to judge progress or worth. Tests should be valid (measure what they intend to), reliable (give consistent results), objective (free of personal bias), norms-based and practical. Importance: to select talent, classify students, assess progress, motivate and plan training. Fitness tests include the 50 m dash for speed, the standing broad jump for explosive leg power, sit and reach for flexibility, sit-ups or partial curl-ups for abdominal strength, push-ups for upper body endurance and the 600 m run or walk for cardiovascular endurance. The Harvard Step Test measures cardiovascular fitness: a subject steps up and down on a bench (20 inches high for boys and 18 inches for girls) 30 times per minute for 5 minutes to a metronome set at 120 beats per minute, then sits and pulse is counted at 1 to 1.5, 2 to 2.5 and 3 to 3.5 minutes. Fitness Index = duration of exercise in seconds x 100 divided by 2 x sum of the three pulse counts. The Rockport One-Mile Walk test estimates VO2 max by timing a one-mile walk and measuring heart rate at the end. The Barrow Three-Item General Motor Ability test uses standing broad jump, zig-zag run and medicine ball put. The Johnson-Metheny test measures motor ability. The Rikli and Jones Senior Citizen Fitness Test has chair stand, arm curl, 6-minute walk or 2-minute step, chair sit-and-reach, back scratch and 8-foot up-and-go. Kraus-Weber tests measure minimum muscular fitness. Khelo India Fitness assessment includes BMI, flexibility, strength, endurance and speed tests. Evaluation uses norms, percentiles and ratings. Test administration needs warm-up, clear instructions, safety, trained testers and recorded results.
Deep dive: Concepts
Test, measurement and evaluation are linked. A good test is valid, reliable and objective. Norms help compare scores. Records help track progress.
Deep dive: Harvard step test

It measures the recovery of the pulse after stepping. A higher fitness index means better cardiovascular fitness. Rating: below 55 poor; 55 to 64 low average; 65 to 79 high average; 80 to 89 good; 90 and above excellent.
Deep dive: Other tests
Barrow tests general motor ability. Rockport estimates aerobic capacity. Rikli and Jones tests help the elderly. Kraus-Weber checks minimum fitness. Each has specific items and scoring.
Hindi saransh
Test, mapan aur mulyankan: Harvard step test se hriday-shwasan kshamta aur Barrow test se motor kshamta ka mapan hota hai.
Remember Fitness Index = (100 x seconds) / (2 x sum of pulse counts).

Test and Measurement in Sports

A test is a tool or procedure used to collect information about a quality

🔑

Big idea

  • A test is a tool or procedure used to collect information about a quality
  • Measurement is the process of collecting numerical data using a test
  • Evaluation is interpreting the data to judge progress or worth
  • Tests should be valid (measure what they intend to), reliable (give consistent results), objective (free of personal bias), norms-based and practical
Read the full explanation

A test is a tool or procedure used to collect information about a quality; measurement is the process of collecting numerical data using a test; evaluation is interpreting the data to judge progress or worth. Tests should be valid (measure what they intend to), reliable (give consistent results), objective (free of personal bias), norms-based and practical. Importance: to select talent, classify students, assess progress, motivate and plan training. Fitness tests include the 50 m dash for speed, the standing broad jump for explosive leg power, sit and reach for flexibility, sit-ups or partial curl-ups for abdominal strength, push-ups for upper body endurance and the 600 m run or walk for cardiovascular endurance. The Harvard Step Test measures cardiovascular fitness: a subject steps up and down on a bench (20 inches high for boys and 18 inches for girls) 30 times per minute for 5 minutes to a metronome set at 120 beats per minute, then sits and pulse is counted at 1 to 1.5, 2 to 2.5 and 3 to 3.5 minutes. Fitness Index = duration of exercise in seconds x 100 divided by 2 x sum of the three pulse counts. The Rockport One-Mile Walk test estimates VO2 max by timing a one-mile walk and measuring heart rate at the end. The Barrow Three-Item General Motor Ability test uses standing broad jump, zig-zag run and medicine ball put. The Johnson-Metheny test measures motor ability. The Rikli and Jones Senior Citizen Fitness Test has chair stand, arm curl, 6-minute walk or 2-minute step, chair sit-and-reach, back scratch and 8-foot up-and-go. Kraus-Weber tests measure minimum muscular fitness. Khelo India Fitness assessment includes BMI, flexibility, strength, endurance and speed tests. Evaluation uses norms, percentiles and ratings. Test administration needs warm-up, clear instructions, safety, trained testers and recorded results.

📘

Concepts

  • Test, measurement and evaluation are linked
  • A good test is valid, reliable and objective
  • Norms help compare scores
  • Records help track progress
🔄

Harvard step test

  • It measures the recovery of the pulse after stepping
  • A higher fitness index means better cardiovascular fitness
  • Rating: below 55 poor
  • 55 to 64 low average
Read the full explanation

It measures the recovery of the pulse after stepping. A higher fitness index means better cardiovascular fitness. Rating: below 55 poor; 55 to 64 low average; 65 to 79 high average; 80 to 89 good; 90 and above excellent.

🌟

Other tests

  • Barrow tests general motor ability
  • Rockport estimates aerobic capacity
  • Rikli and Jones tests help the elderly
  • Kraus-Weber checks minimum fitness
Read the full explanation

Barrow tests general motor ability. Rockport estimates aerobic capacity. Rikli and Jones tests help the elderly. Kraus-Weber checks minimum fitness. Each has specific items and scoring.

blocks.x: Anatomy is the study of the structure of the body and physiology is the study of its functions. The skeletal system has 206 bones in an adult: 80 in the axial skeleton (skull, vertebral column, ribs, sternum) and 126 in the appendicular skeleton (limbs and girdles). Bones are long (femur), short (carpals), flat (skull, ribs) and irregular (vertebrae). Functions of the skeleton: support, protection, movement, storage of minerals and production of blood cells in the bone marrow. A joint is where two bones meet; types are fixed (skull), slightly movable (vertebrae) and freely movable or synovial joints such as ball and socket (shoulder, hip), hinge (elbow, knee), pivot (neck), gliding (wrist), saddle (thumb) and condyloid. Muscles are of three types: skeletal (voluntary, striated), smooth (involuntary, in organs) and cardiac (involuntary, in heart). The human body has more than 600 muscles. Skeletal muscle fibres are slow twitch (red, endurance) and fast twitch (white, power). Muscle contraction can be isotonic or isometric. The circulatory system consists of the heart, blood and blood vessels. The heart has four chambers: right and left atria and right and left ventricles. Arteries carry blood away from the heart, veins carry blood towards it and capillaries exchange materials. Blood contains plasma, red blood cells (carry oxygen with haemoglobin), white blood cells (defence) and platelets (clotting). Normal resting heart rate is about 72 beats per minute; trained athletes have lower rates. Stroke volume is the blood pumped per beat and cardiac output equals stroke volume times heart rate. The respiratory system includes the nose, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi and lungs; gas exchange occurs in the alveoli. Tidal volume is about 500 ml. Vital capacity is the maximum air exhaled after maximum inhalation. Exercise effects: it strengthens muscles and bones, increases stroke volume and cardiac output, lowers resting heart rate, improves lung capacity, helps digestion and improves mood. Oxygen debt arises during heavy exercise when oxygen supply is less than demand.
Deep dive: Skeletal system
Bones give shape and protection. Red bone marrow makes blood cells. Joints allow different movement. Cartilage covers joint surfaces and ligaments join bone to bone while tendons join muscle to bone.
Deep dive: Muscular and circulatory

Skeletal muscles move bones. Slow-twitch fibres suit long-distance events; fast-twitch suit sprints. The heart pumps blood in a double circulation: pulmonary and systemic. Blood carries oxygen, nutrients and wastes.
Deep dive: Respiratory system and exercise
Inhaled air reaches alveoli where oxygen diffuses into blood. Regular exercise improves vital capacity and the efficiency of the heart. Athletes show bradycardia (low resting heart rate).

lessons.html:
Visual lesson

Fundamentals of Anatomy and Physiology

Anatomy is the study of the structure of the body and physiology is the study of its functions

minutes
formulas
Q&A
quiz
Flat concept map (2D)
1Big idea›2Skeletal system›3Muscular and circulatory›4Respiratory system and…
Bones206
Heart4 chambers
Heart rate72 per min
Tidal volume500 ml
🔑

Big idea

  • Anatomy is the study of the structure of the body and physiology is the study of its functions
  • The skeletal system has 206 bones in an adult: 80 in the axial skeleton (skull, vertebral column, ribs, sternum) and 126 in the appendicular skeleton…
  • Bones are long (femur), short (carpals), flat (skull, ribs) and irregular (vertebrae)
  • Functions of the skeleton: support, protection, movement, storage of minerals and production of blood cells in the bone marrow
Read the full explanation

Anatomy is the study of the structure of the body and physiology is the study of its functions. The skeletal system has 206 bones in an adult: 80 in the axial skeleton (skull, vertebral column, ribs, sternum) and 126 in the appendicular skeleton (limbs and girdles). Bones are long (femur), short (carpals), flat (skull, ribs) and irregular (vertebrae). Functions of the skeleton: support, protection, movement, storage of minerals and production of blood cells in the bone marrow. A joint is where two bones meet; types are fixed (skull), slightly movable (vertebrae) and freely movable or synovial joints such as ball and socket (shoulder, hip), hinge (elbow, knee), pivot (neck), gliding (wrist), saddle (thumb) and condyloid. Muscles are of three types: skeletal (voluntary, striated), smooth (involuntary, in organs) and cardiac (involuntary, in heart). The human body has more than 600 muscles. Skeletal muscle fibres are slow twitch (red, endurance) and fast twitch (white, power). Muscle contraction can be isotonic or isometric. The circulatory system consists of the heart, blood and blood vessels. The heart has four chambers: right and left atria and right and left ventricles. Arteries carry blood away from the heart, veins carry blood towards it and capillaries exchange materials. Blood contains plasma, red blood cells (carry oxygen with haemoglobin), white blood cells (defence) and platelets (clotting). Normal resting heart rate is about 72 beats per minute; trained athletes have lower rates. Stroke volume is the blood pumped per beat and cardiac output equals stroke volume times heart rate. The respiratory system includes the nose, pharynx, larynx, trachea, bronchi and lungs; gas exchange occurs in the alveoli. Tidal volume is about 500 ml. Vital capacity is the maximum air exhaled after maximum inhalation. Exercise effects: it strengthens muscles and bones, increases stroke volume and cardiac output, lowers resting heart rate, improves lung capacity, helps digestion and improves mood. Oxygen debt arises during heavy exercise when oxygen supply is less than demand.

📌

Skeletal system

  • Bones give shape and protection
  • Red bone marrow makes blood cells
  • Joints allow different movement
  • Cartilage covers joint surfaces and ligaments join bone to bone while tendons join muscle to bone
🧠

Muscular and circulatory

  • Skeletal muscles move bones
  • Slow-twitch fibres suit long-distance events
  • Fast-twitch suit sprints
  • The heart pumps blood in a double circulation: pulmonary and systemic
Read the full explanation

Skeletal muscles move bones. Slow-twitch fibres suit long-distance events; fast-twitch suit sprints. The heart pumps blood in a double circulation: pulmonary and systemic. Blood carries oxygen, nutrients and wastes.

🌟

Respiratory system and exercise

  • Inhaled air reaches alveoli where oxygen diffuses into blood
  • Regular exercise improves vital capacity and the efficiency of the heart
  • Athletes show bradycardia (low resting heart rate)
🧮

lessons.title: Fundamentals of Kinesiology and Biomechanics
yt: class 11 physical education kinesiology biomechanics levers newton laws planes axes friction

blocks.x: Kinesiology is the study of human movement, and biomechanics is the application of mechanical principles to the study of living bodies. Importance: improves technique, prevents injury, improves equipment design and helps coaches analyse performance. Movements about joints: flexion (decreasing the angle), extension (increasing the angle), abduction (moving away from the midline), adduction (moving towards the midline), rotation, circumduction, pronation and supination. Planes of the body: sagittal (divides into left and right), frontal or coronal (front and back) and transverse or horizontal (upper and lower). Axes are the lines about which movement occurs: frontal (horizontal) axis, sagittal axis and vertical (longitudinal) axis. Flexion and extension occur in the sagittal plane about the frontal axis. Levers: a lever is a rigid bar that turns about a fulcrum with effort and load. First class: fulcrum between effort and load (seesaw, neck extension). Second class: load between fulcrum and effort (wheelbarrow, calf raise standing on toes). Third class: effort between fulcrum and load (biceps curl); this is the most common in the body. Newton's laws: first (inertia): an object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by an external force; second: force = mass x acceleration; third: for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. Applications: starting a race, swimming push-off, jump landing. Friction is the force opposing relative motion; types are static, sliding, rolling and fluid. Friction helps in running, gripping and braking but wastes energy, and is reduced by lubrication and streamlined shapes. Equilibrium is a state of balance: stable (large base, low centre of gravity), unstable and neutral. Centre of gravity is the point where the weight of the body acts. Lower centre of gravity and wider base give more stability. Projectile motion depends on speed, angle (about 45 degrees for maximum range) and height of release. Force is a push or pull; Torque is turning effect.
Deep dive: Movements and planes

Joint actions are described using flexion, extension, abduction, adduction and rotation. Each happens in a plane about an axis. Examples: a cartwheel moves in the frontal plane; a somersault in the sagittal plane.
Deep dive: Levers

Lever systems give mechanical advantage. In first class levers the fulcrum is in the middle. In second class the load is in the middle and gives a large force. In third class the effort is in the middle giving speed and range.
Deep dive: Newton's laws and friction
Inertia explains why a ball stays at rest. F = ma explains why a lighter ball goes farther for the same force. Action-reaction explains push-off. Friction depends on surfaces and force pressing them.
Hindi saransh
Gati vigyan: kinesiology manav gati ka adhyayan hai; Newton ke teen niyam, lever ke teen varg aur ghashan khel mein upyogi hain.
Remember levers: First = fulcrum middle; Second = load middle; Third = effort middle.

Fundamentals of Kinesiology and Biomechanics

Read the full explanation

Kinesiology is the study of human movement, and biomechanics is the application of mechanical principles to the study of living bodies. Importance: improves technique, prevents injury, improves equipment design and helps coaches analyse performance. Movements about joints: flexion (decreasing the angle), extension (increasing the angle), abduction (moving away from the midline), adduction (moving towards the midline), rotation, circumduction, pronation and supination. Planes of the body: sagittal (divides into left and right), frontal or coronal (front and back) and transverse or horizontal (upper and lower). Axes are the lines about which movement occurs: frontal (horizontal) axis, sagittal axis and vertical (longitudinal) axis. Flexion and extension occur in the sagittal plane about the frontal axis. Levers: a lever is a rigid bar that turns about a fulcrum with effort and load. First class: fulcrum between effort and load (seesaw, neck extension). Second class: load between fulcrum and effort (wheelbarrow, calf raise standing on toes). Third class: effort between fulcrum and load (biceps curl); this is the most common in the body. Newton's laws: first (inertia): an object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by an external force; second: force = mass x acceleration; third: for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. Applications: starting a race, swimming push-off, jump landing. Friction is the force opposing relative motion; types are static, sliding, rolling and fluid. Friction helps in running, gripping and braking but wastes energy, and is reduced by lubrication and streamlined shapes. Equilibrium is a state of balance: stable (large base, low centre of gravity), unstable and neutral. Centre of gravity is the point where the weight of the body acts. Lower centre of gravity and wider base give more stability. Projectile motion depends on speed, angle (about 45 degrees for maximum range) and height of release. Force is a push or pull; Torque is turning effect.

🕰️

Movements and planes

  • Joint actions are described using flexion, extension, abduction, adduction and rotation
  • Each happens in a plane about an axis
  • Examples: a cartwheel moves in the frontal plane
  • A somersault in the sagittal plane
🧠

Levers

  • Lever systems give mechanical advantage
  • In first class levers the fulcrum is in the middle
  • In second class the load is in the middle and gives a large force
  • In third class the effort is in the middle giving speed and range
⚖️

Newton's laws and friction

  • Inertia explains why a ball stays at rest
  • F = ma explains why a lighter ball goes farther for the same force
  • Action-reaction explains push-off
  • Friction depends on surfaces and force pressing them

lessons.title: Psychology and Sports
yt: class 11 physical education psychology sports personality motivation adherence

blocks.x: Psychology is the scientific study of behaviour and mental processes. Sports psychology applies psychological principles to sports to improve performance and well-being. Its aims are to understand how psychological factors affect performance, to teach mental skills, to handle stress and to enhance enjoyment. Personality is the sum of the characteristics that make a person unique. Carl Jung classified people as introverts (inward looking, quiet) and extroverts (outgoing, sociable); an ambivert has both. Sheldon's somatotypes link body build to temperament: endomorph (round, relaxed), mesomorph (muscular, energetic) and ectomorph (thin, introverted). The Big Five traits are openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness and neuroticism. Personality and sports: team sport players are often extroverts; individual sport players are often more introverted, and personality affects choice of sport. Motivation is the force that energises and directs behaviour toward a goal. Intrinsic motivation comes from within (enjoyment, satisfaction); extrinsic motivation comes from outside (rewards, medals, praise). Techniques to motivate: set clear goals, give feedback and rewards, use praise, create a positive environment, vary training and involve athletes in decisions. Achievement motivation is the drive to succeed. Exercise adherence is continuing a programme of exercise; factors that support it include enjoyment, social support, convenience, goal setting and seeing results; barriers include lack of time, injury and lack of facilities. Strategies to improve adherence: set realistic goals, choose enjoyable activities, exercise with friends, keep records and reward progress. Mental skills include goal setting, imagery, relaxation, self-talk and concentration. Anxiety and arousal affect performance; the inverted-U hypothesis says moderate arousal gives best performance. Aggression in sports can be hostile or instrumental. Team cohesion improves performance. Sportspersons should learn to handle pressure and failure and develop confidence.
Deep dive: Personality
Personality is shaped by heredity and environment. Jung's types and Sheldon's body types are early theories. Traits are stable patterns. The Big Five model is widely used.
Deep dive: Motivation
Intrinsic motivation is long lasting; extrinsic can help but may reduce interest if overused. Goals should be specific, measurable and achievable. Coaches use feedback and encouragement.
Deep dive: Exercise adherence
Many people stop exercise within months. Enjoyment, support and planning improve adherence. Time management and variety help. Health benefits motivate long-term participation.

Big idea

  • Psychology is the scientific study of behaviour and mental processes
